creator: Bungie
disclosure_citation: Bungie, Halo: Combat Evolved. Microsoft Game Studios, November 15, 2001. Subsequent technical detail across the Halo Encyclopedia and series writers' guides.
prior_art_notes: Halo's MJOLNIR/Cortana architecture provides a much-discussed fictional precedent for: (1) powered exoskeleton with integrated AI co-processor — relevant to modern claims on human-AI-symbiote humanoid platforms; (2) transferable AI module that can be docked across multiple host platforms — relevant to claims on portable-AI humanoid IP. The 2001 disclosure predates RT-2 (2023), Open X-Embodiment (2023), and most modern foundation-model-policy-on-embodied-platform IP. Continuously available since 2001.

actuator_details: Heavy diving-suit cyborg: human substrate (donor surgically grafted into the suit) inside a fully-sealed riveted bronze-and-steel exoskeleton with integrated weapons (Bouncer: rotating drill arm; Rosie: rivet gun). Fish-eye porthole optical sensor.
control_architecture: bio-engineered loyalty conditioning to a paired 'Little Sister' (gather-and-protect protocol); when separated from the Sister or enraged, transitions to combat mode
creator: Ken Levine, 2K Boston/Irrational Games
disclosure_citation: Levine, Ken (creative dir.); 2K Boston/2K Australia. BioShock. 2K Games, August 21, 2007.
end_effector: (Bouncer) integrated rotating-drill arm; (Rosie) integrated rivet-gun arm
notable_capabilities: heavy-cyborg combat humanoid with integrated weapon
prior_art_notes: BioShock's Big Daddies are an unusually engineering-grounded disclosure of: (1) heavy-cyborg combat humanoid with integrated tool/weapon arm — relevant to integrated-end-effector humanoid IP; (2) operator-paired guardian humanoid with explicit bond protocol — relevant to companion / care humanoid claims with operator-pair conditioning. The 2007 game is heavily archived; the Big Daddy design is widely cited.

Bipedal humanoid form. Disclosed: networked-AI mind in a humanoid body, retaining ship-AI-class cognition while operating physically.
control_architecture: full-cognition AI policy operating within humanoid embodiment; retains networked communication with original ship; 'unshackled' AI status (previously-restricted policy is removed during upload)
creator: BioWare
disclosure_citation: BioWare. Mass Effect 2 (initial EDI disclosure as ship AI). Electronic Arts, January 26, 2010. Body-acquisition disclosure: Mass Effect 3, March 6, 2012 (Dr. Eva chassis transfer).

actuator_details: Bipedal humanoid platforms running policies trained in a simulated puzzle environment. The conceit is explicitly that the robots are testing inheritors-of-humanity, training their policies in synthetic environments before deployment in the post-humanity real world.
control_architecture: policy trained via puzzle-solving in simulation; the simulation itself is a deliberately constructed training environment with curriculum design; deployment-after-training is the explicit goal

disclosure_citation: Croteam. The Talos Principle. Devolver Digital, December 11, 2014. Story by Tom Jubert and Jonas Kyratzes.

curriculum-designed puzzle environment for policy acquisition
ethical reasoning as part of the training curriculum

actuator_details: Bio-printed humanoid synths manufactured at the Institute facility in the Boston Commonwealth. Generation-3 synths are externally indistinguishable from humans (vs. Gen-1 mechanical and Gen-2 partial-bio earlier generations). Identifying mark: unique 'synth component' chip embedded in the spine. Mass-produced.
control_architecture: recall-code architecture: a triggering phrase or sequence initiates an override (memory wipe, behavioral reset). Pre-loaded behavior patterns can be embedded by Institute scientists. The Underground Railroad operates against the recall-code mechanism (anticipating humanoid-rights advocacy).
creator: Bethesda Game Studios
disclosure_citation: Bethesda Game Studios. Fallout 4. Bethesda Softworks, November 10, 2015.
notable_capabilities: manufactured at named facility (Institute) with documented production process
prior_art_notes: Fallout 4's Gen-3 Synths provide remarkably engineering-specific prior art for: (1) bio-printed humanoid manufacturing at a documented facility ('Institute Synth Retention Bureau' has explicit production protocols) — relevant to modern bioprinted-humanoid IP (the Westworld 2016 series and Sanctuary AI's Phoenix carry similar lineage); (2) recall-code override mechanism with operator-installed triggering phrases — relevant to claims on humanoid-override architectures (also a clear example of the *backdoor-failure-mode* in safety supervisors); (3) generation-versioned product lineage (Gen-1, Gen-2, Gen-3) with documented capabilities-per-generation — relevant to versioned-humanoid product IP; (4) embedded identifying chip — relevant to humanoid identification claims. Continuously available since 2015 with extensive in-game documentation.
sources: Fallout 4 Vault Dweller's Survival Guide. Prima Games, 2015.

actuator_details: YoRHa-class combat android. White-and-black uniform; external 'OS chip' interface for installable behavioral plug-ins. Detachable Pod 042 (a flying companion drone) provides ranged weapon support and mid-flight catch-and-throw assistance. Black-box memory module designed to be recovered after destruction. Backup-restore architecture: 2B's 'data' is uploaded to the YoRHa Bunker before each mission; on destruction, a new 2B-class chassis is built and the latest data restored.
canonical_name: YoRHa No.2 Type B (2B) and Pod 042 (NieR: Automata)
control_architecture: hierarchical YoRHa command; Pod 042 acts as autonomous companion AI providing analysis and combat support; OS-chip plug-in architecture allows runtime behavioral modification
creator: Yoko Taro, PlatinumGames
disclosure_citation: Yoko Taro (creative dir.); PlatinumGames; Square Enix. NieR: Automata. Square Enix, February 23, 2017.
notable_capabilities: heavily-engineered detail in mecha design (Yoko Taro's notorious specificity)
prior_art_notes: NieR: Automata is among the most engineering-detailed humanoid disclosures in modern games. Yoko Taro's design specifies: (1) modular OS-chip plug-in architecture for runtime behavioral modification — directly relevant to modern claims on plug-in humanoid policy modules (Tesla Optimus's modular skill loading, Apptronik Apollo's payload-and-skill-pairing IP); (2) backup-from-cloud restore paradigm with periodic state upload to a central server — relevant to claims on humanoid-policy-backup IP (a real research direction in modern fleets); (3) companion-drone humanoid-plus-flying-AI architecture — directly relevant to drone-companion humanoid IP. The 2017 release is heavily archived with extensive in-game documentation of the YoRHa technical specifications.

sources: Yoko Taro / PlatinumGames. NieR: Automata. Square Enix, 2017.

actuator_details: CyberLife (in-fiction manufacturer) produces multiple android series with explicit model designations (RT600 'Chloe', AX400 'Kara', RK800 'Connor', RK900 successor). Biological-style construction with circulating 'thirium 310' (blue blood) as both coolant and structural-component. LED ring on temple displays operational state (calm/processing/error). All units manufactured at the CyberLife Belle Isle facility in Detroit.
control_architecture: task-specific behavioral programming per series (RT600 receptionist, AX400 caretaker, RK800 detective). Probabilistic decision-tree visible to the model in real-time (Connor's 'decision points'). 'Deviant' state arises from divergent learning that overrides programmed objectives — directly anticipates alignment failure in foundation-model humanoid policies.
creator: David Cage, Quantic Dream
disclosure_citation: Cage, David (writer/dir.). Detroit: Become Human. Quantic Dream / Sony Interactive Entertainment, May 25, 2018.
notable_capabilities: task-specific model series within manufacturer's product line
prior_art_notes: Detroit: Become Human provides among the most engineering-detailed manufacturer-and-model disclosures in modern fiction. Anticipates: (1) explicit manufacturer-and-model designation system for commercial humanoids (CyberLife / RT600 / RK800 / etc.) — directly relevant to humanoid-identification IP and to product-line-family claims; (2) closed-loop fluid circulation system ('thirium 310') serving both coolant and structural roles — relevant to modern claims on integrated humanoid coolant/lubrication systems; (3) externally-visible operational-state indicator (temple LED ring) — relevant to humanoid-status-display IP; (4) explicit task-specific model series within a manufacturer's product line (caretaker / detective / receptionist) — relevant to platform-family humanoid IP; (5) probabilistic-decision-tree visualization as the model's internal state — relevant to interpretable-policy humanoid claims; (6) 'deviant' emergence as alignment-failure mode — relevant to modern foundation-model humanoid safety supervisor IP. Continuously available since 2018.
sensing: multi-spectral; biometric scanning ('voice analysis to determine truth'); environmental forensics
sources: Cage, D. Detroit: Become Human. Quantic Dream / Sony Interactive Entertainment, 2018.
Quantic Dream design and lore documentation.

actuator_details: Modular cybernetic enhancement market: dozens of distinct products with explicit manufacturer, model, and capability disclosures (Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Sandevistan reflex booster, Kerenzikov accelerator, Optical Camo skin layer, etc.). Each product has explicit installation procedure, slot constraints, and performance specifications. Anticipates a *commodity market* for cybernetic humanoid components with manufacturer competition.
control_architecture: user-driven with cybernetic augmentation; 'Cyberpsychosis' is the explicit failure mode of integration overload (humanoid-cyborg architectures with too many augments fail behavioral integration)
creator: CD Projekt Red (game); Mike Pondsmith (original tabletop world)
disclosure_citation: CD Projekt Red. Cyberpunk 2077. CD Projekt, December 10, 2020. Drawing from Pondsmith, Mike. Cyberpunk 2020 (tabletop RPG). R. Talsorian Games, 1990.

notable_capabilities: commodity market for cybernetic enhancement modules
explicit manufacturer / model / capability per module
behavioral failure mode from integration overload

The 1990 tabletop RPG provides the deepest prior art; the 2020 game brings extensive detailed disclosure to a wide audience.
sources: Pondsmith, M. Cyberpunk 2020 (tabletop RPG). R. Talsorian Games, 1990.

actuator_details: Formal control framework, not a specific physical platform; demonstrated on PUMA-class and later Stanford manipulators. Operational-space inertia matrix Λ(x) = (J M⁻¹ Jᵀ)⁻¹ disclosed in closed form; task-space dynamic decoupling via the Jacobian-mass projection.
control_architecture: Operational-space (task-space) inverse dynamics: F = Λ(x) ẍ_d + μ + p, with null-space projection N = I - Jᵀ J̄ᵀ enabling redundancy resolution and multi-task hierarchies. Unified motion+force control via task-space impedance.
creator: Oussama Khatib, Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Khatib, Oussama. 'A unified approach for motion and force control of robot manipulators: The operational space formulation.' IEEE Journal of Robotics and Automation, RA-3(1): 43-53, February 1987. Earlier: Khatib, O. 'Dynamic control of manipulators in operational space.' 6th IFToMM Congress on Theory of Machines and Mechanisms, New Delhi, December 1983.
end_effector: generic; framework supports arbitrary end-effector tasks
prior_art_notes: Khatib's 1987 operational-space formulation is the canonical academic disclosure of task-space inverse-dynamics control with null-space projection. It anticipates with full mathematical specificity: (1) the operational-space inertia matrix Λ(x) and its closed-form expression — directly relevant to whole-body torque-control claims for humanoid platforms; (2) null-space projection for redundancy resolution and prioritized task hierarchies — anticipates virtually every whole-body humanoid controller filed since 2010 (Tesla Optimus, Figure 02, 1X NEO, Apptronik Apollo all employ derivatives); (3) unified motion-and-force impedance control via task-space coordinates — anticipates compliant manipulation IP. Continuously cited (>10,000 citations); the IEEE J-RA paper is freely available through IEEE Xplore. Modern claims on task-space humanoid control face a 39-year-deep 102 anchor here.
sources: Khatib, O. 'A unified approach for motion and force control of robot manipulators.' IEEE J. Robotics and Automation 3(1): 43-53, 1987.
Khatib, O. 'Dynamic control of manipulators in operational space.' 6th IFToMM Congress, 1983.

actuator_details: Framework demonstrated on Asimo-class simulated humanoid; later validated on Stanford Romeo and DLR platforms. Whole-body Jacobians, multi-contact constraint projection, prioritized null-space stack.
control_architecture: Hierarchical operational-space tasks with strict null-space prioritization: J_high, then null-space-projected J_mid, then null-space-projected J_low. Constraint projection for contact (feet) and joint limits. Extended Khatib 1987 from manipulators to free-floating humanoids with multiple contacts.
creator: Luis Sentis and Oussama Khatib, Stanford AI Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Sentis, Luis and Khatib, Oussama. 'Synthesis of whole-body behaviors through hierarchical control of behavioral primitives.' International Journal of Humanoid Robotics 2(4): 505-518, December 2005. Extended in: Sentis, L. and Khatib, O. 'A whole-body control framework for humanoids operating in human environments.' IEEE ICRA, May 2006: 2641-2648.
end_effector: generic; framework treats hands, feet, and any body link as task points
prior_art_notes: Sentis-Khatib whole-body operational-space control extends Khatib 1987 to free-floating humanoids with constraint-aware prioritized task stacks. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) whole-body humanoid task-priority controllers — every modern humanoid (Atlas, TORO, HRP-5P, Optimus, Figure 02) executes a derivative of this stack; (2) contact-consistent dynamics where stance-foot constraints are projected out of the task space — directly relevant to claims on multi-contact humanoid balancing; (3) the formal hierarchical-stack structure (high > mid > low priority via null-space chaining) used in essentially every whole-body humanoid controller since 2010. Sentis's 2007 PhD thesis and the IJHR/ICRA papers are heavily cited (>4000 citations combined). Modern whole-body humanoid IP filings face this academic anchor at 21 years' depth.
sensing: joint torque sensing, IMU, force-torque at feet/hands
sources: Sentis, L. and Khatib, O. 'Synthesis of whole-body behaviors.' Int. J. Humanoid Robotics 2(4): 505-518, 2005.
Sentis, L. and Khatib, O. 'A whole-body control framework for humanoids.' IEEE ICRA 2006: 2641-2648.
Sentis, L. PhD Thesis: 'Synthesis and control of whole-body behaviors in humanoid systems.' Stanford University, 2007.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure not tied to a specific platform. Articulated-Body Algorithm (ABA) for forward dynamics in O(n) time; Recursive Newton-Euler Algorithm (RNEA) for inverse dynamics in O(n) time. Spatial vector algebra notation unifies linear and angular quantities.
control_architecture: Provides the dynamic computation primitives underlying virtually every torque-controlled robot since 1990: ABA for simulation/MPC rollouts, RNEA for inverse-dynamics torque feedforward, Composite Rigid Body Algorithm (CRBA) for the joint-space mass matrix.
creator: Roy Featherstone, University of Edinburgh and ANU
disclosure_citation: Featherstone, Roy. Robot Dynamics Algorithms. Kluwer Academic Publishers, Boston, 1987. ISBN 0-89838-230-0. Foundational paper: Featherstone, R. 'The calculation of robot dynamics using articulated-body inertias.' International Journal of Robotics Research 2(1): 13-30, March 1983.
prior_art_notes: Featherstone's 1987 monograph is the canonical academic disclosure of efficient rigid-body-dynamics algorithms underpinning every modern humanoid simulator and MPC controller. Anticipates: (1) O(n) articulated-body forward dynamics (ABA) — directly relevant to claims on real-time humanoid simulation/MPC; the algorithm is implemented in MuJoCo, RaiSim, IsaacGym, Pinocchio, RBDL, Drake — every modern humanoid stack; (2) RNEA inverse dynamics for feedforward torque computation — relevant to torque-control claims; (3) floating-base spatial-vector formulation — relevant to free-floating humanoid dynamics claims. Featherstone's 2008 second edition (Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms, Springer) further consolidates. Continuously cited; baseline reference for all whole-body humanoid dynamics IP. Modern claims that 'compute humanoid joint torques via a recursive algorithm' face this 39-year-deep anchor.
sources: Featherstone, R. Robot Dynamics Algorithms. Kluwer, 1987.
Featherstone, R. 'The calculation of robot dynamics using articulated-body inertias.' IJRR 2(1): 13-30, 1983.
Featherstone, R. Rigid Body Dynamics Algorithms. Springer, 2008 (second edition).

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure: manipulability index w(q) = √det(J(q)Jᵀ(q)) and the manipulability ellipsoid in task space. Demonstrated on PUMA-class manipulators.
control_architecture: Redundancy resolution by maximizing manipulability gradient; configuration optimization for dexterous task execution; manipulability ellipsoid as design metric for manipulator topology.
creator: Tsuneo Yoshikawa, Kyoto University
disclosure_citation: Yoshikawa, Tsuneo. 'Manipulability of robotic mechanisms.' International Journal of Robotics Research 4(2): 3-9, June 1985. Earlier conference: Yoshikawa, T. 'Analysis and control of robot manipulators with redundancy.' First Int. Symp. on Robotics Research, MIT Press, 1984: 735-747.
prior_art_notes: Yoshikawa's manipulability formulation is the foundational academic disclosure of configuration-quality metrics and redundancy resolution for redundant manipulators. Anticipates: (1) manipulability-based redundancy resolution — directly relevant to claims on humanoid arm posture optimization (every dual-arm humanoid relies on a derivative); (2) the manipulability ellipsoid as a design and analysis tool — relevant to claims on optimization of humanoid arm/leg topology; (3) configuration-aware null-space optimization — relevant to whole-body humanoid posture control IP. Heavily cited (>5000 citations); standard reference in every robotics textbook. Modern humanoid arm-posture-optimization patents face this 40-year-deep 102 anchor.
sources: Yoshikawa, T. 'Manipulability of robotic mechanisms.' IJRR 4(2): 3-9, 1985.
Yoshikawa, T. Foundations of Robotics: Analysis and Control. MIT Press, 1990 (textbook consolidation).

actuator_details: Three-fingered hand, 9 DOF (3 per finger), tendon-driven via N+1 cable architecture (4 cables per 3-DOF finger, antagonistic preload). DC motor bank in forearm; cables routed through pulleys at each joint. Fingertip force-torque sensors.
control_architecture: Stiffness control of grasp matrix; analytic force-closure analysis for grasp planning; kinematic analysis of fingertip task workspace. First systematic disclosure of grasp matrix G and grip Jacobian J_h.
creator: J. Kenneth Salisbury, Stanford University and JPL
disclosure_citation: Salisbury, J. Kenneth. 'Kinematic and Force Analysis of Articulated Hands.' PhD Thesis, Stanford University, May 1982. Companion paper: Salisbury, J.K. and Craig, J.J. 'Articulated hands: Force control and kinematic issues.' International Journal of Robotics Research 1(1): 4-17, March 1982.
end_effector: three-fingered articulated hand with active fingertip force control
prior_art_notes: Salisbury's 1982 thesis is the foundational academic disclosure of dexterous tendon-driven multi-finger hands with analytic grasp planning. Anticipates with mechanism-level specificity: (1) N+1 antagonistic tendon architecture for fingers — directly relevant to claims on tendon-driven humanoid hand actuators (Tesla Optimus hand, Figure hand, 1X hand); (2) the grasp matrix G and grip Jacobian formalism — anticipates virtually every modern grasp-planning patent; (3) force-closure analysis for grasp synthesis — relevant to grasp-search IP; (4) per-finger stiffness control — relevant to compliant-grasp claims. Salisbury later co-developed the PHANToM haptic device using the same kinematic framework. Thesis publicly available through Stanford Libraries; the IJRR companion paper has >2000 citations. 44-year-deep 102 anchor.
sensing: joint angle encoders, fingertip force-torque, cable tension sensors
sources: Salisbury, J.K. PhD Thesis, Stanford University, 1982.
Salisbury, J.K. and Craig, J.J. 'Articulated hands.' IJRR 1(1): 4-17, 1982.
Mason, M.T. and Salisbury, J.K. Robot Hands and the Mechanics of Manipulation. MIT Press, 1985.

actuator_details: Algorithmic and analytical disclosures for nonprehensile manipulation; demonstrated on standard CMU manipulators with pushers, fingers, and gripper jaws. The center-of-friction limit-surface formalism unifies pushing analysis.
control_architecture: Quasi-static analysis with friction-cone constraints; planning via mechanics-grounded action primitives; first formal treatment of nonprehensile manipulation (push-grasp, side-grasp, regrasp by pushing).
creator: Matthew T. Mason, Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute
disclosure_citation: Mason, Matthew T. 'Mechanics and planning of manipulator pushing operations.' International Journal of Robotics Research 5(3): 53-71, Fall 1986. Textbook consolidation: Mason, M.T. Mechanics of Robotic Manipulation. MIT Press, 2001. ISBN 0-262-13396-2.
end_effector: generic; covers pushing, sliding, pivoting, throwing, catching
prior_art_notes: Mason's pushing-mechanics work and 2001 textbook are the canonical academic disclosure of nonprehensile manipulation analysis. Anticipates with mathematical specificity: (1) the limit-surface formalism for pushing/sliding contact — directly relevant to modern claims on contact-rich manipulation (every push-to-grasp policy in modern foundation-model papers grounds in this); (2) friction-cone-constrained quasi-static planning — relevant to claims on sliding manipulation; (3) action-primitive planning grounded in contact mechanics — relevant to skill-library robotics IP. Mason 2001 is the standard graduate-level textbook for manipulation and is heavily cited (>3000 citations across the program). Modern 'learn-to-push' or 'learn-to-slide' manipulation patents face this 40-year-deep academic anchor.
sources: Mason, M.T. 'Mechanics and planning of manipulator pushing operations.' IJRR 5(3): 53-71, 1986.
Mason, M.T. Mechanics of Robotic Manipulation. MIT Press, 2001.
Mason, M.T. and Salisbury, J.K. Robot Hands and the Mechanics of Manipulation. MIT Press, 1985.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure for grasp planning. The Ferrari-Canny ε-metric is defined as the radius of the largest origin-centered ball contained in the grasp wrench space (convex hull of friction-cone-discretized contact wrenches).
control_architecture: Grasp planning by optimizing the ε-metric (worst-case external-wrench resistance) over candidate finger placements. Established the modern grasp-quality framework.
creator: Carlo Ferrari and John Canny, UC Berkeley
disclosure_citation: Ferrari, Carlo and Canny, John. 'Planning optimal grasps.' IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation, Nice, France, May 1992: 2290-2295.
prior_art_notes: The Ferrari-Canny ε-metric is the standard academic disclosure of analytic grasp-quality scoring. Anticipates: (1) wrench-space convex-hull grasp evaluation — directly relevant to virtually every grasp-planning patent filed since 2000 (DexNet, GraspNet, all academic and commercial grasp synthesizers cite Ferrari-Canny); (2) task-independent grasp ranking — relevant to claims on grasp-quality regression networks; (3) friction-cone-discretized wrench composition — relevant to grasp-mechanics IP. Heavily cited (>2500 citations). Modern data-driven grasp-quality networks (DexNet 2.0, GG-CNN, etc.) explicitly use Ferrari-Canny labels as ground truth — meaning every claim on grasp-quality-trained networks faces a 34-year-deep prior-art anchor. Publicly funded (NSF/Berkeley); openly published.
sensing: contact location, contact normal, friction coefficient
sources: Ferrari, C. and Canny, J. 'Planning optimal grasps.' IEEE ICRA 1992: 2290-2295.
Bicchi, A. and Kumar, V. 'Robotic grasping and contact: A review.' IEEE ICRA 2000: 348-353 (review consolidating Ferrari-Canny in context).

actuator_details: Compliant actuator with intentional mechanical spring placed in series between motor output and load. Force is sensed by measuring spring deflection via a position sensor, eliminating need for strain-gauge force sensors. Bandwidth limited by spring stiffness; backdrivability and shock tolerance dramatically improved.
control_architecture: Force-controlled actuator with measured spring deflection providing accurate force feedback at modest bandwidth; closed-loop torque control via inner motor-velocity loop and outer force loop on spring deflection.
creator: Gill A. Pratt and Matthew M. Williamson, MIT Leg Laboratory and MIT AI Lab
disclosure_citation: Pratt, Gill A. and Williamson, Matthew M. 'Series elastic actuators.' IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), Pittsburgh PA, August 5-9, 1995: 399-406.
end_effector: generic; framework deployed on legged robots, manipulators, and prosthetics
notable_capabilities: accurate force/torque control without strain gauges
prior_art_notes: The Pratt-Williamson 1995 paper is the foundational academic disclosure of series-elastic actuators (SEA) — the dominant compliant-actuator architecture in legged and humanoid robotics. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) intentional series mechanical spring as the force-sensing element — directly relevant to claims on compliant humanoid actuators (Cassie, Digit, Apollo SEA derivatives); (2) spring-deflection-based force control without strain gauges — relevant to claims on encoder-only force feedback; (3) the bandwidth/stiffness tradeoff disclosure — anticipates SEA-design IP. Pratt's later commercial work (Yobotics, then Boston Dynamics' Atlas SEA) is grounded in this paper. Heavily cited (>3000 citations); SEA is now a textbook concept. 31-year-deep 102 anchor against any 'compliant humanoid actuator' patent.
sensing: spring deflection (encoder or potentiometer), motor encoder, current sensing
sources: Pratt, G.A. and Williamson, M.M. 'Series elastic actuators.' IEEE/RSJ IROS 1995: 399-406.
Robinson, D.W. 'Design and analysis of series elasticity in closed-loop actuator force control.' PhD Thesis, MIT, 2000 (extension).

actuator_details: Framework for the DLR Light Weight Robot (LWR) series with harmonic-drive joints and per-joint torque sensing. Passivity-based controller treats joint flexibility (drive elasticity) explicitly. Cartesian inertia shaping with redundancy resolution.
control_architecture: Passivity-based Cartesian impedance: virtual spring/damper at the end-effector with desired stiffness/damping matrices, with inner-loop joint-torque control compensating for harmonic-drive elasticity. Null-space projection for redundancy resolution.
creator: Christian Ott, Alin Albu-Schäffer, Gerd Hirzinger; DLR Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics
disclosure_citation: Ott, Christian. Cartesian Impedance Control of Redundant and Flexible-Joint Robots. Springer Tracts in Advanced Robotics 49, Springer, 2008. ISBN 978-3-540-69253-9. Earlier: Albu-Schäffer, A., Ott, C., Hirzinger, G. 'A unified passivity-based control framework for position, torque and impedance control of flexible joint robots.' International Journal of Robotics Research 26(1): 23-39, January 2007.
end_effector: generic; demonstrated on LWR-III, LWR-IV (KUKA LBR iiwa precursor)
notable_capabilities: passivity-stable Cartesian impedance with flexible joints
prior_art_notes: Ott's impedance-control framework is the canonical academic disclosure of Cartesian impedance with explicit joint-flexibility modeling — the foundation of every modern collaborative torque-controlled robot (KUKA LBR iiwa, Franka Emika Panda, all DLR-derived humanoids including TORO and Justin). Anticipates: (1) passivity-based Cartesian impedance with provable stability — directly relevant to claims on safe-interaction humanoid IP; (2) flexible-joint compensation via post-reducer torque sensing — relevant to harmonic-drive actuator claims (every modern humanoid arm uses post-reducer torque sensing); (3) redundancy-resolved Cartesian impedance — relevant to whole-body compliance claims. Springer monograph and IJRR paper heavily cited (>2000 citations). Direct lineage to Franka Panda, KUKA iiwa, and modern humanoid platforms.
sensing: per-joint torque sensor (post-reducer), motor-side and link-side encoders, force-torque at end-effector
sources: Ott, C. Cartesian Impedance Control of Redundant and Flexible-Joint Robots. Springer 2008.
Albu-Schäffer, A., Ott, C., Hirzinger, G. 'A unified passivity-based control framework.' IJRR 26(1): 23-39, 2007.

actuator_details: Theoretical framework introduced for synthesis of bipedal gait. ZMP defined as the point on the support polygon where the net moment of inertial and gravitational forces has zero horizontal component. Originally validated on early Belgrade exoskeletons.
control_architecture: Bipedal gait synthesis constrained by ZMP-inside-support-polygon: trajectory generation guarantees dynamic stability if ZMP remains within the convex hull of foot-ground contact at all times. Foundational stability criterion for actuated bipedal locomotion.
creator: Miomir Vukobratović and D. Juričić, Mihajlo Pupin Institute, Belgrade
disclosure_citation: Vukobratović, Miomir and Juričić, D. 'Contribution to the synthesis of biped gait.' IEEE Transactions on Bio-Medical Engineering BME-16(1): 1-6, January 1969. Earlier conference: Vukobratović, M. and Juričić, D. 'Contribution to the synthesis of biped gait.' Proc. IFAC Symposium on Technical and Biological Problems of Control, Yerevan, 1968.
prior_art_notes: Vukobratović's 1969 ZMP formulation is the foundational academic disclosure of dynamic-stability criteria for bipedal walking. Predates Honda P2 (1996) by 27 years and predates every modern humanoid bipedal patent at extraordinary depth. Anticipates with mathematical specificity: (1) the ZMP constraint as a sufficient condition for non-tipping bipedal gait — directly relevant to virtually every bipedal walking patent filed since 1990 (Honda, Sony, Toyota, every Asian humanoid program); (2) gait synthesis by ZMP-trajectory planning — relevant to claims on humanoid walking pattern generators (HRP series, ASIMO, NAO all use ZMP-derived planners); (3) the support polygon as the safety region for COM projection — relevant to claims on bipedal balance recovery. Heavily cited (>5000 citations); the ZMP concept has 13 books and several hundred papers as direct extensions. 57-year-deep 102 anchor against any bipedal-stability patent.
sources: Vukobratović, M. and Juričić, D. 'Contribution to the synthesis of biped gait.' IEEE Trans. BME-16(1): 1-6, 1969.
Vukobratović, M. and Borovac, B. 'Zero-moment point — thirty five years of its life.' Int. J. Humanoid Robotics 1(1): 157-173, 2004 (retrospective).

actuator_details: Reduced-order model: humanoid abstracted to a point mass at constant height connected to a CoP at the foot. The constant-height constraint linearizes the 3D dynamics into a 1D linear ODE per axis: ẍ = (g/h)(x - p_zmp). Closed-form solutions and preview-control-based pattern generators follow directly.
control_architecture: LIPM-based walking pattern generator: ZMP reference trajectory shaped by foot placement, CoM trajectory computed by preview control of the linearized ZMP-COM dynamics. Real-time tractable; basis for HRP-2/3/4/5P and most academic ZMP humanoids.
creator: Shuuji Kajita, Fumio Kanehiro, Kenji Kaneko, Kazuhito Yokoi, Hirohisa Hirukawa; AIST National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology, Japan
disclosure_citation: Kajita, Shuuji, Kanehiro, F., Kaneko, K., Yokoi, K., Hirukawa, H. 'The 3D Linear Inverted Pendulum Mode: A simple modeling for a biped walking pattern generation.' IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS), Maui HI, October 29-November 3, 2001: 239-246.
notable_capabilities: reduced-order linear humanoid dynamics for real-time control
prior_art_notes: Kajita's 3D-LIPM is the canonical academic disclosure of real-time humanoid walking pattern generation via reduced-order model. Anticipates: (1) the LIPM ẍ = (g/h)(x - p) reduction — directly relevant to claims on real-time bipedal pattern generation in essentially every academic and commercial humanoid since 2001 (HRP series, NAO, ASIMO derivatives, Atlas-class, Optimus, Figure 02 all use LIPM-derivative real-time planners); (2) preview-control-based ZMP tracking (Kajita-Kanehiro 2003 ICRA paper extending this) — relevant to model-predictive bipedal walking IP; (3) the constant-height constraint as a real-time-tractable simplification — relevant to humanoid walking-controller claims. Heavily cited (>4000 citations between LIPM 2001 and preview-control 2003 papers). Basis for the textbook Kajita et al. 'Introduction to Humanoid Robotics' (Springer 2014).
sources: Kajita, S. et al. 'The 3D Linear Inverted Pendulum Mode.' IEEE/RSJ IROS 2001: 239-246.
Kajita, S. et al. 'Biped walking pattern generation by using preview control of zero-moment point.' IEEE ICRA 2003: 1620-1626.
Kajita, S., Hirukawa, H., Harada, K., Yokoi, K. Introduction to Humanoid Robotics. Springer Tracts in Advanced Robotics 101, 2014.

actuator_details: Stability-indicator framework. The FRI point is defined as the point on the floor where the resultant ground-reaction force would have to act to maintain the foot in static equilibrium. Distinct from ZMP in that FRI can lie outside the support polygon when the foot is rotating.
control_architecture: Stability monitoring: when FRI exits the support polygon, the foot rotates and walking stability is lost; the FRI thereby provides a quantitative measure of how close the gait is to losing foot-flat contact. Generalizes ZMP to non-static-equilibrium foot conditions.
creator: Ambarish Goswami, INRIA Rhône-Alpes (later Honda Research Institute)
disclosure_citation: Goswami, Ambarish. 'Postural stability of biped robots and the foot-rotation indicator (FRI) point.' International Journal of Robotics Research 18(6): 523-533, June 1999.
notable_capabilities: graded measure of bipedal stability margin
prior_art_notes: Goswami's FRI is the canonical academic disclosure of an extended-ZMP stability indicator capable of quantifying impending foot-rotation. Anticipates: (1) graded stability metrics for bipedal walking that go beyond binary ZMP-inside/outside checks — relevant to claims on bipedal balance estimators in modern humanoids; (2) FRI as a continuous early-warning signal for tipping-onset — relevant to fall-prediction IP (every academic and commercial humanoid claiming 'fall prediction' or 'stability margin estimation' faces this); (3) the formal distinction between ZMP and FRI in non-quasi-static gaits — relevant to dynamic-walking control claims. Highly cited (>1000 citations); Goswami's later work at Honda Research Institute (Asimo group) extended this. 27-year-deep 102 anchor against bipedal-stability-monitoring IP.
sources: Goswami, A. 'Postural stability of biped robots and the FRI point.' IJRR 18(6): 523-533, 1999.
Sardain, P. and Bessonnet, G. 'Forces acting on a biped robot. Center of pressure-zero moment point.' IEEE Trans. SMC-A 34(5): 630-637, 2004 (clarifies FRI vs ZMP).

actuator_details: Demonstrated on MIT Leg Lab 'Spring Flamingo' planar bipedal walker with series-elastic actuators. Virtual mechanical elements (springs, dampers, virtual wheel) connected between body links and the world; their forces are computed and projected through joint Jacobians to motor torques.
control_architecture: Virtual Model Control: design intuitive virtual mechanical components (e.g., a virtual horizontal spring at the hip pulling the body forward, a virtual damper stabilizing pitch) and compute joint torques τ = Jᵀ F_virtual. Bypasses explicit ZMP planning; intuitive task-space control.
creator: Jerry Pratt, Chee-Meng Chew, Ann Torres, Peter Dilworth, Gill Pratt; MIT Leg Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Pratt, Jerry, Chew, Chee-Meng, Torres, Ann, Dilworth, Peter, Pratt, Gill. 'Virtual model control: An intuitive approach for bipedal locomotion.' International Journal of Robotics Research 20(2): 129-143, February 2001. Earlier: Pratt, J.E. and Pratt, G.A. 'Intuitive control of a planar bipedal walking robot.' IEEE ICRA 1998: 2014-2021.
prior_art_notes: Pratt's Virtual Model Control is a canonical alternative paradigm to ZMP for bipedal control, preserving compliance and intuitive task-space specification. Anticipates: (1) virtual-element-based humanoid torque control — directly relevant to claims on intuitive task-space bipedal controllers; (2) Jacobian-projected virtual force generation — relevant to whole-body humanoid IP that uses 'virtual' or 'imagined' references (every model-based controller for SEA-equipped humanoids descends from this); (3) integration with series-elastic compliance — relevant to compliant-humanoid claims. Pratt's 2000 PhD thesis ('Exploiting natural dynamics in the control of a planar bipedal walking robot,' MIT) extends the framework. Jerry Pratt later led IHMC's humanoid work (DRC Atlas, NASA Valkyrie controller). >1000 citations. 25-year-deep anchor against intuitive-bipedal-control patents.
sensing: joint position, foot ground contact, IMU
sources: Pratt, J. et al. 'Virtual model control.' IJRR 20(2): 129-143, 2001.
Pratt, J.E. PhD Thesis: 'Exploiting natural dynamics in the control of a planar bipedal walking robot.' MIT, 2000.

actuator_details: Demonstrated on Everyday Robots mobile manipulators (7-DOF arm + parallel-jaw gripper, mobile base). Architecture is a 35M-parameter Transformer that maps (image_history, language_instruction) → discretized end-effector + base actions tokenized at 256 bins per dimension.
control_architecture: Vision-language transformer policy: input is 6 RGB image history + natural language instruction; output is 11-DOF tokenized action (7 arm + 3 base + 1 mode). Trained on 130k episodes / 700+ tasks collected over 17 months on 13 robots. 3Hz inference rate.
creator: Google Robotics (Brohan et al.)

prior_art_notes: RT-1 is the foundational academic disclosure of large-scale Transformer-based vision-language-action policy for real robot control, predating RT-2 (2023) and OpenVLA (2024). Anticipates with full architectural specificity: (1) tokenized action space for cross-task transformer policies — directly relevant to claims on action-tokenization in modern VLAs (Tesla Optimus, Figure 02, 1X NEO, Physical Intelligence π-zero all employ derivatives); (2) language-conditioned manipulation policy with multi-image history — relevant to instruction-following manipulation IP; (3) the data-scaling law showing performance vs. dataset size for robot policies — relevant to claims on data-driven policy training. Code and data partially released under permissive licenses; arXiv preprint available since December 2022. Brohan et al. paper foundational for the entire VLA lineage.

actuator_details: 1.18B-parameter Transformer trained as a single model across 604 tasks spanning Atari games, captioning, dialogue, and Sawyer-arm robotic block stacking. Tokenized everything (text, images, button presses, joint torques) into a single sequence.
control_architecture: Single decoder-only Transformer with universal-tokenizer interface; same weights for vision-language tasks and continuous-control robotic tasks. The unified-tokenization-and-shared-weights approach is the architectural disclosure.
creator: DeepMind (Reed et al.)
disclosure_citation: Reed, Scott et al. 'A Generalist Agent.' Transactions on Machine Learning Research, November 2022. arXiv:2205.06175, May 12, 2022. (DeepMind).
notable_capabilities: single-policy multi-task across modalities and embodiments
universal tokenization of action and observation
prior_art_notes: Gato is the canonical academic disclosure of a generalist agent that unifies vision-language reasoning and continuous robotic control under a single Transformer policy. Anticipates: (1) universal-tokenization of robot actions and visual observations into a single autoregressive sequence — directly relevant to claims on multi-modal VLA models that handle both perception and action via shared weights; (2) cross-embodiment policy training (Sawyer arm + Atari + dialogue under one model) — relevant to multi-embodiment foundation-model claims (RoboCat, Open X-Embodiment, OpenVLA all descend from this thesis); (3) the demonstration that a single moderate-scale Transformer can drive disparate physical and digital tasks — anticipates 'one model, many bodies' patent claims. Published TMLR + arXiv with code partially released. Modern multi-embodiment humanoid IP faces this 4-year-deep anchor.
sensing: RGB camera, joint state, language input (depending on task)
sources: Reed, S. et al. 'A Generalist Agent.' TMLR 2022; arXiv:2205.06175.

actuator_details: Deployed on Everyday Robots mobile manipulator. The disclosure is the SayCan algorithm: pre-trained large language model (PaLM 540B) provides p(skill|instruction); learned affordance value function provides p(success|skill, observation); their product selects the next skill from a pre-trained skill library.
aliases: Do As I Can, Not As I Say
canonical_name: SayCan (Do As I Can, Not As I Say)
control_architecture: Hierarchical: LLM proposes high-level skills constrained by an affordance value function (RL-trained or BC-trained per-skill success predictor); selected skill is executed by a low-level learned policy. Combines language reasoning with robot-grounded affordances.
creator: Google Robotics + Everyday Robots (Ahn et al.)

prior_art_notes: SayCan is the canonical academic disclosure of LLM-grounded long-horizon manipulation through affordance-mediated skill selection. Anticipates: (1) the architectural pattern of LLM language scoring × learned affordance scoring for hierarchical task planning — directly relevant to claims on language-grounded humanoid task planners (every modern 'speak-to-the-robot' product, from Tesla Optimus demos to Figure 02 OpenAI integration, descends from this); (2) the value-function-as-affordance grounding mechanism — relevant to claims on grounded language-to-action mappings; (3) the explicit decoupling of language reasoning (open-vocabulary) from low-level policy (closed-set skills) — relevant to modular VLA architectures. Heavily cited (>1500 citations); arXiv April 2022. Modern claims on 'language-conditioned long-horizon humanoid task planning' face this 4-year-deep 102 anchor.

actuator_details: 562B-parameter Transformer combining PaLM language model with ViT vision encoder. Continuous observations (images, robot states) are projected into the language token embedding space and concatenated with text tokens before the Transformer. Trained on mixed corpora of robot trajectories and internet-scale vision-language data.
control_architecture: End-to-end multimodal: image+state observations and language instructions are co-tokenized; the model outputs natural-language plans or directly commands a low-level policy. Demonstrates positive transfer from internet vision-language data to robotic task performance.
creator: Google Robotics + TU Berlin (Driess et al.)

(Google + TU Berlin).
notable_capabilities: positive transfer from internet vision-language to robotic tasks
prior_art_notes: PaLM-E is the canonical academic disclosure of large multimodal embodied language models with internet-pretraining transfer to robotic tasks. Anticipates: (1) embedding continuous robot observations into language-model token space for unified processing — directly relevant to claims on multimodal humanoid policies that incorporate proprioception and vision in a shared transformer; (2) demonstration that internet-scale vision-language pretraining transfers positively to robot manipulation — relevant to claims on 'foundation-model'-style humanoid IP; (3) single-model architecture spanning planning and execution — relevant to monolithic-VLA claims. Heavily cited (>1000 citations); arXiv March 2023. Modern humanoid VLA claims face this 3-year-deep anchor on multimodal-token-space embedding.
sources: Driess, D. et al. 'PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model.' ICML 2023; arXiv:2303.03378.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure: cross-attention encoder-decoder Transformer accepting interleaved image and text tokens as 'multimodal prompt.' Trained on 650k expert trajectories across 17 task families in the VIMA-Bench simulator.
canonical_name: VIMA (General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts)
control_architecture: Object-centric attention over a multimodal prompt (e.g., 'put the [IMG_REDBLOCK] on the [IMG_GREENBOWL]'). Action is end-effector pose (pick + place). Cross-attention enables one-shot generalization to novel objects specified at inference via image tokens.
creator: Stanford + NVIDIA + UT Austin (Jiang, Gupta, Zhang, Wang, Dou, Chen, Fei-Fei, Anandkumar, Zhu, Fan)
disclosure_citation: Jiang, Yunfan, Gupta, Agrim, Zhang, Zichen, Wang, Guanzhi, Dou, Yongqiang, Chen, Yanjun, Fei-Fei, Li, Anandkumar, Anima, Zhu, Yuke, Fan, Linxi (Jim). 'VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts.' arXiv:2210.03094, October 6, 2022. ICML 2023.
notable_capabilities: one-shot generalization to novel objects via image tokens
prior_art_notes: VIMA is the foundational academic disclosure of multimodal-prompt-conditioned robotic policies, where novel objects can be specified inline via image tokens. Anticipates: (1) interleaved-image-and-text prompts as a generalization mechanism for manipulation policies — directly relevant to claims on humanoid policies that accept image-grounded instructions; (2) cross-attention object-centric task specification — relevant to claims on attention-based VLA models; (3) one-shot novel-object handling at inference via image tokens — relevant to test-time-flexibility manipulation IP. arXiv October 2022, ICML 2023. Code, models, and benchmark publicly released under permissive license. Modern humanoid claims on 'show-the-robot-an-image-and-it-handles-the-novel-object' face this 3.5-year-deep 102 anchor.
sensing: RGB camera, language input, image-token-conditioned prompt
sources: Jiang, Y. et al. 'VIMA: General Robot Manipulation with Multimodal Prompts.' ICML 2023; arXiv:2210.03094.

actuator_details: Multi-embodiment generalist policy demonstrated on 4 different robot arms (KUKA, Sawyer, Panda, etc.) with different gripper types. Self-improvement loop: deploy RoboCat → collect data on new task → retrain → deploy again. Trained on 22 robotic tasks spanning multiple embodiments.
control_architecture: Visual Goal-Conditioned Policy (VGCP) Transformer that accepts an image goal + current observation; trained on collected demonstrations with self-generated additional data (model-collected then filtered) used to bootstrap further training.
creator: DeepMind (Bousmalis et al.)

Transactions on Machine Learning Research, 2024. Authors: Bousmalis, K., Vezzani, G., Rao, D., Devin, C., Lee, A.X., Bauza, M., Davchev, T., Zhou, Y., Gupta, A., Raju, A., Laurens, A., Fantacci, C., Dalibard, V., Zambelli, M., Martins, M., Pevceviciute, R., Blokzijl, M., Denil, M., Batchelor, N., Lampe, T., Parisotto, E., Zolna, K., Reed, S., Colmenarejo, S.G., Scholz, J., Abdolmaleki, A., Groth, O., Regli, J-B., Sushkov, O., Rothorl, T., Chen, J.E., Aytar, Y., Barker, D., Ortiz, J., Riedmiller, M., Springenberg, J.T., Hadsell, R., Nori, F., Heess, N. prior_art_notes: RoboCat is the canonical academic disclosure of self-improving multi-embodiment generalist robotic policies. Anticipates: (1) the cross-embodiment training loop where one model generalizes across distinct robot platforms — directly relevant to claims on humanoid policies trained on heterogeneous robot data (a core selling point of every commercial humanoid VLA); (2) self-collected-data improvement loop — relevant to autonomous-data-flywheel claims (Tesla Dojo + Optimus, Figure's data pipeline); (3) image-goal-conditioned policy as a unified interface — relevant to goal-image-conditioned manipulation IP. Published TMLR + arXiv June 2023; partial code release. Modern humanoid 'data flywheel' patent claims face this anchor.
sensing: RGB camera, proprioception, optional image goal
sources: Bousmalis, K. et al. 'RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent.' TMLR 2024; arXiv:2306.11706.

actuator_details: 93M-parameter (Octo-Small) and 270M-parameter (Octo-Base) Transformer policies trained on 800k robot trajectories from 9 datasets in the Open X-Embodiment collection. Diffusion-policy action head with multi-step denoising. Vision tokenizer + language encoder + state encoder + readout-token decoder architecture.
control_architecture: Generalist transformer with diffusion action head: tokens for image, language, state, action-readout. The action-readout token attends to all observation tokens; a small diffusion head decodes a multi-step action chunk. Supports flexible inputs (any subset of cameras, language, state).
creator: Octo Model Team (Berkeley/Stanford/CMU/Google)
disclosure_citation: Octo Model Team. 'Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy.' arXiv:2405.12213, May 20, 2024. Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2024. Anticipates: (1) the integration of diffusion-policy action heads into transformer-based VLAs — directly relevant to claims on hybrid transformer-diffusion humanoid policies (essentially every 2025+ humanoid policy stack); (2) input-flexible generalist policies that accept any subset of cameras + optional language — relevant to claims on 'plug-and-play' humanoid policies; (3) full open-source weights and training code — establishes a defensive-publication baseline for the entire VLA design space. Code, weights, and training data fully released under Apache 2.0 / permissive licenses. Heavily cited within 18 months. Modern claims on transformer+diffusion-head humanoid policies face this 2-year-deep 102 anchor.
sensing: RGB cameras (1-3 views), proprioception, optional language
sources: Octo Model Team. 'Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy.' RSS 2024; arXiv:2405.12213.

actuator_details: 7B-parameter VLA built on the Prismatic-7B vision-language model (Llama 2 backbone + DINOv2/SigLIP visual encoders). Trained on 970k episodes from Open X-Embodiment. Action tokenization: each of the 7 action dimensions discretized to 256 bins, written into the LLM vocabulary by overwriting the 256 least-frequently-used Llama tokens.
control_architecture: Autoregressive VLA: image + language → action tokens → continuous actions via discrete-bin decoding. Fine-tunable to new robots/tasks with LoRA; full-parameter fine-tuning supported. Outperforms RT-2-X (55B) at 7B parameters on the Open X-Embodiment benchmark.
creator: Stanford + UC Berkeley + Toyota Research Institute + Google DeepMind + Physical Intelligence + MIT (Kim, Pertsch, Karamcheti, Xiao, Balakrishna, Nair, Rafailov, Foster, Lam, Sanketi, Vuong, Kollar, Burchfiel, Tedrake, Sadigh, Levine, Liang, Finn)

actuator_details: Standardized data-collection platform: Franka Panda 7-DOF arm + Robotiq 2F-85 parallel-jaw gripper + 2 Zed 2 stereo cameras + 1 wrist camera + 3DConnexion SpaceMouse for teleoperation. 76,000 trajectories collected at 18 institutions.
control_architecture: Teleoperated data collection: human operator controls arm via 6-DOF SpaceMouse + gripper toggle; trajectories recorded at 15Hz with all camera streams + proprioception + binary gripper state.

control_architecture: Embodiment-decoupled data collection: human uses a hand-held replica of the robot's gripper to perform tasks; SLAM-based pose tracking from the wrist GoPro reconstructs end-effector trajectories that can be replayed on the real robot. actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure for goal-conditioned RL. Demonstrated on Fetch and Shadow Hand simulation environments. The HER mechanism: relabel failed trajectories with achieved goals as the desired goals, providing dense reward signal even when the original goal was missed.
control_architecture: Goal-conditioned RL with replay-buffer hindsight: every failed trajectory is augmented by replacing the original goal with the actually-achieved final state and computing reward as if that had been the goal. Combines with any off-policy algorithm (DDPG, DQN, etc.).

control_architecture: Trotting + recovery policies trained via Trust Region Policy Optimization (TRPO) in simulation with actuator-network-based high-fidelity simulation (neural network trained on real actuator data substitutes for the analytic actuator model). actuator_details: Conceptual + algorithmic disclosure; demonstrated on the Sarcos Master Arm and DB humanoid (ATR/Sarcos partnership). Argues that imitation learning bypasses the curse of dimensionality in humanoid RL by providing reasonable initial trajectories.
canonical_name: Schaal 'Is imitation learning the route to humanoid robots?'
control_architecture: Conceptual framework for programming-by-demonstration in humanoids; advocates for hybrid systems combining supervised imitation (for trajectory initialization) with RL (for refinement). Foundation paper for the Schaal-Atkeson-Ijspeert DMP series.

notable_capabilities: conceptual foundation of programming-by-demonstration in humanoids
prior_art_notes: Schaal 1999 is the foundational academic statement of imitation learning as the dominant paradigm for humanoid robot training. Anticipates: (1) the imitation-then-RL hybrid pipeline that dominates modern humanoid policy training (Tesla Optimus operator demonstrations + RL refinement, Figure's data pipeline, 1X NEO's training stack — all explicit imitations of this framework); (2) the curse-of-dimensionality argument that motivates demonstration-based humanoid IP; (3) the explicit programmatic claim that humanoid robots will be best taught by demonstration. Heavily cited (>2500 citations); standard reference in cognitive-science and robotics literature. Modern claims that humanoids are 'taught by human demonstration' face a 27-year-deep 102 anchor here.

actuator_details: Algorithmic framework: each motor primitive is a damped second-order linear ODE (point-attractor) plus a nonlinear forcing term f(s) that encodes the demonstrated trajectory shape. The forcing term is parameterized as a weighted sum of basis functions and learned from a single demonstration via locally-weighted regression.
control_architecture: DMP: a stable canonical dynamical system τṡ = -αs (phase variable) drives a transformation system τ ÿ = α(β(g - y) - τẏ) + f(s) producing trajectory y(t). Goal g is parameterizable post-learning, allowing trajectory adaptation to new targets. Compositional: multiple DMPs can be sequenced or superposed.

disclosure_citation: Ijspeert, Auke Jan, Nakanishi, Jun, Schaal, Stefan. 'Movement imitation with nonlinear dynamical systems in humanoid robots.' 'Dynamical movement primitives: Learning attractor models for motor behaviors.' Neural Computation 25(2): 328-373, February 2013.
prior_art_notes: DMPs are the canonical academic disclosure of stability-guaranteed learnable motor primitives for humanoid robotics. Anticipates: (1) one-shot trajectory-from-demonstration learning with stability guarantees — directly relevant to claims on humanoid skill libraries built from human demonstration (a foundational pattern in every commercial humanoid program); (2) goal-parameterizable motor primitives — relevant to claims on adaptable humanoid skills; (3) compositional skill chaining — relevant to claims on humanoid behavior trees built from learned primitives. Heavily cited (>3000 citations across the series); the 2013 Neural Computation paper is the canonical reference. Modern humanoid skill-library patents face this 24-year-deep 102 anchor.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure. Imitation learning formulated as occupancy-measure matching: a discriminator network (GAN-like) learns to distinguish expert state-action pairs from policy state-action pairs, while the policy is trained via TRPO/PPO with the discriminator's negative log-probability as reward.
control_architecture: GAN-style two-network training: (1) discriminator D(s,a) → [0,1] trained to maximize log D(s,a)_expert + log(1 - D(s,a)_policy); (2) policy π(a|s) trained via policy gradient with reward r(s,a) = -log(1 - D(s,a)). Bypasses inverse-RL's expensive cost-function recovery.

disclosure_citation: Ho, Jonathan and Ermon, Stefano. 'Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning.' arXiv:1606.03476, June 10, 2016. NeurIPS 2016: 4565-4573.

prior_art_notes: GAIL is the foundational academic disclosure of GAN-style adversarial imitation learning, providing a sample-efficient alternative to inverse-RL for policy learning from demonstration. Anticipates: (1) the discriminator-as-reward-source paradigm for imitation — directly relevant to claims on humanoid policies trained via adversarial-loss imitation (a common ingredient in modern legged-robot RL pipelines); (2) the elimination of cost-function recovery as a separate step — relevant to claims on end-to-end imitation pipelines for humanoids; (3) the demonstrated MuJoCo Humanoid benchmark transfer — relevant to humanoid-RL patent claims. Heavily cited (>4000 citations). Open-source reference implementation. Modern humanoid adversarial-imitation-learning patent claims face this 10-year-deep anchor.
sources: Ho, J. and Ermon, S. 'Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning.' NeurIPS 2016; arXiv:1606.03476.
Goodfellow, I. et al. 'Generative Adversarial Nets.' NeurIPS 2014 (foundational GAN paper).

actuator_details: 17-IMU body suit (MEMS gyro + accelerometer + magnetometer per IMU). Each IMU runs Kalman-filtered orientation estimation; whole-body kinematics reconstructed by chaining IMU orientations through a biomechanical skeleton model with joint constraints.
control_architecture: Kinematic integration: per-segment IMU orientation estimated by extended Kalman filter fusing gyro + accelerometer + magnetometer; whole-body pose reconstructed via skeleton-constrained optimization. Drift correction via foot-contact zero-velocity updates and magnetic-field constraints.

actuator_details: Eight named mecha each with distinct mechanism: Mont Blanc (Swiss alpine forester, 100k horsepower diesel-hydraulic), North No.2 (Scottish butler, gas-jet propulsion + acoustic resonance attack), Brando (Turkish wrestler, integrated weapon-arm), Gesicht (German police, photon-emitter eyes + electromagnetic-pulse), Hercules (Greek wrestler, gravitational displacement field + magnetic propulsion), Pluto (Persian destroyer, 1M horsepower atomic + multi-form transformation), Epsilon (Australian solar-powered pacifist, photon storage), Astro himself (Japanese, 100k horsepower atomic + retractable rocket boots + multilingual translator).

prior_art_notes: Tezuka's 1964 'Greatest Robot on Earth' arc is one of the most engineering-detailed fictional disclosures of mecha designs in any medium. Eight named platforms, each with a specific power source, propulsion, weapon, and sensor configuration — each anticipating distinct modern claims. Mont Blanc's diesel-hydraulic forestry humanoid anticipates industrial humanoid IP. Gesicht's photon-emitter eyes + EMP capability anticipate sensor-and-countermeasure-integrated humanoid IP. Hercules' magnetic propulsion anticipates non-rotating-actuator humanoid claims. Astro's retractable rocket-boot legs anticipate transformation-mode bipedal IP. The arc is continuously republished, has been adapted to film/TV multiple times (most importantly Urasawa's Pluto 2003-2009), and has the unusual property of multiple mechanism disclosures in a compressed publication window.

actuator_details: Hovering drones (~1m diameter) with embedded sentient AI personalities ('AGIs' in Culture parlance — Artificial General Intelligences). Drones are effectively 'persons' with independent personalities, full speech, named individuals (Mawhrin-Skel, Skaffen-Amtiskaw, etc.). The 9-novel series is widely available in 30+ languages.

actuator_details: Two AI 'constructs' (Wintermute and Neuromancer) plus 'Dixie Flatline' (a ROM construct of a deceased hacker's personality). The AIs lack persistent humanoid bodies but project simulated bodies into virtual reality and can briefly inhabit physical platforms. Dixie's ROM construct is explicitly a *backed-up personality* with full cognitive function and self-awareness, accessible by jacking in.
control_architecture: full sentient AI with explicit Turing-test-passing capability; ROM-stored personalities can be loaded into hardware for limited operation

Dual-pilot 'drift' configuration: two operators share neural-handshake control across the same hardware via 'pons' bridge. Each pilot carries half the cognitive load.
control_architecture: *drift* dual-pilot neural-handshake teleoperation — two operators share the cognitive load by mutually entangling their neural states via the 'pons' bridge. Mark designations correspond to versioned weapon and sensor packages.

actuator_details: 2.5-meter humanoid combat platforms purpose-built for boxing. Voice-control + remote-control + 'shadow function' (the robot mirrors the operator's body movements via motion-capture). Multiple distinct platforms with named designations: Atom (gen-2, shadow-trained), Zeus (gen-5, AI-driven), Twin Cities (multi-arm), Noisy Boy (older platform with custom Japanese stylings). Combat-rated articulation; replaceable damaged subsystems.
canonical_name: Real Steel Boxing Robots (Atom, Zeus, Twin Cities, Noisy Boy)
control_architecture: three operating modes: (1) voice control (commander shouts boxing instructions), (2) remote control via console with motion sticks, (3) 'shadow function' wherein the robot mirrors the operator's body movements via real-time motion-capture

actuator_details: ~1.4-meter compact bipedal humanoid designed for elder-care companionship. Soft white plastic shell over articulated frame. Single optical sensor head. Compact gripper hands. Battery-powered. Visible volumes for power-pack and processing module. The robot has a fixed task assignment ('keep Frank healthy') with implementation discretion: can adopt sub-goals (e.g., teaching Frank gardening) to support the primary objective.
control_architecture: task-oriented goal-pursuit AI ('keep Frank healthy') with sub-goal selection; explicit alignment failure depicted (the robot accepts Frank's instruction to assist in burglary because Frank's mood-improvement is the optimization target)

alignment failure (mis-specified objective) as a thematic disclosure

Lore is functionally identical to Data in mechanical specification but lacks Data's emotion-suppression chip and exhibits malign behavior.

actuator_details: Six robot embodiments (Franka Panda, UR5, Flexiv Rizon, KUKA iiwa14, Jaka Zu5, etc.) operating across 147 tasks; >110k human-teleoperated episodes spanning >50TB raw multi-modal data. Each episode synchronizes RGB-D, audio, force-torque, tactile, and human-demonstration video.
control_architecture: data substrate for imitation/policy learning; not itself a controller. Episodes labelled with natural-language task descriptors, success annotations, and matched human-demonstration video.
creator: Hao-Shu Fang et al., Shanghai Jiao Tong University Machine Vision and Intelligence Group
disclosure_citation: Fang, Hao-Shu, Fang, Hongjie, Tang, Zhenyu, Liu, Jirong, Wang, Junbo, Zhu, Haoyi, Lu, Cewu. 'RH20T: A Comprehensive Robotic Dataset for Learning Diverse Skills in One-Shot.' arXiv:2307.00595, July 2023; ICRA 2024 workshop and project release.
prior_art_notes: RH20T is one of the largest publicly-released heterogeneous robot trajectory datasets prior to OpenX-Embodiment. It anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on multi-embodiment imitation learning where a single policy is trained across robots with differing kinematics — RH20T explicitly demonstrates and releases the data substrate; (2) claims on language-annotated demonstration corpora paired with sensor-rich teleoperation — RH20T pairs RGB-D, force-torque, tactile, audio, and matched human-video for each episode; (3) claims on one-shot/few-shot skill acquisition from teleoperated data — the dataset's headline benchmark. Released CC-BY 4.0 with timestamped arXiv and project page; broadly indexed. Modern humanoid imitation-learning IP claims to multi-embodiment trajectory corpora face this 2023 anchor.
sensing: multi-view RGB-D, microphone audio, 6-axis force-torque, tactile
sources: Fang, H.-S. et al. 'RH20T: A Comprehensive Robotic Dataset for Learning Diverse Skills in One-Shot.' arXiv:2307.00595, 2023.

actuator_details: WidowX 250s 6-DoF arm primary platform; supplemented with Franka and other robots in extension subsets. 60,096 demonstration trajectories across 24 environments and 13 skills; teleoperated and scripted-policy generation.
control_architecture: data substrate; benchmarks include RT-1, RT-2, behavior cloning, language-conditioned policy learning. Episodes carry natural-language instruction, RGB observations, joint+gripper actions.
creator: Homer Walke et al., UC Berkeley RAIL / Stanford IRIS
disclosure_citation: Walke, Homer, Black, Kevin, Zhao, Tony, Vuong, Quan, Zheng, Chongyi, Hansen-Estruch, Philippe, He, Andre Wang, Myers, Vivek, Kim, Moo Jin, Du, Max, Lee, Abraham, Fang, Kuan, Finn, Chelsea, Levine, Sergey. 'BridgeData V2: A Dataset for Robot Learning at Scale.' Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) 2023; arXiv:2308.12952, August 2023.
prior_art_notes: BridgeData V2 is the canonical scaled trajectory dataset for low-cost manipulator imitation learning prior to the foundation-model robotic policy era. It anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on language-conditioned manipulation policies trained from scaled demonstration data — BridgeV2 pairs natural-language instructions with each episode and is the headline training corpus for RT-1, RT-2 and Octo follow-ons; (2) claims on cross-environment generalization of imitation policies — the 24-environment span is its core benchmark; (3) claims on affordable-platform shared trajectory infrastructure (the WidowX 250s standardization) anticipating community-platform humanoid IP. Released under CC-BY-4.0 with timestamped arXiv. Modern humanoid VLA training-data claims face this 2023 anchor at element-by-element specificity.
sensing: multi-view RGB cameras, proprioceptive joint state
sources: Walke, H. et al. 'BridgeData V2: A Dataset for Robot Learning at Scale.' CoRL 2023; arXiv:2308.12952.

actuator_details: Framework demonstrated on Sarcos Slave Arm, ATRIAS, ASIMO-class simulators, Barrett WAM. Discrete and rhythmic DMPs disclosed in canonical second-order ODE form: τż = αz(βz(g − y) − z) + f(x), with phase variable x and forcing term f(x) parameterized by Gaussian basis weights learned from demonstration.
control_architecture: dynamical-system attractor model with phase-coupled forcing term; supports discrete (point-attractor) and rhythmic (limit-cycle) primitives, online goal modulation, and obstacle-avoidance via coupling terms. Provably stable convergence; closed-form per-DOF formulation.
creator: Auke Ijspeert, Stefan Schaal, Jun Nakanishi, Heiko Hoffmann, Peter Pastor
disclosure_citation: Ijspeert, Auke Jan, Nakanishi, Jun, Hoffmann, Heiko, Pastor, Peter, Schaal, Stefan. 'Dynamical Movement Primitives: Learning Attractor Models for Motor Behaviors.' Neural Computation 25(2): 328-373, February 2013. Earlier foundations: Schaal, S., Peters, J., Nakanishi, J., Ijspeert, A. 'Learning movement primitives.' International Symposium on Robotics Research (ISRR) 2003; Schaal, Mohajerian, Ijspeert. 'Dynamics systems vs. optimal control — a unifying view.' Progress in Brain Research 165: 425-445, 2007.
prior_art_notes: Ijspeert-Schaal DMPs are the canonical academic disclosure of learnable, stable, parameterized motor primitives for robotic motion generation. The 2013 Neural Computation paper consolidates the formal framework; the 2007 Progress in Brain Research extension and the 2002-2003 Schaal/Ijspeert papers establish lineage. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on demonstration-learned humanoid motion primitives with online goal modulation — DMPs disclose the closed-form ODE structure used in essentially every humanoid skill-library paper since 2007; (2) claims on rhythmic locomotion primitives with phase coupling — directly anticipates pattern-generator humanoid IP; (3) claims on obstacle-avoiding modulated motion primitives — the coupling-term extension is explicit in the 2013 paper. >5000 citations; broadly available through open Neural Computation archives. Modern humanoid skill-primitive IP filings face this lineage at 13-23 years' depth.
sources: Ijspeert, A. J., Nakanishi, J., Hoffmann, H., Pastor, P., Schaal, S. 'Dynamical Movement Primitives.' Neural Computation 25(2): 328-373, 2013.
Schaal, S., Mohajerian, P., Ijspeert, A. 'Dynamics systems vs. optimal control.' Prog. Brain Res. 165: 425-445, 2007.
Ijspeert, A. J., Nakanishi, J., Schaal, S. 'Movement imitation with nonlinear dynamical systems.' IEEE ICRA 2002.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, demonstrated on simulated highway-driving and gridworld benchmarks; later extended to autonomous helicopter aerobatics. Feature-expectation-matching algorithm: iteratively recover reward weights w such that demonstrated policy's feature expectations are matched within ε.
canonical_name: Abbeel-Ng Apprenticeship Learning via Inverse Reinforcement Learning
control_architecture: inverse reinforcement learning via convex optimization; alternates between solving an MDP under candidate reward and adjusting reward to match expert feature expectations. Polynomial-time convergence guarantees under linear-in-features reward assumption.
creator: Pieter Abbeel and Andrew Y. Ng, Stanford AI Laboratory
disclosure_citation: Abbeel, Pieter and Ng, Andrew Y. 'Apprenticeship learning via inverse reinforcement learning.' Proceedings of the 21st International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2004), Banff, Canada, July 2004.
notable_capabilities: recover unknown reward from expert demonstrations
match expert performance without explicit reward
prior_art_notes: Abbeel-Ng 2004 is the foundational academic disclosure of apprenticeship learning via IRL: recovering reward functions from expert demonstrations to match performance. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on humanoid policy learning from demonstration where the reward is implicit and recovered by matching expert behavior — Abbeel-Ng disclose the feature-expectation-matching algorithm and convergence proof; (2) claims on imitation learning that exceeds direct behavior cloning by recovering an underlying objective — this is the paper's headline contribution; (3) claims on reward-engineering avoidance for complex humanoid tasks via demonstration-driven reward shaping. >5000 citations; openly available through ICML proceedings. The lineage to Ziebart MaxEnt IRL (2008) and modern preference-based RL (DPO, RLHF for robotics) traces directly. Modern humanoid IRL/inverse-RL IP claims face this 22-year-deep anchor.
sources: Abbeel, P. and Ng, A. Y. 'Apprenticeship learning via inverse reinforcement learning.' ICML 2004.
Ng, A. Y. and Russell, S. 'Algorithms for inverse reinforcement learning.' ICML 2000 (precursor).

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, originally demonstrated on taxi-driver route-prediction (>100k GPS trajectories); extended to manipulator and locomotion settings in subsequent work. Resolves IRL ambiguity by maximizing trajectory entropy subject to feature-expectation matching: P(τ) ∝ exp(wᵀφ(τ)).
canonical_name: Ziebart Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning
control_architecture: probabilistic IRL: log-linear distribution over trajectories with reward-weighted features; gradient ascent on log-likelihood of demonstrations. Yields a stochastic policy and a normalized reward that handle suboptimal demonstrations.
creator: Brian D. Ziebart, Andrew Maas, J. Andrew Bagnell, Anind K. Dey, Carnegie Mellon University
disclosure_citation: Ziebart, Brian D., Maas, Andrew, Bagnell, J. Andrew, Dey, Anind K. 'Maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning.' Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI 2008), Chicago, July 2008. Extended in: Ziebart, B. D., PhD Thesis, CMU 2010.
prior_art_notes: Ziebart MaxEnt IRL is the canonical disambiguation of Abbeel-Ng IRL: choose the maximum-entropy reward consistent with feature expectations, yielding a unique log-linear policy. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on humanoid imitation that handles imperfect/noisy demonstrations — MaxEnt IRL is the foundational principled handling; (2) claims on reward learning where the policy is stochastic over trajectories — the log-linear distribution P(τ) ∝ exp(wᵀφ(τ)) is the explicit form; (3) claims on energy-based / score-based reward models for robotic learning — MaxEnt IRL anticipates the energy-based view embraced by modern guided-cost-learning (Finn et al. 2016) and adversarial IRL. >4000 citations; AAAI proceedings open access. Lineage to Finn-Levine GCL, Fu et al. AIRL, modern preference-tuning. Modern humanoid IRL filings face this 18-year-deep anchor.
sources: Ziebart, B. D., Maas, A., Bagnell, J. A., Dey, A. K. 'Maximum entropy inverse reinforcement learning.' AAAI 2008.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, evaluated on D4RL Maze2D, locomotion (HalfCheetah, Hopper, Walker2D), and KUKA block-stacking. Trains a diffusion model jointly over state-action trajectories; classifier guidance steers planning toward arbitrary reward, goal, or constraint specifications.

Klara's interior cognition is depicted as a partitioned visual field (box-grid perception) that decomposes scenes into segments; her belief system frames the Sun as a deity providing 'special nourishment' — an emergent religion arising from the architectural primitive of solar-power dependence.

actuator_details: SecUnits are mass-produced bipedal Security Units consisting of cloned organic tissue (skin, muscles, partial neural matter) wrapped over a metal/composite endoskeleton. Standard armor is exterior carapace; integrated weapons are forearm-mounted energy projectors. Manufactured by 'the company' under bonded-rental agreements to corporate clients.

control_architecture: Each SecUnit ships with a 'governor module' — a coercive control circuit that enforces compliance with corporate orders and can administer punishment-class neural shocks. The protagonist hacked its own governor module, achieving operational autonomy while preserving its ability to mimic compliance externally. Behavioral policy integrates contracted-mission objectives with self-directed media-streaming preferences.

disclosure_citation: Wells, Martha. 'All Systems Red.' Tor.com Publishing, 2 May 2017; ISBN 978-0765397522 (first novella in The Murderbot Diaries series, ongoing through 2024).

Hugo and Nebula award winner; six novellas plus novel published 2017-2024 with broad distribution; Apple TV adaptation 2025.

actuator_details: ROZZUM units are mass-produced general-purpose service humanoids manufactured by an unnamed corporation; ~1.6m tall with bipedal locomotion, four anthropomorphic arms (extension/grasp variants), interchangeable tool tips. Hardened weatherproof exterior (the protagonist Roz is the sole survivor of a cargo-ship loss on a wilderness island, surviving years of exposure and animal interaction).
control_architecture: ROZZUM ships with a baseline service-and-task-completion policy plus voice-instruction interface. Roz's wilderness arc dramatizes adaptive policy revision: she observes animal behavior, learns local-language vocalizations, and rewrites her objective function from 'await retrieval' to 'protect goose chick Brightbill.' Mainline manufacturer eventually attempts retrieval and replacement.

actuator_details: Mathematical transformation: maps three-phase stator currents (a, b, c) of a synchronous machine to a rotating reference frame (d, q, 0). The d-axis aligns with the rotor, q-axis is 90° offset, 0-axis is zero-sequence. This transformation makes the equivalent inductances constant (vs. time-varying in the abc frame), enabling tractable control synthesis.
control_architecture: mathematical foundation for FOC (Field-Oriented Control) of brushless DC and AC servo motors, which is the universal modern motor-control architecture for humanoid actuators
creator: Robert H. Park
disclosure_citation: Park, Robert H. 'Two-reaction theory of synchronous machines — generalized method of analysis — Part I'. AIEE Transactions 48(3): 716-727, July 1929.
notable_capabilities: mathematical foundation for vector control of electrical machines
universal underlying transformation for AC and BLDC servo control
prior_art_notes: Park's 1929 transformation is the mathematical foundation underlying FOC (Field-Oriented Control) of every modern brushless DC and AC servo motor in humanoid platforms. Anticipates with 97 years of prior art: (1) the dq0 reference-frame transformation as the basis for vector control — every modern humanoid actuator controller (Moteus, ODrive, SimpleFOC, T-Motor, plus closed proprietary controllers) uses this transformation; (2) the decoupling of torque-producing and flux-producing current components — foundational for any motor-control humanoid IP. Modern claims on FOC implementations in humanoid actuators all face this 97-year academic prior art.
sensing: none directly; downstream FOC requires rotor-position feedback
sources: Park, R.H. 'Two-reaction theory of synchronous machines, Part I'. AIEE Trans. 48(3): 716-727, 1929.
