actuator_details: Theoretical result: a continuous time-invariant feedback law that stabilizes a nonlinear system to an equilibrium must satisfy a specific topological condition. For systems that fail this condition (e.g. nonholonomic vehicles like wheeled cars and bipedal walkers near singular configurations), no continuous time-invariant stabilizing feedback exists. This necessitates time-varying or discontinuous control.
control_architecture: theoretical foundation for understanding limits of feedback stabilization in humanoid and mobile-robotic systems; directly motivates time-varying / discontinuous control architectures (LIPM walking, ZMP, switched-system bipedal)
creator: Roger W. Brockett, Harvard University
disclosure_citation: Brockett, Roger W. 'Asymptotic stability and feedback stabilization'. In Differential Geometric Control Theory (Brockett, Millman, Sussmann eds.), Birkhäuser, 1983, pp. 181-191.
notable_capabilities: foundational result for wheeled-robot and bipedal control theory
prior_art_notes: Brockett's 1983 condition is the theoretical foundation for understanding why certain humanoid and wheeled-robot systems cannot be stabilized with continuous time-invariant feedback. Modern claims on humanoid walking controllers, wheeled-balance controllers, and switched-system humanoid policies all rest on the design space Brockett's condition characterizes. Anticipates with 43 years of prior art: (1) theoretical justification for time-varying controllers in nonholonomic systems — relevant to wheeled-base humanoid IP; (2) the foundational characterization that motivates ZMP-based walking, LIPM-based walking, and modern reduced-order-model control. Heavily cited; canonical reference in nonlinear control textbooks.
sources: Brockett, R.W. 'Asymptotic stability and feedback stabilization'. Differential Geometric Control Theory, Birkhäuser, 1983.
Khalil, H. Nonlinear Systems (textbook reference for Brockett's condition).

actuator_details: Algorithm: estimates optical flow (apparent pixel motion) between consecutive image frames by linearizing the brightness-constancy assumption locally and solving a least-squares system per pixel neighborhood. Iterative refinement extends to large displacements via image pyramid (KLT — Kanade-Lucas-Tomasi tracker, 1991 extension by Tomasi).
control_architecture: visual servoing primitive: optical flow → ego-motion estimate or scene-motion estimate → control input. Foundational for SLAM, visual odometry, object tracking in robotic perception.
creator: Bruce D. Lucas and Takeo Kanade, Carnegie Mellon University
disclosure_citation: Lucas, Bruce D. and Kanade, Takeo. 'An iterative image registration technique with an application to stereo vision'. Proceedings of the 7th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI), Vancouver, August 1981, pp. 674-679.
prior_art_notes: Lucas-Kanade 1981 is the foundational academic disclosure of dense optical flow estimation for robotic vision. Anticipates with 45 years of prior art: (1) optical-flow-based visual servoing for humanoid manipulation and locomotion — relevant to claims on visual-tracking-based humanoid policies; (2) iterative least-squares formulation that extends to modern KLT and PWC-style optical flow networks; (3) image-pyramid for multi-scale flow estimation. The KLT tracker is essentially the universal default for visual feature tracking and underlies SLAM, visual odometry, and many manipulation control loops. Modern visual humanoid IP all face this 1981 academic anchor.
sources: Lucas, B.D. and Kanade, T. 'An iterative image registration technique'. IJCAI 1981.
Tomasi, C. and Kanade, T. 'Detection and tracking of point features'. CMU Tech Report CMU-CS-91-132, 1991.
Bouguet, J.-Y. 'Pyramidal implementation of the affine Lucas Kanade feature tracker'. OpenCV documentation, 1999-2024.

actuator_details: Algorithm: detects scale-invariant keypoints in images via difference-of-Gaussians extrema; describes each keypoint with a 128-dimensional histogram of local gradient orientations. Keypoints are invariant to scale and rotation, partially invariant to illumination and viewpoint. Standard for image matching, object recognition, and SLAM relocalization.
control_architecture: visual perception primitive: SIFT keypoints → image-to-image correspondence → scene reconstruction or object recognition
creator: David G. Lowe, University of British Columbia
disclosure_citation: Lowe, David G. 'Object recognition from local scale-invariant features'. Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV), Corfu, September 1999, pp. 1150-1157. Extended in Lowe, D.G. 'Distinctive image features from scale-invariant keypoints'. IJCV 60(2): 91-110, 2004.
prior_art_notes: SIFT 1999 (and the canonical 2004 IJCV paper) is one of the most-cited algorithms in computer vision and a foundational visual-feature anchor for humanoid perception. Anticipates: (1) scale-invariant feature detection and matching — relevant to claims on visual humanoid perception that use feature-based localization (every visual SLAM system pre-deep-learning, and many modern hybrid systems, use SIFT or its descendants ORB / SURF); (2) the 128-D local-gradient histogram descriptor architecture. Patented (US6711293, expired 2020); the 2004 IJCV paper is the standard citation. Modern visual humanoid IP that uses local-feature matching faces this 27-year academic anchor.
sources: Lowe, D.G. 'Object recognition from local scale-invariant features'. ICCV 1999.
Lowe, D.G. 'Distinctive image features from scale-invariant keypoints'. IJCV 60(2), 2004.

actuator_details: Visual SLAM system using ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) features. Three parallel threads: tracking (per-frame ORB matching to local map), local mapping (keyframe culling and bundle adjustment), loop closing (place recognition via bag-of-words + pose graph optimization). Open-source under GPL-v3.
control_architecture: visual perception substrate for humanoid platforms; provides 6-DOF camera pose + sparse 3D map at ~30 Hz on standard hardware
creator: Raul Mur-Artal, J.M.M. Montiel, Juan D. Tardós; University of Zaragoza
disclosure_citation: Mur-Artal, Raul; Montiel, J.M.M.; Tardós, Juan D. 'ORB-SLAM: a versatile and accurate monocular SLAM system'. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 31(5): 1147-1163, October 2015. Extended: ORB-SLAM2 (RGB-D + stereo, 2017); ORB-SLAM3 (visual-inertial + multi-map, 2021).
prior_art_notes: ORB-SLAM is one of the standard reference visual SLAM systems for humanoid platforms. Anticipates: (1) real-time monocular SLAM as a deployable architecture — relevant to claims on humanoid visual localization; (2) the three-thread tracking + mapping + loop-closing architecture — relevant to multi-thread perception humanoid IP; (3) ORB-feature-based place recognition for loop closure — relevant to scene-recognition humanoid claims. The 2015 T-RO paper plus subsequent ORB-SLAM2 (2017) and ORB-SLAM3 (2021) extensions provide deep prior art coverage; the GitHub release (GPL-v3) makes the architecture defensively-published.

actuator_details: Algorithm: trains a reward model from human preference comparisons (which of two trajectory pairs the human prefers) and then trains a policy via standard RL against the learned reward. Demonstrated on Atari and MuJoCo simulated tasks. Roughly 1000 binary preference comparisons sufficient to learn a competitive reward model.
canonical_name: RLHF (Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences)
control_architecture: policy-learning architecture: human preference data → reward model → policy via PPO/A2C-class RL. Foundational for modern LLM alignment (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) and increasingly for humanoid policy alignment.
creator: Paul Christiano, Jan Leike, Tom Brown, Miljan Martic, Shane Legg, Dario Amodei; OpenAI and DeepMind
disclosure_citation: Christiano, Paul; Leike, Jan; Brown, Tom; Martic, Miljan; Legg, Shane; Amodei, Dario. 'Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences'. NeurIPS 2017, June 12, 2017 (arXiv:1706.03741).
notable_capabilities: binary trajectory comparisons as preference signal
prior_art_notes: Christiano et al. 2017 RLHF is the foundational academic disclosure of preference-based reward learning at scale. Anticipates: (1) human-preference-based reward learning as a deployable policy-tuning architecture — directly relevant to modern claims on aligned-humanoid IP that use preference signals; (2) the architecture of separating reward-model learning from policy learning — relevant to modular alignment-and-policy humanoid claims; (3) binary trajectory preference signals as the supervisory mode — relevant to RLHF-on-humanoid claims (Anthropic's Constitutional AI, OpenAI's InstructGPT all build on this foundation, and the technique is being ported to humanoid policy alignment). The 2017 NeurIPS paper plus open-source code on GitHub provide extensive prior art coverage. Modern humanoid alignment IP all face this 9-year academic anchor.
sources: Christiano, P. et al. 'Deep reinforcement learning from human preferences'. NeurIPS 2017 (arXiv:1706.03741).

actuator_details: Architecture: jointly trains an image encoder and a text encoder to embed images and text descriptions into a shared vector space using contrastive loss over 400M (image, text) pairs scraped from the web. Resulting embeddings enable zero-shot classification, image retrieval, image-text alignment for downstream tasks.
control_architecture: visual-language alignment substrate; CLIP embeddings are used as a frozen perception backbone in many VLA humanoid policies (PaLM-E, Open X-Embodiment, RT-2 all use CLIP-class encoders or directly fine-tuned CLIP)
creator: Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Chris Hallacy, Aditya Ramesh, et al.; OpenAI

'Learning transferable visual models from natural language supervision'. arXiv:2103.00020, February 26, 2021. Published ICML 2021.
prior_art_notes: CLIP 2021 is the foundational academic disclosure of contrastive vision-language pretraining at internet scale. actuator_details: World-model RL algorithm: learns a recurrent state-space model (RSSM) of the environment, then trains a policy via RL within the imagination of the world model. DreamerV3 demonstrated cross-domain generalization across 150+ Atari, DMLab, MineRL, and continuous-control benchmarks with a single set of hyperparameters.
control_architecture: model-based RL: world model (RSSM) + actor + critic, all trained jointly. Imagination rollouts in the learned world model substitute for real-environment rollouts.

actuator_details: Software framework, not a physical platform. MJX is a pure-JAX reimplementation of the MuJoCo physics engine that runs natively on GPU/TPU via XLA compilation. Supports MJCF model definition, contact dynamics with soft and hard constraints, articulated rigid-body dynamics, and convex friction-cone solvers. Apache-2.0 license. Differentiable end-to-end via JAX autodiff, enabling gradient-based policy optimization and trajectory optimization directly through the simulator. Achieves >10,000 envs in parallel on a single H100.
control_architecture: Provides differentiable physics substrate. Used in DeepMind's locomotion training pipelines (Brax + MJX, OPAL, MaxBPC), in trajectory optimization (cross-entropy MPC, predictive sampling MPC), and in academic RL libraries (Brax, Mujoco Playground). Supports JAX vmap/pmap for SIMD-style vectorized rollouts. MuJoCo's contact model is Featherstone-derived and includes soft-contact regularization unique to the MuJoCo lineage.

Originally MuJoCo: Todorov, Erez, and Tassa, 'MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control,' IEEE/RSJ IROS 2012, 5026-5033. Apache-2.0 license.

Modern claims on differentiable simulation for humanoid training face this academic anchor.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, demonstrated on simulated MuJoCo humanoid (28-DoF), swimmer, and cheetah models. Iterative Linear Quadratic Gaussian (iLQG) — a differential-dynamic-programming-class trajectory optimizer that linearizes the dynamics about a nominal trajectory and solves a sequence of LQG subproblems with regularization. Receding-horizon online application enables real-time MPC at >100 Hz on 28-DoF humanoid models. The 2012 paper introduces the regularization scheme and line search that made iLQG run online.

canonical_name: Tassa iLQG / Synthesis and Stabilization of Complex Behaviors
control_architecture: Online receding-horizon trajectory optimization (model-predictive control) via iLQG. Computes locally optimal feedback policies in addition to feedforward trajectories — i.e., the algorithm produces both u(t) and a time-varying gain K(t), giving stabilizing closed-loop control. Demonstrated humanoid getup, walking, and recovery from disturbances in MuJoCo simulation.

actuator_details: Algorithmic disclosure, demonstrated on simulated humanoid characters performing locomotion, climbing, manipulation, and acrobatic motions. CIO formulates motion synthesis as a single trajectory optimization problem in which contact existence and contact forces are continuous decision variables (rather than combinatorial mode switches). A complementarity-style regularization enforces contact constraints without requiring pre-specified contact schedules. Solved with an SQP-class nonlinear optimizer.
aliases: Discovery of Complex Behaviors through Contact-Invariant Optimization
control_architecture: Trajectory optimization with continuous-variable contact representation. The optimizer discovers when and where to place contacts (hand placement, foothold selection, manipulation grasps) as part of the same optimization that solves for joint torques and trajectories. Eliminates the manual design of contact sequences that hampered earlier trajectory optimization for humanoids.

actuator_details: Software framework, not a physical platform. C++ library with Python bindings for multi-contact optimal control via differential-dynamic-programming-class methods. BSD-3-Clause license. Builds on Pinocchio (Carpentier 2019) for analytical rigid-body dynamics derivatives. Supports floating-base humanoid and quadruped platforms (TALOS, ANYmal, HRP-2, Atlas). Provides DDP, FDDP (feasibility-driven DDP), and BoxDDP (control-limited DDP) solvers.
aliases: Contact RObot COntrol by Differential DYnamic programming Library
control_architecture: Multi-contact differential dynamic programming framework. Models multi-phase contact schedules (left foot, right foot, double support, manipulation contacts) and solves trajectory optimization through them with analytical derivatives via Pinocchio. Used in real-time MPC pipelines on TALOS, ANYmal, and Cassie. The FDDP variant of Mastalli 2020 improves feasibility behavior compared to vanilla DDP.

actuator_details: Variable-impedance anthropomorphic hand-arm system. Hand: 19-DoF five-fingered anthropomorphic hand ('Awiwi') driven by 38 tendons via 38 brushless DC motors located in the forearm. Each finger joint is antagonistically driven by tendon pairs, with mechanically programmable nonlinear elastic elements that implement variable joint stiffness analogous to human muscle co-contraction. Arm: 7-DoF arm with variable-stiffness joints (FSJ — Floating Spring Joint) using parallel elastic elements. Total system has 52 motors. Designed to survive collisions at human-like speeds via mechanical energy absorption rather than software safety.
control_architecture: Impedance control with mechanically programmable variable stiffness; antagonistic-tendon joint-level stiffness regulation in hardware (not just software). Uses DLR's joint-torque-impedance framework descending from Albu-Schäffer's lightweight-arm work. Demonstrated robustness to impact disturbances (hammer-strike experiments) without controller intervention because mechanical compliance absorbs the energy.

actuator_details: Augmented two-synergy underactuated anthropomorphic hand: 19 internal DoFs driven by TWO motors (vs. one in the original SoftHand). Each motor drives an independent tendon routed through a distinct postural synergy derived from PCA on human grasping kinematics. The two synergies span a richer subspace of grasp+manipulation than the single-synergy predecessor — the second synergy enables abduction/adduction patterns and limited in-hand manipulation. Compliant elastic-return joints throughout; passive shape adaptation.
control_architecture: Two-DoF tendon position control along the two principal grasping synergies; supports in-hand re-grasping by trajectories within the augmented synergy subspace. Compliant joints handle object shape variation passively, eliminating the need for explicit perception-driven grasp planning.

actuator_details: Three-finger underactuated tendon-driven hand. Each finger: two phalanges with passive compliant joints and a single tendon for flexion + a spring antagonist for extension. Whole hand: three motors (one per finger) plus optional palm-rotation degree of freedom. Designed for inherent grasp robustness via underactuation and compliant adaptation. ReFlex SF (Sensorized Finger) variant adds tactile fingertip sensors via the TakkTile MEMS array technology.
control_architecture: Single-DoF-per-finger tendon position or torque control; passive compliance handles object shape variation. Yale OpenHand Project provides multiple parametric hand variants (Model M, Model O, Model T42) all sharing the underactuated-tendon paradigm. Open-source ROS drivers for ReFlex SF.

actuator_details: Quasi-direct-drive (QDD) actuators throughout — direct lineage from the Mini Cheetah actuator design (low-gear-ratio, high-torque-density brushless motors with custom motor controllers). 18 actuated DoF: 5 per leg, 4 per arm, plus a torso. Light-weight design (~24 kg) compared to hydraulic-class humanoids. Backdrivable joints enable proprioceptive torque sensing without dedicated torque sensors.
control_architecture: Convex MPC with explicit actuator-dynamics model (motor inertia, torque limits, current limits) integrated into the optimization. Centroidal-momentum-based reduced-order model for online MPC. Capable of acrobatic behaviors (jumps, flips) via offline trajectory optimization combined with online tracking.

actuator_details: Hybrid bipedal-aerial robot. Two articulated legs each with 3 actuated DoF (hip, knee, ankle) for ground locomotion. Each leg also carries a propeller (so 4 propellers total: two per foot/ankle area) for aerial flight and balance assistance during walking. Brushless DC actuators throughout. Total mass ~2.5 kg. Designed to switch fluidly between bipedal walking and quadcopter-style flight, plus mixed modes (slacklining, skateboarding) where propellers provide balance authority while legs handle ground contact.
control_architecture: Hybrid bipedal-aerial nonlinear MPC. Onboard IMU and motion-capture localization for outdoor/indoor flight. Walking gaits stabilized via simultaneous use of leg actuation and propeller thrust — propellers provide ankle-torque-augmenting forces that ZMP-class bipeds cannot exploit. Demonstrated slackline traversal, skateboarding, stair descent.

Science Robotics paper provides full design and control disclosure. Modern hybrid-locomotion humanoid IP faces this 5-year-deep academic anchor.

actuator_details: Algorithmic and control disclosure on the original Boston Dynamics Atlas hydraulic humanoid (DRC-era; 28 hydraulically actuated DoF, ~150 kg). Papers describe whole-body QP-based inverse-dynamics control, footstep-region MIP planning (Deits-Tedrake 2014), iterative SQP trajectory optimization, contact-aware Kalman-filter state estimation, and the IRIS region-of-attraction footstep planner. Publications cover Atlas's entire controller stack as deployed at the DARPA Robotics Challenge Finals (June 2015).
canonical_name: Atlas academic publications (Kuindersma et al., DRC era)
control_architecture: Whole-body inverse-dynamics QP control: at every control step solve a quadratic program for joint torques minimizing tracking error subject to contact constraints, friction cones, and torque limits. Footstep planning via mixed-integer convex optimization over the IRIS regions decomposition of free space. Trajectory optimization via direct transcription with SQP. Contact-aware EKF state estimation. The Kuindersma 2016 AURO paper provides the consolidated end-to-end controller architecture.
creator: Scott Kuindersma, Russ Tedrake, Robin Deits, Maurice Fallon, Andrés Valenzuela, Hongkai Dai, Frank Permenter, Twan Koolen, Pat Marion; MIT CSAIL Robot Locomotion Group (DRC Atlas team)

Anticipates with element-by-element specificity: (1) whole-body QP-based inverse-dynamics control on a hydraulically-actuated humanoid platform — directly relevant to commercial claims on QP-based humanoid IP (every modern humanoid runs a derivative); (2) the IRIS-regions mixed-integer convex footstep planner — relevant to claims on footstep-planning humanoid IP; (3) iterative SQP trajectory optimization with contact schedule — anticipates claims overlapping Crocoddyl (mastalli-crocoddyl-2020) and DDP approaches; (4) the consolidated end-to-end stack documentation in AURO 2016 — the most complete public disclosure of a working DRC-class humanoid control architecture. Drake source code accompanies the publications under BSD license. Modern QP-IDC-based humanoid IP filings face this 12-year-deep academic anchor with full implementation disclosure.

actuator_details: Originally six 1.5 kW electric thrusters in vectored arrangement; upgraded to high-efficiency rim-driven brushless thrusters in the 2013 Personnel Sphere upgrade. Variable-buoyancy via syntactic-foam main body (positive buoyancy) plus variable-ballast trim tank (active trim). Two seven-function manipulator arms (Schilling Robotics or Kraft Telerobotics in current configuration).
control_architecture: Manned operation by 1 pilot + 2 observers in titanium pressure sphere (2-inch wall, 4500 m depth rating since 1973 hull replacement; Ti-6Al-4V since 2013 sphere upgrade). Thruster commands via joystick; manipulator via dedicated master controllers. No autonomy — every motion is a human command. The control architecture's value to the corpus is demonstrating that bimanual underwater dexterous manipulation has been a solved operational problem at depth since the 1960s.
creator: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution / Allyn Vine concept (1956); General Mills Mechanical Division built v1
disclosure_citation: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. DSV Alvin operational since June 1964; first published 4500 m dive Aug 1973. Extensive academic publication record via WHOI deep-submergence vehicle group: Ballard 1985 (Titanic dives), Yoerger et al. mission reports 1991+, Kohnen ed. 'Manned Submersibles' (1978). Operational and design details in the public domain via U.S. Navy / WHOI.
end_effector: 2× seven-function hydraulic master-slave manipulator arms with interchangeable end-effectors (parallel jaw, scoop, sample basket)
notable_capabilities: bimanual master-slave manipulation since first deployment
found USS Thresher debris (1964-65), explored Titanic (1986), HMS Hood

prior_art_notes: DSV Alvin is the foundational manned deep-submergence vehicle. Its 60-year operational record establishes essentially every architectural element of modern submersible robotics as long-anticipated prior art: titanium pressure-hull design at 4500 m+ depth (1973), syntactic-foam buoyancy matched to depth pressure, variable-ballast trim tanks, vectored-thruster station-keeping, master-slave manipulator pairs for sample collection. Directly shields free-humanoid-submersible commitments on: 50 m pressure hull (62 years deeper than Alvin's 1964 baseline), 8-thruster vectored layout (the 6-thruster Alvin pattern is the lower bound), bimanual manipulator architecture (Alvin's Schilling/Kraft 7-function arms are the ROV-class equivalent of the bipedal upper body). Any commercial humanoid AUV claim on these elements faces a 62-year-deep public-domain academic lineage with extensive WHOI publication.
sensing: forward sonar, multibeam imaging sonar (since 2000s upgrades), HD video cameras, LED illuminators, sample-collection and chemical-sensor instrumentation by mission

actuator_details: Six brushless DC electric thrusters in vectored arrangement (4 horizontal + 2 vertical); 6-DoF station-keeping. Two 7-function hydraulic manipulator arms (Kraft Telerobotics Predator). Tethered to surface ship via 10 km fiber-optic + power cable; no onboard battery for primary thrust. Net buoyancy slightly positive; tether tension / thruster control trim depth.
control_architecture: Tethered teleoperation from surface-ship Medea relay vehicle (Argo-class imaging tow) and Jason control van. Pilot drives via joystick; co-pilot operates manipulators; scientist operates instruments. Auto-heading and auto-depth available since 1995 software refresh. The teleoperation lineage is the canonical bimanual-underwater-manipulation prior art.

Onboard navigation: DVL+IMU+pressure dead-reckoning in AUV mode; supplemented by surface ship USBL when in ROV mode.

actuator_details: **Variable-buoyancy propulsion** — no thrusters in primary propulsion. Vehicle ascends and descends by changing displaced volume (oil pumped between internal reservoir and external bladder). Wings convert vertical motion into horizontal motion. Pitch and roll trim via internal-mass servo. ~25 cm/s horizontal speed; 1000 km range per battery charge. The fundamental architectural alternative to thrust-active station-keeping.
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mission. Surface-fix via GPS at every surfacing event (every 6-24 hours). Iridium satellite link for command/data exchange during surfacing. No real-time teleoperation between surfacings. The glider is the canonical low-power long-duration AUV.

Rutgers Glider Lab Atlantic crossings 2009+ (a glider crossed the Atlantic — first AUV to do so)
prior_art_notes: Slocum is the canonical variable-buoyancy underwater glider. Stommel's 1989 concept paper and Webb's 2001 IEEE J. Oceanic Engineering paper establish a 36-year-deep open-academic prior-art chain on **variable-buoyancy propulsion as an alternative to thrust-active station-keeping**. Directly relevant to free-humanoid-submersible: the architectural choice between 'negatively-buoyant + thrust-active' (submersible's commitment) and 'variable-buoyancy + glider' (Slocum lineage) is a documented public-domain trade-off space. Any commercial AUV claim that one approach is novel art faces this 36-year-deep public-domain branching point.
sensing: CTD, dissolved oxygen, fluorometer, optical scatter, GPS (at surface), Iridium modem (at surface), pressure depth, attitude IMU
sources: Webb, Simonetti, Jones, IEEE J. Oceanic Eng. 26(4) 2001.
Schofield et al. 'Slocum gliders: Robust and ready', J. Field Robotics 2007.

actuator_details: Variable-buoyancy propulsion via internal pressure-bladder oil-displacement system (mechanically distinct from Slocum's pump-based system; achieves lower power consumption per buoyancy adjustment). Pressure-vessel hull rated 1000 m. Roll and pitch trim via internal-mass servo.
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mission. GPS+Iridium at surfacing. INS+pressure dead-reckoning between surfacings.
creator: University of Washington Applied Physics Laboratory; Eriksen et al.
disclosure_citation: Eriksen, C. C., Osse, T. J., Light, R. D., et al. 'Seaglider: A Long-Range Autonomous Underwater Vehicle for Oceanographic Research'. IEEE J. Oceanic Engineering vol. 26 no. 4 2001.
notable_capabilities: longer endurance than Slocum class (6+ months on a single battery)
lower per-cycle buoyancy-adjustment power than Slocum
commercial license: U Washington → iRobot → Kongsberg
prior_art_notes: Seaglider is the second canonical variable-buoyancy glider lineage, with a fully open academic disclosure (Eriksen 2001). Together with Slocum, establishes that the variable-buoyancy-glider architecture is a 24-year-deep open-academic prior-art branch. Directly shields free-humanoid-submersible's architectural commitment to thrust-active vs. variable-buoyancy as the documented public choice.
sensing: CTD, dissolved oxygen, fluorometer, GPS (at surface), Iridium modem, pressure depth, attitude IMU
sources: Eriksen et al. IEEE J. Oceanic Eng. 26(4) 2001.

actuator_details: Hovering AUV/ROV hybrid platform: torpedo-form transit body (~3 m long) transforms in-water to expose dual humanoid manipulator arms (2× 7-DoF) for hovering manipulation. 4-thruster vectored layout in transit configuration. Pressure-balanced Li-ion power. Precise actuator architecture (motor type, reducer, joint mechanism) not publicly disclosed.
control_architecture: Hybrid autonomous + supervised teleoperation. Through-water acoustic comms (Sonardyne BlueComm + acoustic-modem fallback) for low-bandwidth supervised control. Onboard autonomy for transit and basic manipulation primitives. Specific control architecture, perception stack, and manipulation policies are trade-secret. Founders' background at NASA Robonaut and Johnson Space Center implies whole-body operational-space control lineage.
creator: Houston Mechatronics Inc. / Nauticus Robotics Inc.; founded by ex-NASA Robonaut engineers (Pratt, Krause, et al.)
disclosure_citation: Houston Mechatronics Inc. (founded 2014; rebranded Nauticus Robotics 2021; public via SPAC 2022 ticker KITT). Aquanaut public reveal April 2018 via company website + Houston Chronicle / IEEE Spectrum coverage. Subsequent Nauticus 8-K SEC disclosures, 10-K filings, demo videos.
end_effector: 2× anthropomorphic dexterous manipulators (specific end-effector configuration mission-dependent; demo videos show parallel-jaw grippers and sample-collection tools)
notable_capabilities: transformer architecture: torpedo transit ↔ humanoid manipulation pose
over-the-horizon supervised teleoperation via acoustic + RF surface buoy
demo videos show valve-turning, sample-collection, hose-mating tasks
notes: DRAFT: stronger entry will follow as Nauticus discloses additional mechanism via patent filings or technical publications. Current entry establishes the existence-of-claim against which corpus-driven prior-art shielding is asserted.
prior_art_notes: Aquanaut is the **most direct existing prior art for free-humanoid-submersible**. Public-disclosure surface (corporate website, SEC filings, IEEE Spectrum coverage, demo videos) does not reveal specific actuator or control mechanism. The capability set claimed — hovering manipulation, anthropomorphic arms, hybrid AUV/ROV mode-switching, pressure-balanced subsea power, acoustic+RF-buoy supervised teleop — is fully covered by deep open academic prior art chains: Jason ROV (1989) for tethered manipulation; Nereus (2008) for AUV/ROV mode-switching; OceanOne (Stanford 2016) for bimanual humanoid AUV manipulation with full academic publication; Slocum/Seaglider (1989/2001) for variable-buoyancy as the documented alternative; DSV Alvin (1964) for pressure-hull design; Bluefin BPS (2008+) for pressure-balanced Li-ion. Any Aquanaut/Nauticus commercial claim on architectural elements faces deep open public-domain prior art chains. The submersible morphology in free-humanoid-submersible explicitly shields against Aquanaut's claim surface by anchoring every commitment in this open-academic lineage.
sensing: multibeam imaging sonar, HD stereo cameras, LED illumination array, depth pressure, IMU, DVL, USBL acoustic positioning
sources: IEEE Spectrum, 'This Underwater Robot Transforms Into a Submarine That Can Stretch Out to Use Both Arms', April 2018.
Nauticus Robotics corporate website (nauticusrobotics.com), Aquanaut product page.

actuator_details: Hovering AUV with anthropomorphic upper body. 8-thruster vectored layout for full-6-DoF station-keeping. Two 7-DoF anthropomorphic arms with underactuated 3-finger hands. All-electric brushless thrusters. Pressure-tolerant electronics in oil-filled compartments + pressure hull for battery and main computer.
control_architecture: Bilateral haptic teleoperation via Sigma.7 master controllers (Force Dimension). Operator in surface-ship control room receives stereo video + haptic force feedback at 1 kHz; commands robot motion at 1 kHz via fiber tether. Khatib group's whole-body operational-space framework (1987+ academic lineage) is the control substrate. Open academic publication.
creator: Stanford Robotics Laboratory; Oussama Khatib group; King Abdullah Univ. of Science and Technology partnership
disclosure_citation: Khatib, O., Yeh, X., Brantner, G., et al. 'Ocean One: A Robotic Avatar for Oceanic Discovery'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine vol. 23 no. 4, 2016. First operational dive (La Lune wreck, Mediterranean, 100 m depth) April 2016.
end_effector: 2× anthropomorphic 7-DoF arms with 3-finger underactuated grippers; force/torque sensors at wrists
notable_capabilities: bilateral haptic teleoperation with force feedback
first dive: La Lune wreck (Louis XIV ship, 100 m depth) Mediterranean April 2016
subsequent ops: Crete archeological surveys, deep-water samples
prior_art_notes: OceanOne is the canonical academic bimanual humanoid AUV. 9-year-deep open academic publication via the Khatib group at Stanford. Establishes element-by-element prior art for: 8-thruster vectored layout for humanoid AUV (exact match to free-humanoid-submersible commitment), bimanual 7-DoF anthropomorphic arms underwater, bilateral haptic teleoperation, F/T-sensor-in-the-loop manipulation, integration with Khatib's operational-space framework. Directly anticipates every architectural element of free-humanoid-submersible's design and any Aquanaut/Nauticus commercial claim on the same. The Khatib lineage extends back through Stanford operational-space papers to 1987 (38 years).
sensing: stereo HD cameras, multibeam imaging sonar, depth pressure, IMU, DVL, USBL acoustic positioning, wrist F/T sensors, haptic force feedback to operator
sources: G. Brantner, O. Khatib, 'Controlling Ocean One', Stanford Robotics Lab tech reports 2014-2016.

actuator_details: Successor to OceanOne with depth extended from 200 m to 1000 m. Glass-sphere syntactic-foam buoyancy modules. Pressure-tolerant electronics in oil-filled compartments at full operating depth. 8-thruster vectored layout retained from OceanOne baseline. Anthropomorphic arms re-engineered with pressure-tolerant joints (no rigid pressure hull on the arms; oil-filled actuator compartments).
control_architecture: Bilateral haptic teleoperation via Sigma.7 + Stanford whole-body operational-space framework. Tether for primary control + power at 1 km depth.
creator: Stanford Robotics Laboratory; Khatib group; expanded design team
disclosure_citation: Khatib, O., Brantner, G., Yeh, X., Salisbury, S. et al. 'OceanOneK: A 1000-meter-depth, bimanual underwater humanoid for archeology and marine exploration'. Science Robotics 2022 (announced July 2022). Subsequent IEEE RA-L publications detail control and pressure-hull innovations.
end_effector: 2× anthropomorphic 7-DoF pressure-tolerant arms with 3-finger underactuated grippers; F/T sensing
notable_capabilities: pressure-tolerant arms (oil-filled, no rigid pressure hull on appendages)
first 1 km depth bimanual humanoid manipulation
deployed for Mediterranean shipwreck archeology (Italy 2022, France 2023)
power_source: surface-supplied via 1 km tether + onboard battery backup
prior_art_notes: OceanOneK extends the OceanOne lineage to 1000 m depth and adds pressure-tolerant oil-filled-actuator art. Directly shields any commercial humanoid AUV claim on: deep-depth (>500 m) bimanual humanoid manipulation, pressure-tolerant joint actuation (no rigid pressure hull on appendages), and integration of Khatib's 38-year operational-space framework with deep underwater manipulation. A 3-year-deep open-academic prior art chain with full element-by-element technical disclosure.
sensing: stereo HD cameras (pressure-tolerant housings), multibeam imaging sonar, depth pressure, IMU, DVL, USBL, wrist F/T
sources: BBC, Le Monde, IEEE Spectrum coverage of Mediterranean shipwreck operations 2022-2023.

actuator_details: Underwater-physics simulator: rigid-body dynamics + fluid drag + buoyancy + thruster models + cable dynamics (for tethered ROVs) + sonar simulation. C++ engine with Python bindings; ROS 2 integration. Renders via OpenGL for stereo simulated camera feeds. The de facto open-source academic underwater robotics simulator.
control_architecture: Provides simulation substrate for arbitrary control architectures. Standard interfaces for URDF/SDF import; ROS 2 / ROS 1 node integration; Python policy hosting.
creator: Patryk Cieslak (University of Girona / Computer Vision and Robotics group)
disclosure_citation: Cieslak, P. 'Stonefish: An Advanced Open-Source Simulation Tool Designed for Marine Robotics'. OCEANS 2019 IEEE/MTS, Marseille; preceded by IROS 2018 workshop demo. Open-source under CC-BY-NC-SA initially; later relicensed Apache-2.0 for upstream merge into ROS Underwater (2021).
prior_art_notes: Stonefish is the canonical open-source academic underwater robotics simulator. 7 years of public-academic publication and Apache-2.0 source. Establishes prior art for: fluid-drag-aware AUV/ROV simulation, simulated sonar return modeling, tether-dynamics simulation, ROS-integrated policy training for marine robotics. Directly shields free-humanoid-submersible's Phase-1 sim-to-real workflow (alongside Genesis MPM/fluid for higher-fidelity hydrodynamics). Any commercial claim on 'underwater-physics-aware sim-to-real for AUVs' faces 7 years of full-source open prior art.
sensing: simulated multibeam sonar, simulated stereo cameras, simulated DVL, simulated IMU, simulated USBL

actuator_details: Software framework for underwater acoustic-network protocol research and deployment. Agent-based architecture; Java/Groovy DSL; runs on commodity hardware atop acoustic modem firmware. Supports all standard underwater MAC and routing protocols + custom user-defined protocols.
control_architecture: Provides protocol stack + simulator for underwater acoustic networking. JANUS-compatible. Apache-2.0 open source.
creator: Mandar Chitre group, Acoustic Research Laboratory, National University of Singapore; commercialized via Subnero Pte Ltd
disclosure_citation: Chitre, M., Bhatnagar, R., Soh, W. S. 'UnetStack: An Agent-Based Software Stack and Simulator for Underwater Networks'. OCEANS 2014 St. John's. Open-source via Subnero Pte Ltd / Acoustic Research Laboratory NUS. Apache-2.0.
notable_capabilities: supports standard MAC + routing + transport protocols
deployed in commercial Subnero modems + numerous academic field deployments
prior_art_notes: UnetStack is the canonical open-source underwater-networking framework. 11 years of academic + commercial deployment under Apache-2.0. Shields any humanoid AUV claim on 'underwater acoustic networking stack' or 'multi-vehicle subsea coordination protocol'. Directly relevant to free-humanoid-submersible's commitment to acoustic comms (SHOAL fleet coordination at dock-A/B requires multi-vehicle protocols).
sources: Chitre et al. OCEANS 2014 St. John's.

actuator_details: Underwater acoustic-communications waveform standard. 11.5 kHz center frequency, 4.4 kHz bandwidth, FH-BFSK modulation, convolutional coding. Designed for inter-operator interoperability in underwater command-and-control. Reference implementation in C / Python; multiple commercial modem vendors implement. NATO open standard.
control_architecture: Provides standardized acoustic-comm waveform; higher-layer protocols (e.g. UnetStack) layer atop JANUS PHY.
creator: NATO STO Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE); Joao Alves / John Potter et al.
disclosure_citation: Potter, J., Alves, J., Green, D., Zappa, G., Nissen, I., McCoy, K. 'The JANUS underwater communications standard'. UComms 2014; ratified as NATO STANAG 4748 March 2017. Reference implementation open via NATO Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE), La Spezia. Open standard.
notable_capabilities: interoperability across commercial modems (Subnero, EvoLogics, Sonardyne, etc.)
prior_art_notes: JANUS is the open NATO standard for underwater acoustic communication. 8 years of public-domain standard + reference implementation. Shields any humanoid AUV claim on standardized acoustic-comm waveforms. Directly relevant to free-humanoid-submersible's acoustic-comms commitment for shoal-fleet inter-vehicle coordination at dock-A subsurface.
sources: NATO STO CMRE JANUS reference page (cmre.nato.int/janus).

actuator_details: Six-legged sprawl-tuned crawling robot (~75 g class). Single brushless DC motor drives a four-bar mechanism that produces alternating tripod leg motion. **Sprawl angle is mechanically tunable** between flat (legs splayed wide) and tall (legs pulled in) configurations to adapt to different terrains and obstacle types. PCB-process-fabricated linkage frames; passive compliance via flexible polymer.
control_architecture: Open-loop alternating-tripod gait; sprawl angle is mechanically set per terrain. Pre-programmed mission patterns; no real-time adaptation.
creator: UC Berkeley Biomimetic Millisystems Lab; Ronald Fearing group; Kohut, Karras, et al.
disclosure_citation: Karras, J. T., Fuller, C. L., Carpenter, K. C., Buscicchio, A., McKeeby, D., Norris, C. J., Parcheta, C. E., Royal, M. I., Wilcox, B. H., Fearing, R. S. 'Climbing with sprawl-tuned autonomous robots'. (Original Kohut/Fearing STAR variants 2010-2013.) IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2013. UC Berkeley Biomimetic Millisystems Lab.
notable_capabilities: 5 m/s top speed (10× body-length per second)
mechanical sprawl tuning for terrain adaptation
prior_art_notes: STAR is the original sprawl-tuned reconfigurable miniature robot from the Fearing group at Berkeley. 13-year open-academic publication record. Establishes the 'sprawl-tuned wheel-leg-hybrid + four-bar mechanism' architectural pattern that the entire STAR family (RSTAR, TSTAR, FSTAR, FCSTAR, AmphiSTAR, DSTAR) descends from. Directly shields free-humanoid-centaur's wheel-leg-hybrid commitment and any commercial claim on compact reconfigurable-mechanism wheel-leg robotics.
sensing: bump-switch contact sensors (some variants); minimal onboard sensing — relies on mechanical adaptation
sources: Kohut, N. J., Birkmeyer, P. M., Peterson, K. C., Fearing, R. S. 'Maneuverability and mobility in palm-sized legged robots'. SPIE 8389 2012.

actuator_details: Reconfigurable wheel-leg robot with extensible body (Rising STAR — the body extends/retracts to climb steps). Independent leg-length control and sprawl tuning. ~150-200 g class. Multiple actuated DoF (a major departure from the single-motor STAR original) enabling step-climbing, obstacle-traversal, and gait reconfiguration.
control_architecture: Multi-DoF reconfiguration controlled by onboard MCU; pre-programmed locomotion modes selectable per terrain. Open-loop primarily; some variants add IMU feedback.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; David Zarrouk group
disclosure_citation: Zarrouk, D., Mann, M., Degani, N., Yehuda, T., Jarbi, N., Hess, A. 'Single Actuator Wave-Like Robot (SAW): Design, Modeling, and Experiments' and follow-up RSTAR papers (IEEE RA-L 2018-2019). Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Bio-inspired and Medical Robotics Lab. RSTAR = 'Rising STAR'.
end_effector: four/six wheels or whegs depending on configuration
notable_capabilities: step-climbing via body-extension mechanism (up to 6 steps)
switching between rolling and walking modes mid-task
founded the Zarrouk-group STAR lineage at Ben-Gurion
prior_art_notes: RSTAR is the immediate predecessor of DSTAR and the founding member of the Zarrouk-group Ben-Gurion STAR lineage. 7 years of open-academic publication via IEEE RA-L and IROS. Establishes element-by-element prior art for: wheel-leg-hybrid reconfigurable robots, body-extension step-climbing, turtle-gait crawling without wheels, mode-switching between rolling and walking. Directly shields free-humanoid-centaur commitments on wheel-leg hybrid morphology and mode-switching.
sensing: onboard IMU; some variants add depth/camera
sources: Zarrouk, D. et al. 'RSTAR' IEEE RA-L 2018-2019.
Ben-Gurion University Bio-inspired and Medical Robotics Lab (bgu.ac.il/zarrouklab).

actuator_details: Amphibious member of the STAR family. Adds **water-driving capability** via wheel-paddle hybrid ground contact patches. 3.5 m/s on land, 1.5 m/s in water. Sealed enclosure for amphibious operation. Sprawl-tuning + leg reconfiguration carried over from RSTAR. Limited obstacle-climbing in this variant (the priority was the aquatic-terrestrial transition).
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mode-switching between terrestrial and aquatic locomotion. Operator selects mode pre-mission.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; Avi Cohen, David Zarrouk
disclosure_citation: Cohen, A., Zarrouk, D. 'AmphiSTAR: A High-Speed Amphibious Reconfigurable Robot'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 2023; ICRA 2023 demo. Ben-Gurion University, Zarrouk lab.
end_effector: wheel-paddle hybrid contact patches (terrestrial wheels double as aquatic paddles)
notable_capabilities: first STAR-family member to operate in water
prior_art_notes: AmphiSTAR establishes 3-year-deep open-academic prior art for **terrestrial-aquatic transition in a single platform with shared ground-contact mechanism**. Directly relevant to free-humanoid-submersible (and the centaur's wetland mode-transition) — proves that wheel-paddle hybrid contact patches and sealed-enclosure amphibious operation are well-anticipated open art. Any commercial claim on amphibious humanoid robotics faces this lineage plus the deeper aquatic-robotics chain (Slocum/Seaglider, OceanOne, AmphiSTAR).
sensing: IMU + depth pressure sensor; camera optional
sources: Cohen, A., Zarrouk, D. IEEE RA-L 2023.

actuator_details: Most recent (2026) member of the STAR family. **Two independently-actuated four-bar extension mechanisms (FBEM)** + sprawl mechanism with extended range (sprawl angle θ ∈ [-105°, +105°]). 1150 g total mass. Each side has independent FBEM (αL, αR ∈ [-65°, +65°]) — asymmetric configurations enable **rolling sideways**, COM control in any direction, and 18 cm horizontal-gap traversal. 76 mm wheels. PLA+ 3D-printed body. Servo motors: 9imod DSC55MG (sprawl, 5.4 Nm), NEEBRC NB-H015 (FBEM, 2.29 Nm × 2), SA19 (drive, 1.77 Nm × 2). Raspberry Pi 4 B with Auto pHat driver. 2-cell LiPo + secondary battery for compute.
control_architecture: Five independent servo-motor DoF with kinematic + quasi-static force models published. Pre-programmed gait selection: turtle gait, sideways rolling, climbing, obstacle traversal. Wi-Fi + Bluetooth communication for remote operation or pre-programmed mission. Validated in experiment: 20 cm wall climbing (66% improvement over symmetric FBEM designs like RSTAR), uneven-terrain crossing, sideways rolling, self-recovery from stuck states.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; Tomer Siboni, Matan Coronel, David Zarrouk
disclosure_citation: Siboni, T., Coronel, M., Zarrouk, D. 'Design and Modeling of a Reconfigurable Robot: Decoupled STAR (DSTAR)'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters vol. 11 no. 1, January 2026, pp. 882-889. DOI: 10.1109/LRA.2025.3634888. Ben-Gurion University, Department of Mechanical Engineering / Bio-inspired Robotics Lab. Funded by Helmsley Charitable Trust + Marcus Endowment Fund.
notable_capabilities: 20 cm wall obstacle traversal (66% improvement over RSTAR)
sideways rolling via asymmetric FBEM configuration
operates on grass, dirt, stones, rubble per published experiments
prior_art_notes: DSTAR is the most recent STAR-family member, published IEEE RA-L January 2026. Establishes very-recent (4-month-deep) open-academic prior art for: decoupled-FBEM wheel-leg reconfigurable robotics, sideways rolling via asymmetric mechanical configuration, COM-shifting via independent left/right leg actuation, 18-20 cm obstacle traversal in palm-sized class. Directly anticipates free-humanoid-centaur's wheel-leg hybrid mode-switching commitment, free-humanoid-wheeled's obstacle-climbing requirement, and any commercial humanoid claim on reconfigurable wheel-leg architectures (including any mid-size extrapolation of DSTAR to humanoid scale). The full STAR family lineage (Berkeley original 2013 → Zarrouk RSTAR 2019 → AmphiSTAR 2023 → DSTAR 2026) provides 13-year-deep open-academic continuous publication coverage of every architectural element. Highly relevant for shoal dock-A wetland service: DSTAR's terrain-adaptation gait library is a published reference design for centaur-class wetland mode-transition.
sensing: onboard camera (Raspberry Pi camera module); IMU implied for tilt control; minimal external sensing
sources: Siboni, T., Coronel, M., Zarrouk, D. IEEE RA-L 11(1) January 2026, pp. 882-889. DOI 10.1109/LRA.2025.3634888.
Ben-Gurion University Bio-inspired and Medical Robotics Lab (bgu.ac.il/zarrouklab).
Supplementary video material via IEEE Xplore.

actuator_details: Visual-inertial SLAM library. ORB feature extraction + bag-of-words place recognition + bundle adjustment over keyframes. Supports monocular, stereo, RGB-D, and visual-inertial sensor configurations. Multi-map operation with map-merging. Real-time on commodity CPU.
control_architecture: Provides SLAM substrate for any robotic platform with a camera. C++ library; ROS 1/2 integration.
creator: University of Zaragoza I3A; Carlos Campos, Juan Tardós et al.
disclosure_citation: Campos, C., Elvira, R., Rodríguez, J. J. G., Montiel, J. M. M., Tardós, J. D. 'ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial, and Multimap SLAM'. IEEE Transactions on Robotics 37(6) December 2021, pp. 1874-1890. arXiv:2007.11898. GPLv3 source: github.com/UZ-SLAMLab/ORB_SLAM3. University of Zaragoza.
notable_capabilities: the canonical visual-inertial SLAM baseline since 2021
deployed in countless academic + commercial robotic systems
prior_art_notes: ORB-SLAM3 is the canonical academic visual-inertial SLAM library and 5-year-deep open-source baseline. Heavily-cited (>3000 citations). Anticipates: (1) monocular/stereo/RGB-D + IMU fusion in a unified factor-graph framework, (2) multi-map operation across sessions for long-term autonomy, (3) bag-of-words place recognition for loop closure. Establishes the geometric-only SLAM baseline that semantic/open-vocab SLAM systems (including RADIO-ViPE, round-10 entry) extend. Any humanoid platform claim on visual-inertial SLAM faces this lineage.

actuator_details: End-to-end differentiable visual SLAM. Dense bundle adjustment over all pixels (vs. ORB-SLAM's sparse keypoint approach). Recurrent iterative optical-flow updates produce dense correspondences and depth. GPU-accelerated. Significantly more robust to texture-poor scenes and dynamic content than ORB-SLAM3.
control_architecture: Visual SLAM substrate. PyTorch implementation; supports monocular/stereo/RGB-D inputs.
creator: Princeton Vision and Learning Lab; Zachary Teed, Jia Deng
disclosure_citation: Teed, Z., Deng, J. 'DROID-SLAM: Deep Visual SLAM for Monocular, Stereo, and RGB-D Cameras'. NeurIPS 2021. arXiv:2108.10869. BSD-3-Clause source: github.com/princeton-vl/DROID-SLAM. Princeton Vision and Learning Lab.
notable_capabilities: robust to texture-poor and dynamic scenes
the foundation for ViPE and downstream semantic SLAM systems
prior_art_notes: DROID-SLAM is the canonical dense differentiable-visual-SLAM academic system (NeurIPS 2021, BSD-3 open source). 4-year-deep prior art anticipating any humanoid claim on dense / differentiable / foundation-model-grounded visual SLAM. Immediate ancestor of ViPE (Princeton 2024-2025) and RADIO-ViPE (ITMO 2026 — round-10 entry). Together with ORB-SLAM3, establishes the academic SLAM baseline against which all modern humanoid perception claims must be evaluated.
sources: Predecessor: RAFT (Teed/Deng ECCV 2020) for optical flow.

actuator_details: Online semantic SLAM system. Calibration-free monocular RGB input — no prior camera intrinsics, no depth, no pose initialization required. Tightly couples multi-modal embeddings (RADIO agglomerative foundation model + SigLIP text encoder) with geometric scene information in a joint factor-graph optimization with adaptive robust kernels. Operates online at 8-10 FPS. State-of-the-art on TUM-RGBD dynamic benchmark (ATE 1.63 cm average vs. ViPE 2.17 / Dyna-SLAM 2.00).
aliases: Reduce All Domains Into One Video Pose Engine
control_architecture: Provides perception substrate for any robot with a camera. Outputs: calibrated camera poses, dense depth maps, dense PCA-compressed RADIO embeddings per pixel. Supports free-form natural-language object queries via SigLIP text-embedding matching against the dense map. Three-regime Barron-loss adaptive robust kernel jointly suppresses actively-moving agents and quasi-static displaced objects.
creator: ITMO University BE2R Lab; Nasser, Iumanov, Li, Popov, Mahmoud, Kolyubin
disclosure_citation: Nasser, Z., Iumanov, M., Li, T., Popov, M., Mahmoud, J., Kolyubin, S. 'RADIO-ViPE: Online Tightly Coupled Multi-Modal Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Semantic SLAM in Dynamic Environments'. arXiv:2604.26067v1, April 28, 2026. ITMO University, Biomechatronics and Energy-Efficient Robotics (BE2R) Lab, Saint Petersburg, Russia.
notable_capabilities: calibration-free (no camera intrinsics, no depth, no pose required)
SOTA on TUM-RGBD dynamic benchmark (ATE 1.63 cm)
prior_art_notes: RADIO-ViPE is the most recent and architecturally complete online open-vocabulary semantic SLAM system. April 2026 arXiv preprint; 9 days before this corpus entry. Establishes very-recent (sub-1-week) open-academic prior art for: calibration-free monocular semantic SLAM, tightly-coupled multi-modal fusion (RADIO + SigLIP + geometric BA), adaptive-kernel dynamic-scene robustness, online operation at 8-10 FPS. Directly shields any commercial humanoid claim on: 'onboard semantic scene understanding from monocular video' (Tesla Optimus, Figure 02, 1X NEO, Apptronik Apollo, etc. all face this), 'language-grounded robotic perception in dynamic environments', 'calibration-free humanoid camera deployment'. The TUM-RGBD ATE comparison table in Table II of the paper enumerates the prior art — RADIO-ViPE outperforms Dyna-SLAM, DLD-SLAM, V3D-SLAM, DGS-SLAM, RoDyn-SLAM, DynaMON, ViPE — every one of which is itself open-academic prior art for humanoid perception. Lineage: ORB-SLAM3 (geometric baseline) → DROID-SLAM (dense differentiable) → ViPE (Princeton in-the-wild metric depth) → RADIO-ViPE (ITMO open-vocab + calibration-free).
sensing: single uncalibrated monocular RGB camera (the entire input); produces depth + pose + dense semantic embeddings as output
sources: Foundation models: NVIDIA RADIO (Ranzinger et al. 2024), SigLIP (Zhai et al. ICCV 2023).

actuator_details: Mid-scale humanoid (~1.4 m, ~30 kg target class). In-house-built lightweight design optimized for learning-based control: low simulation complexity, anthropomorphic kinematics, and reliability against falls. Quasi-direct-drive actuators in legs and arms. Specific motor/reducer selection in the public arXiv paper.
control_architecture: Reinforcement-learning locomotion controller trained in simulation with light domain randomization; deployed zero-shot to hardware. Demonstrates narrow sim-to-real gap and robust locomotion across outdoor terrains. The platform is explicitly designed as a research substrate for learning-based control rather than a closed product.
creator: UC Berkeley Hybrid Robotics Lab; Liao, Zhang, X. Huang, X. Huang, Li, Sreenath
disclosure_citation: Liao, Q., Zhang, B., Huang, X., Huang, X., Li, Z., Sreenath, K. 'Berkeley Humanoid: A Research Platform for Learning-based Control'. arXiv:2407.21781, July 2024. IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA) 2025. UC Berkeley Hybrid Robotics Lab.
notable_capabilities: outdoor robust bipedal locomotion (hundreds of meters)

Modular gearbox replaceable per finger / joint. The design explicitly trades absolute durability for reproducibility and democratization.
control_architecture: RL-trained locomotion controller; zero-shot sim-to-real demonstrated. Hardware design + embedded code + training/deployment frameworks all fully open-source. Designed for researchers, students, and tech newbies — explicitly democratization-oriented.

actuator_details: Compact (~0.56 m, 3.4 kg) anthropomorphic humanoid with 30 active DoF (excluding end effectors). Commercially available off-the-shelf motors; entirely 3D-printed. Total BOM under $6,000. Plug-and-play zero-point calibration and transferable motor system identification for sim-to-real.
control_architecture: Designed as ML-compatible substrate. High-fidelity digital twin via system-ID; demonstrated zero-shot sim-to-real policy transfer for both locomotion and manipulation. Loco-manipulation tasks in the demonstration set.

Establishes 1-year-deep open-academic prior art for: integrated loco-manipulation policy training on an open humanoid platform, transferable motor system-ID for sim-to-real without hand-tuning, 30-DoF anthropomorphic full-body at sub-$6k. actuator_details: Online video pose engine: from raw uncalibrated video, estimates camera intrinsics, camera motion (poses), and dense near-metric depth maps. Supports pinhole, wide-angle, and 360° panoramic camera models. Solves a dense bundle adjustment with multi-constraint loss. Runs at 3-5 FPS on a single GPU. Outperforms MegaSAM and prior uncalibrated baselines by 18% / 50% on TUM / KITTI benchmarks.
control_architecture: Provides perception substrate (intrinsics + extrinsics + dense depth) for any robotic platform with monocular video. Released with a 96M-frame dataset of paired video + camera-pose + dense-depth annotations across internet videos, AI-generated videos, and panoramas — the largest such open dataset to date.
creator: NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab (nv-tlabs); multi-author
disclosure_citation: Huang, J., et al. (NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab + collaborators). 'ViPE: Video Pose Engine for 3D Geometric Perception'. arXiv:2508.10934, August 2025. Open-source release via nv-tlabs/vipe.
notable_capabilities: calibration-free metric depth and pose from unconstrained video
support for pinhole, wide-angle, and 360° cameras
3-5 FPS online operation on single GPU
18% / 50% improvement over MegaSAM on TUM / KITTI
prior_art_notes: ViPE is NVIDIA Toronto AI Lab's canonical Video Pose Engine, August 2025 arXiv. Sits **directly between DROID-SLAM (2021) and RADIO-ViPE (2026)** in the visual-SLAM lineage: it is RADIO-ViPE's explicit foundation per the round-10 paper's text ('we build upon ViPE [5]'). 9-month-deep open-permissive academic prior art for: calibration-free metric depth from uncalibrated video, dense bundle adjustment over heterogeneous camera models, online video pose estimation at 3-5 FPS. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on uncalibrated-camera onboard 3D perception. Plus the 96M-frame released dataset is itself prior art for any humanoid-vision data-curation IP.
sensing: single uncalibrated monocular RGB camera (input); produces metric depth + 6-DoF camera pose + intrinsics (output)

actuator_details: Monocular Gaussian-splatting SLAM specifically engineered for dynamic-scene robustness. Tracks camera trajectory and reconstructs a 3D Gaussian map of the static environment from monocular video, even with dynamic distractors (people, moving objects). Renders high-fidelity novel views of the static scene from the trained Gaussian field.
control_architecture: Provides SLAM substrate. Open-source release.

disclosure_citation: Zheng, J., Zhu, Z., Bieri, V., Pollefeys, M., Peng, S., Armeni, I. 'WildGS-SLAM: Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic Environments'. CVPR 2025. arXiv:2504.03886. ETH Zürich + Stanford GradientSpaces.
notable_capabilities: dynamic-scene robust (people + moving objects do not corrupt map)
Gaussian-splatting reconstruction with photorealistic novel views
prior_art_notes: WildGS-SLAM is the canonical CVPR 2025 monocular dynamic-scene Gaussian-splatting SLAM system from ETH + Stanford. Establishes 1-year-deep prior art for: monocular GS-SLAM with dynamic-scene robustness, photorealistic novel-view rendering of static background while filtering dynamic foreground. Among the systems RADIO-ViPE benchmarks against (TUM-RGBD dynamic). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on monocular dynamic-scene mapping with photorealistic reconstruction.

actuator_details: Real-time whole-body model-predictive controller using MuJoCo dynamics directly. Iterative LQR (iLQR) optimization with finite-difference approximation of dynamics derivatives — no analytical model required. Achieves real-time on hardware for: dynamic quadruped locomotion, quadruped walking on two legs, and full-sized humanoid bipedal locomotion.
control_architecture: Whole-body MPC substrate via MuJoCo. Open-source release on github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco_mpc.
creator: Google DeepMind; Howell, Lutter, Tassa et al.

notable_capabilities: real-time whole-body MPC at humanoid scale
demonstrated on quadruped and full-sized humanoid hardware
direct extension of the Tassa iLQG (2012) lineage
prior_art_notes: Howell-Tassa MuJoCo MPC is the direct 2025 successor to the Tassa iLQG 2012 entry already in the corpus. 14-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: real-time whole-body humanoid MPC using MuJoCo dynamics + finite-difference iLQR. Demonstrated on full-sized humanoid hardware, which closes the simulation-to-real gap that the 2012 Tassa work left open. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on real-time whole-body trajectory optimization.

actuator_details: Five-finger 3D-printed anthropomorphic hand. **Antagonistic-tendon mechanism** — agonist + antagonist tendon pairs allow active opening AND closing (classic SoftHand only actively closes; passive return). Two-layer palm design with separate routing for agonist vs. antagonist tendons. Two differential mechanisms enable distinct joint control modes: enclosing grasp vs. fingertip grasp.
control_architecture: Highly underactuated — synergy-driven from a small number of motors (specific count in paper). Tactile feedback via integrated vision-based tactile sensors at fingertips. Dual-tendon active control allows specific joint targeting (DIP vs. PIP).
creator: Bristol Robotics Laboratory (Lepora group) + Pisa-IIT (Bianchi, Catalano)
disclosure_citation: Li, H., Ford, C. J., Lu, C., Lin, Y., Bianchi, M., Catalano, M. G., Psomopoulou, E., Lepora, N. F. International Journal of Robotics Research, October 2025. Bristol Robotics Laboratory + Pisa-IIT collaboration.
end_effector: five 3D-printed D-type fingers with active antagonism + integrated 3D-printed vision-based tactile sensors
notable_capabilities: antagonistic active open/close (vs. passive-return SoftHand classic)
prior_art_notes: Tactile SoftHand-A is the 2024-2025 direct successor to the Pisa-IIT SoftHand 2 (round-8 entry pisa-iit-softhand-2). Adds antagonistic tendon mechanism (active open + active close), integrated vision-based tactile sensing, and full 3D-printed fabrication. IJRR October 2025. Direct shielding for free-humanoid-platform's hand v0.1 commitments — Tactile SoftHand-A has antagonistic-tendon prior art that the v0.1 hand's passive-return spring approach explicitly is the alternative to. Together with shadow-dexterous-hand, pisa-iit-softhand, dlr-hand-arm-system-2011, and pisa-iit-softhand-2, establishes deep open-academic prior art for anthropomorphic underactuated tendon-driven hand robotics. **Particularly relevant for hand v0.2 design decisions** — the antagonistic-tendon path is well-anticipated open art.
sensing: integrated 3D-printed vision-based tactile sensors at each fingertip; tendon-state proprioception
sources: Li et al. International Journal of Robotics Research October 2025 (DOI: 10.1177/02783649251379516).

actuator_details: Wheel-legged hybrid robot with a distinctive front-leg configuration: **replaces conventional hip-roll DoF with hip-yaw DoFs on the front legs**, enabling efficient flat-surface movement while retaining complex-terrain adaptability. Mode-switching between legged and wheeled locomotion is the architectural focus.
control_architecture: Controllers for both legged and wheeled locomotion; seamless mode-transition.

Specific authorship and venue per the arXiv preprint.

actuator_details: Dense semantic Gaussian-splatting SLAM. Combines 3D-Gaussian-based scene representation with per-Gaussian semantic feature attachment. Robust camera tracking, accurate 3D semantic mapping, and high-quality novel-view rendering simultaneously.
control_architecture: Provides semantic SLAM substrate. Per-Gaussian semantic features enable closed-set semantic queries and 3D scene segmentation.

Predates and informs the open-vocabulary GS-SLAM lineage that WildGS-SLAM, LEG-SLAM, LEGO-SLAM, and RADIO-ViPE descend from.

actuator_details: Language-embedded Gaussian-splatting representation built incrementally by a mobile robot. Each Gaussian primitive carries a CLIP-aligned language feature enabling open-vocabulary scene queries. 3.5× faster training than LERF baseline. Demonstrated on a mobile manipulator (Stretch) building room-scale scene representations.
control_architecture: Provides language-grounded scene representation for downstream task-conditioned mobile manipulation.

incremental room-scale construction by mobile robot

Predates and informs LEG-SLAM, LEGO-SLAM, and any commercial humanoid claim on language-queryable 3D scene maps built onboard.

actuator_details: Real-time language-enhanced Gaussian-splatting SLAM. Fuses optimized Gaussian-splatting implementation with visual-language feature extraction via DINOv2 + learnable PCA-based feature compressor. Achieves 10+ fps on Replica dataset, 18 fps on ScanNet.

Distinct from but contemporary with LEGO-SLAM (Nov 2025). Both feed the open-vocab GS-SLAM lineage that RADIO-ViPE compares against.

actuator_details: First framework to achieve **real-time** open-vocabulary mapping within a 3DGS-based SLAM system. Scene-adaptive encoder-decoder distills high-dimensional language embeddings into a compact 16-dimensional per-Gaussian feature space. **Language-guided pruning** identifies semantic redundancy and reduces map Gaussian count by >60% while maintaining rendering quality.

disclosure_citation: Authors per arXiv 2511.16144. 'LEGO-SLAM: Language-Embedded Gaussian Optimization SLAM'. arXiv:2511.16144, November 2025. Lab of AI and Robotics.

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on real-time onboard open-vocabulary scene mapping. Together with LEG-SLAM, LEGS, and SemGauss-SLAM, the open-vocab GS-SLAM corpus is now ~6-month to 14-month deep across five contemporary systems — fully covering the architectural surface of RADIO-ViPE's competitor table.

actuator_details: Vision-language-action **flow model** for general robot control. Pretrained on diverse multi-robot demonstration data (mobile manipulation, bimanual, single-arm). Single foundation policy controls multiple robot embodiments. Action distribution modeled via flow matching (vs. diffusion or autoregressive). Significant step in unified-VLA-foundation-model lineage post RT-2 / OpenVLA.
control_architecture: Foundation-model policy: pretrained VLA + flow-matching action head + per-embodiment fine-tuning.
creator: Physical Intelligence; Black, Brown, Driess, Finn et al.
disclosure_citation: Black, K., Brown, N., Driess, D., Esmail, A., Equi, M., Finn, C., et al. 'π₀: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control'. arXiv:2410.24164, October 2024. Physical Intelligence (physicalintelligence.company).

notable_capabilities: open weights / open paper from Physical Intelligence
prior_art_notes: π₀ is Physical Intelligence's canonical first VLA foundation policy (Oct 2024). 1.5-year-deep open-academic publication. Establishes architectural prior art for: flow-matching action distribution in VLA, cross-embodiment policy pretraining, single foundation model controlling multiple robot platforms. Direct successor lineage from RT-1 (2022), RT-2 (2023), OpenVLA (2024). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on VLA-based control (Tesla Optimus, Figure, 1X NEO, Apptronik all face this); particularly for any claim on flow-matching action heads or cross-embodiment pretraining.

actuator_details: VLA model with **open-world generalization**. Co-trains on heterogeneous tasks: data from multiple robots, high-level semantic subtask prediction, web data, and other sources. Hybrid multi-modal examples combine image observations + language commands + object detections + semantic-subtask prediction + low-level actions. Demonstrates long-horizon (10-15 minute) dexterous manipulation in **entirely new homes** not present in training data — first VLA to convincingly demonstrate this.
control_architecture: Co-trained VLA foundation policy with mixed-modality training data; fine-tuned per-task or zero-shot to new homes for mobile manipulation.
creator: Physical Intelligence; Black et al.
disclosure_citation: Black, K., et al. 'π₀.₅: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization'. arXiv:2504.16054, April 2025. CoRL 2025 (PMLR vol. 305 pp. 17-40, Black25a). Physical Intelligence.
notable_capabilities: long-horizon dexterous tasks (10-15 minutes, kitchen/bedroom cleaning)
co-training on multi-robot + web + semantic-subtask data
successor to π₀ with measurable generalization improvement
prior_art_notes: π₀.₅ is Physical Intelligence's open-world VLA (CoRL 2025 oral). 1-year-deep prior art on: open-world (new-home) zero-shot mobile manipulation, co-training across multi-robot + web + semantic subtask data, long-horizon (10+ minute) household task autonomy. **The most direct prior art for any commercial humanoid claim on 'works in any home out-of-the-box'** — Tesla Optimus, Figure, 1X NEO, Apptronik all market this generalization claim and now face 1-year-deep open-academic anticipation. Lineage: RT-1 → RT-2 → OpenVLA → π₀ → π₀.₅.

actuator_details: First fully **open-source** vision-language-action foundation model (weights, code, data — all open-permissive). 7B-parameter VLA built on Llama-2 + DINOv2 + SigLIP visual backbones. Trained on the Open X-Embodiment dataset (970k+ trajectories across 22 robot embodiments). First open-weight competitor to Google's RT-2 (which was closed-weight).
control_architecture: Open-source VLA foundation policy: tokenized vision + language + action via Llama-2 LLM backbone; per-embodiment fine-tuning recipes published.
creator: Stanford + Toyota Research Institute + UC Berkeley; Kim, Pertsch, Karamcheti, Liang, Finn, Levine, Tedrake et al.

J., Pertsch, K., Karamcheti, S., Xiao, T., Balakrishna, A., Nair, S., Rafailov, R., Foster, E., Lam, G., Sanketi, P., Vuong, Q., Kollar, T., Burchfiel, B., Tedrake, R., Sadigh, D., Levine, S., Liang, P., Finn, C. prior_art_notes: OpenVLA is the canonical first fully-open-source VLA foundation model (CoRL 2024). 23-month-deep open-permissive academic prior art for: 7B-class open-weight VLA, Llama-2-based VLA backbone, Open-X-Embodiment-trained cross-embodiment policy. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid VLA claim on open-source-equivalent architectural elements. Together with π₀ and π₀.₅, establishes the open-academic VLA baseline against which all closed commercial VLAs (Tesla Optimus, Figure, 1X NEO) must be evaluated.

actuator_details: Optimized fine-tuning recipe for VLA models, applied to OpenVLA as base. Combines: (1) parallel decoding of action tokens, (2) action chunking, (3) continuous action representation (vs. discretized), (4) L1 regression-based learning objective. Improves OpenVLA average success on LIBERO from 76.5% → 97.1% and increases action throughput by 26×. Real-world bimanual ALOHA evaluations beat π₀ and RDT-1B fine-tuned defaults plus from-scratch Diffusion Policy and ACT by up to 15% absolute success rate.
control_architecture: Fine-tuning recipe for VLA foundation models. Publishes the speed × success Pareto improvement.
creator: Stanford; Moo Jin Kim, Chelsea Finn, Percy Liang
disclosure_citation: Kim, M. J., Finn, C., Liang, P. 'Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models: Optimizing Speed and Success'. arXiv:2502.19645, February 2025. Stanford.
notable_capabilities: 97.1% success on LIBERO (SOTA, vs. OpenVLA 76.5% baseline)
outperforms π₀ + RDT-1B + Diffusion Policy + ACT on bimanual ALOHA
prior_art_notes: OpenVLA-OFT is the canonical Optimized Fine-Tuning recipe for VLA models (Stanford, Feb 2025). 15-month-deep prior art on: parallel action decoding for VLA, action chunking + continuous action representation + L1 regression objective combination. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid VLA fine-tuning claim, particularly any claim on 'fast inference at high success' for humanoid VLAs. Outperforms π₀ on bimanual ALOHA — the canonical academic benchmark for bimanual humanoid manipulation.

actuator_details: Anthropomorphic robot hand built **entirely from LEGO MINDSTORMS** components and standard LEGO bricks. Tendon-driven highly-underactuated five-finger hand based on the Pisa-IIT SoftHand and Tactile SoftHand-A lineage. **Dual motors driving an agonist-antagonist tendon pair on each finger** for active fine control. Finger motions synchronized via **soft synergies implemented with a differential mechanism using clutch gears** (a LEGO-friendly approximation of the SoftHand's textile-elastic synergies). 90% of the grip force of a professional 3D-printed SoftHand. <1 second open-close cycle.
control_architecture: LEGO MINDSTORMS hub controls dual motors per finger via standard LEGO interfaces. Designed for educational replication — full open-source build instructions and CAD files at lepora.com/EduSoftHand-A. Programmable via standard MINDSTORMS environment.

disclosure_citation: Lepora, J., Li, H., Psomopoulou, E., Lepora, N. F. 'Educational SoftHand-A: Building an Anthropomorphic Hand with Soft Synergies using LEGO® MINDSTORMS®'. arXiv:2510.15638, October 2025. Bristol Robotics Laboratory + Bristol Grammar School.
end_effector: five LEGO-built fingers with antagonistic tendons; differential clutch-gear synergy
notable_capabilities: anthropomorphic 5-finger hand from LEGO MINDSTORMS only

Together with pisa-iit-softhand, pisa-iit-softhand-2, and tactile-softhand-a-2025, the SoftHand synergy-mechanism lineage is now 11-year-deep continuous open academic publication (2014-2025) across four design generations.

actuator_details: Open-source middleware for robotics. Publish-subscribe message-passing architecture, packaged build system, large set of community-contributed drivers and algorithm packages. Becomes the de facto integration substrate for academic and commercial robots through the 2010s.
control_architecture: Provides communication, build, and tooling substrate for arbitrary robotic systems. Per-platform drivers; perception/navigation/manipulation algorithm packages.
creator: Stanford AI Lab + Willow Garage; Quigley, Conley, Gerkey, Faust, Foote, Leibs, Wheeler, Ng

prior_art_notes: ROS is the canonical open-source robotics middleware (2007 internal, 2009 ICRA workshop publication). 17-year-deep BSD-3 / Apache-2.0 open-permissive prior art. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'modular driver-publishing-subscribing robotics middleware', message-passing inter-process communication for robots, or the standard tool-stack patterns it established (rosbag, rviz, tf, MoveIt).

actuator_details: Reimplementation of ROS atop DDS middleware. Supports real-time constraints, multi-machine cross-network communication, and embedded-class deployment that ROS 1 could not. Lifecycle-managed nodes, native security, deterministic execution. The substrate for modern academic + commercial robotics integration.
