creator: Open Robotics; multi-author community
disclosure_citation: Open Robotics. ROS 2 'Ardent Apalone' first stable release December 8, 2017. Architectural redesign of ROS atop DDS (Data Distribution Service) for real-time, multi-vehicle, and embedded use. Apache-2.0.
notable_capabilities: deployed on quadrupeds (ANYmal D, Spot), humanoids, AUVs, drones
prior_art_notes: ROS 2 is the modern academic + commercial robotics middleware (2017+). 8-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: real-time DDS-based robotics middleware, lifecycle-managed component architectures for multi-robot systems, QoS-aware inter-vehicle messaging. All four free-humanoid-family morphologies (platform/wheeled/centaur/submersible) commit to ROS 2 as the integration substrate, shielded by this entry.
sources: Macenski, S., Foote, T., Gerkey, B., Lalancette, C., Woodall, W. 'Robot Operating System 2: Design, architecture, and uses in the wild'. Science Robotics 7(66) 2022.

actuator_details: Physics simulation engine optimized for model-based control: stable contact dynamics, fast forward + inverse dynamics, smooth analytical derivatives. Designed expressly for the iLQG / MPC use case (Tassa iLQG 2012 entry uses MuJoCo). The dominant academic simulator for humanoid and manipulator policy training since the mid-2010s.
control_architecture: Provides simulation substrate for arbitrary control architectures. Standard MJCF model format; Python (mujoco) and C bindings.
creator: Emo Todorov, Tom Erez, Yuval Tassa (originally University of Washington / Roboti LLC; now Google DeepMind)
disclosure_citation: Todorov, E., Erez, T., Tassa, Y. 'MuJoCo: A physics engine for model-based control'. IROS 2012. Originally proprietary (Roboti LLC); acquired by Google DeepMind October 2021 and released under Apache-2.0.
notable_capabilities: MJCF model format (which OpenLoco compiles to)
the substrate for thousands of robotics RL/MPC papers
prior_art_notes: MuJoCo is the canonical academic physics engine for model-based robotic control (Todorov-Erez-Tassa 2012). 13-year-deep prior art spanning the proprietary Roboti era (2012-2021) and the open-source DeepMind era (2021+). The substrate that the Tassa iLQG entry, Howell-Tassa MuJoCo MPC entry, MJX entry, and Genesis simulator entry all build on or interop with. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on contact-rich policy training simulation. MJCF is the format OpenLoco compiles to, so MuJoCo is the reference simulator for the entire free-humanoid-family.
sensing: simulated cameras, IMUs, joint sensors, force/torque

actuator_details: Model-based design + verification toolkit for robotics. Multibody dynamics + collision + contact + linear/nonlinear systems theory + MPC + LCP/QP solvers in a unified C++/Python framework. Strong emphasis on formal verification and deterministic semantics — the feature distinguishing Drake from MuJoCo. Used at MIT, TRI, Boston Dynamics, and across academia.
control_architecture: Multibody dynamics + systems framework + optimization-based control toolkit. Provides MPC / TVLQR / QP-based whole-body control templates.
creator: MIT CSAIL Robot Locomotion Group + Toyota Research Institute; Russ Tedrake et al.
disclosure_citation: Tedrake, R., the Drake Development Team. 'Drake: Model-Based Design and Verification for Robotics'. drake.mit.edu, project active since ~2010 with formal v1.0 in January 2019. BSD-3-Clause source: github.com/RobotLocomotion/drake. MIT CSAIL + Toyota Research Institute.
notable_capabilities: Tedrake's MIT 6.832 underactuated robotics course substrate
prior_art_notes: Drake is the canonical MIT/TRI model-based design + verification toolkit for robotics (Tedrake et al., active since ~2010, v1.0 Jan 2019). 6-year-deep formal-release prior art, 15-year-deep project. Distinct from MuJoCo by emphasis on deterministic verifiable semantics (relevant for safety-critical / certification use cases). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on verifiable model-based control or whole-body QP/MPC architectures. Free-humanoid-platform/wheeled/centaur/submersible all reference Drake as a tertiary simulator option for whole-body MPC validation.

actuator_details: GPU-parallelized physics simulator for robotic RL. End-to-end GPU pipeline: simulation, observation extraction, neural network inference, policy update — no CPU round-trip. Enables thousands of parallel environment instances on a single GPU. The substrate for ANYmal sim-to-real perceptive locomotion (Hwangbo 2019 → Lee 2020 → Miki 2022 lineage).
control_architecture: GPU-batched physics + RL training pipeline. PyTorch / JAX integration.
creator: NVIDIA + ETH Zürich Robotic Systems Lab; Makoviychuk et al.
disclosure_citation: Makoviychuk, V., Wawrzyniak, L., Guo, Y., Lu, M., Storey, K., Macklin, M., Hoeller, D., Rudin, N., Allshire, A., Handa, A., State, G. 'Isaac Gym: High-Performance GPU-Based Physics Simulation For Robot Learning'. NeurIPS 2021 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks. arXiv:2108.10470.
notable_capabilities: thousands of parallel environments per GPU
prior_art_notes: Isaac Gym is the canonical first-generation NVIDIA GPU-parallelized robotic RL simulator (NeurIPS 2021). 4-year-deep open-permissive prior art. Direct ancestor of Isaac Lab (round-8 entry nvidia-isaac-lab-2024) and the substrate for the canonical sim-to-real ANYmal perceptive-locomotion papers. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on GPU-parallelized RL training; particularly the thousands-of-parallel-envs scaling that commercial humanoid vendors cite as proprietary.

actuator_details: Vision foundation model trained by **agglomerative multi-teacher distillation** from CLIP, DINOv2, and SAM. Single backbone inheriting all three teacher capabilities: zero-shot vision-language, dense pixel-level features, open-vocabulary segmentation. Released across multiple sizes (RADIO-B/L/H). Used as the perception substrate for RADIO-ViPE (round-10 entry) and other downstream robotics systems.
control_architecture: Provides dense per-pixel multi-modal embeddings consumable by downstream perception, SLAM, manipulation, or VLA pipelines.
creator: NVIDIA Learning and Perception Research; Ranzinger, Heinrich, Kautz, Molchanov
disclosure_citation: Ranzinger, M., Heinrich, G., Kautz, J., Molchanov, P. 'AM-RADIO: Agglomerative Vision Foundation Model -- Reduce All Domains Into One'. arXiv:2312.06709, December 2023. CVPR 2024. NVIDIA Learning and Perception Research. RADIOv2.5 follow-up: arXiv:2412.07679 December 2024.
notable_capabilities: single-pass inference (no multi-model ensemble at deployment)
outperforms individual teachers on combined evaluations
prior_art_notes: AM-RADIO is the canonical agglomerative-distillation vision foundation model (NVIDIA, CVPR 2024). 1.5-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: multi-teacher vision-foundation distillation, single-backbone CLIP+DINOv2+SAM amalgamation. **The literal embedding substrate of RADIO-ViPE** — the round-10 RADIO-ViPE entry's name comes from this. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on multi-modal vision-foundation backbones for onboard perception.
sources: Ranzinger et al. arXiv:2312.06709 December 2023; CVPR 2024.
Heinrich et al. RADIOv2.5 arXiv:2412.07679 December 2024.

actuator_details: Vision-language contrastive model trained with **sigmoid loss** (rather than CLIP's softmax loss). Enables much larger batch sizes without quadratic memory cost, leading to faster training and stronger zero-shot performance. The default vision-language encoder for many modern VLAs (e.g., OpenVLA uses SigLIP + DINOv2).
control_architecture: Provides aligned vision + text embeddings for downstream open-vocabulary perception, retrieval, and policy conditioning.
creator: Google Research; Zhai, Mustafa, Kolesnikov, Beyer
disclosure_citation: Zhai, X., Mustafa, B., Kolesnikov, A., Beyer, L. 'Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training'. arXiv:2303.15343, March 2023. ICCV 2023. Google Research.
notable_capabilities: sigmoid loss enables large-batch contrastive training
faster training than CLIP at equivalent quality
open weights via HuggingFace google/siglip-* family
the standard text-encoder for VLA / VLM systems
prior_art_notes: SigLIP is the canonical sigmoid-loss vision-language foundation model (Google ICCV 2023). 2-year-deep prior art for: sigmoid-loss contrastive vision-language training, large-batch-friendly training regime. The text-encoder backbone in OpenVLA, RADIO-ViPE, and many VLA systems. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on open-vocabulary text-image alignment for instruction following.
sources: Zhai et al. arXiv:2303.15343 March 2023; ICCV 2023.

actuator_details: Self-supervised vision foundation model. Trained on 142M curated images via image-level + patch-level self-distillation losses. Produces high-quality dense per-pixel features without supervision. ViT backbone in S/B/L/g sizes. The standard self-supervised vision encoder for modern robotic perception.
control_architecture: Provides dense per-pixel features for downstream perception (segmentation, depth, monocular depth via DPT heads, embedding-based SLAM).
creator: Meta AI Research (FAIR); Oquab, Darcet, Moutakanni et al.
disclosure_citation: Oquab, M., Darcet, T., Moutakanni, T., Vo, H., Szafraniec, M., Khalidov, V., Fernandez, P., Haziza, D., Massa, F., El-Nouby, A., et al. 'DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision'. arXiv:2304.07193, April 2023. Meta AI Research (FAIR). Apache-2.0 release.
notable_capabilities: backbone in OpenVLA, LEG-SLAM, many other systems
prior_art_notes: DINOv2 is the canonical Meta self-supervised vision foundation model (April 2023). 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: self-supervised dense visual features at scale, ViT-g-class image encoders for robotics. The vision encoder in OpenVLA, LEG-SLAM, and many other systems in the corpus. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on self-supervised onboard visual feature learning.

actuator_details: Open-weight large language model family from Meta. 7B / 13B / 70B parameter sizes. **First open-weight LLM at GPT-3.5-class capability**, released under a permissive (though not strictly OSI-open) custom license. The language-model backbone of OpenVLA (round-12 entry) and many other VLA systems.
control_architecture: Provides language understanding + generation substrate for downstream agents, VLAs, and instruction-following policies.
creator: Meta AI; Touvron, Martin, Stone, et al.
disclosure_citation: Touvron, H., Martin, L., Stone, K., et al. 'Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models'. arXiv:2307.09288, July 2023. Meta AI.
prior_art_notes: LLaMA 2 is Meta's canonical open-weight LLM (July 2023). 2-year-deep open-permissive prior art for: 7B-70B-class open-weight language models. The language backbone of OpenVLA — directly anchors the LLM-grounded VLA architectural pattern. Shields any commercial humanoid claim on LLM-grounded instruction following where Llama-class open weights are an architectural alternative.

actuator_details: Dynamic-scene visual SLAM built atop ORB-SLAM2. Detects moving objects via multi-view geometry + Mask R-CNN deep learning, then **inpaints the static background** that was occluded by dynamic objects. Produces a static-only map suitable for long-term applications. The canonical foundational dynamic SLAM system.
control_architecture: Provides dynamic-scene SLAM substrate. Builds atop ORB-SLAM2.
creator: University of Zaragoza I3A; Bescos, Fácil, Civera, Neira
disclosure_citation: Bescos, B., Fácil, J. M., Civera, J., Neira, J. 'DynaSLAM: Tracking, Mapping and Inpainting in Dynamic Scenes'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 3(4) 2018; IROS 2018. arXiv:1806.05620. Universidad de Zaragoza I3A. GPLv3 source: github.com/BertaBescos/DynaSLAM.
notable_capabilities: dynamic-object detection via multi-view geometry + Mask R-CNN
background inpainting for static map construction
outperforms ORB-SLAM2 baselines on dynamic TUM-RGBD sequences
the foundational reference for dynamic-scene visual SLAM
prior_art_notes: DynaSLAM is the canonical foundational dynamic-scene visual SLAM system (Bescos et al. RA-L + IROS 2018). 7-year-deep open-copyleft prior art. Anchor of the dynamic-SLAM lineage that the entire RADIO-ViPE Table II benchmarks against (DLD-SLAM, V3D-SLAM, DGS-SLAM, RoDyn-SLAM, DynaMON are all DynaSLAM descendants). Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'SLAM that works in dynamic environments with moving people'.
sources: Bescos et al. arXiv:1806.05620 June 2018; RA-L + IROS 2018.

actuator_details: Camera tracking + depth estimation pipeline for in-the-wild monocular videos with dynamic content. Differentiable bundle adjustment layer iteratively updates scene geometry + camera parameters. Integrates monocular depth priors into training and inference. Uncertainty-aware global BA. The closest predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE — RADIO-ViPE / ViPE explicitly cite MegaSaM as the prior baseline.
control_architecture: Provides camera-pose + depth substrate for downstream applications.
creator: Google DeepMind + UC Berkeley + U. Michigan (per arXiv 2412.04463)
disclosure_citation: Authors per arXiv 2412.04463. 'MegaSaM: Accurate, Fast, and Robust Structure and Motion from Casual Dynamic Videos'. arXiv:2412.04463, December 2024. Google DeepMind + UC Berkeley + University of Michigan.
notable_capabilities: robust to dynamic content in casual videos
the closest predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE
notes: DRAFT: full author list should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: MegaSaM (Dec 2024) is the immediate predecessor to NVIDIA ViPE in the calibration-free dynamic-monocular-video pose+depth lineage. 5-month-deep prior art for: differentiable BA with monocular depth priors + uncertainty-aware global BA on in-the-wild dynamic videos. ViPE explicitly outperforms MegaSaM in its results table; that comparison only exists if MegaSaM is the prior art baseline. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on calibration-free in-the-wild video perception.

actuator_details: First system to embed CLIP language features into a NeRF radiance field, enabling open-vocabulary 3D scene queries. The architectural ancestor of LEGS (Berkeley AUTOLab IROS 2024) and the entire language-embedded-Gaussian-splatting lineage that followed. ICCV 2023 Oral. CC-BY 4.0 / open-source.
control_architecture: Provides language-grounded 3D scene representation.
creator: UC Berkeley AUTOLab + BAIR; Kerr, Kim, Goldberg, Kanazawa, Tancik
disclosure_citation: Kerr, J., Kim, C. M., Goldberg, K., Kanazawa, A., Tancik, M. 'LERF: Language Embedded Radiance Fields'. arXiv:2303.09553, March 2023. ICCV 2023 (Oral). UC Berkeley AUTOLab + Berkeley AI Research.
notable_capabilities: open-vocabulary 3D scene queries via natural-language text
the architectural ancestor of LEGS, LEG-SLAM, LEGO-SLAM
prior_art_notes: LERF is the canonical first language-embedded NeRF (Berkeley + BAIR, ICCV 2023 Oral). 2-year-deep prior art for: CLIP-embedded 3D radiance fields, open-vocabulary natural-language 3D scene queries. The architectural ancestor of LEGS (round-12), LEG-SLAM (round-12), LEGO-SLAM (round-12), and any commercial claim on language-queryable 3D scene representations. Predates the Gaussian-splatting instantiations and establishes the architectural pattern.
sources: Kerr et al. arXiv:2303.09553 March 2023; ICCV 2023.

actuator_details: 1.2-billion-parameter diffusion-based VLA foundation model for **bimanual manipulation**. Pre-trained on the largest multi-robot demonstration corpus to date and fine-tuned on a 6K+ episode bimanual dataset. Uses diffusion model formulation (vs. flow-matching π₀ or autoregressive RT-2/OpenVLA) for action distribution.
control_architecture: Diffusion VLA foundation policy. Open-weight via HuggingFace robotics-diffusion-transformer/rdt-1b. Apache-2.0 / similar open license.
creator: Tsinghua TSAIL (THU-ML); Songming Liu et al.
disclosure_citation: Liu, S., et al. 'RDT-1B: a Diffusion Foundation Model for Bimanual Manipulation'. arXiv:2410.07864, October 2024. ICLR 2025. Tsinghua TSAIL (THU-ML) lab.
notable_capabilities: 1.2B parameters — largest diffusion-based robot foundation model
zero-shot generalization to unseen objects + scenes
prior_art_notes: RDT-1B is THU-ML's canonical diffusion-based VLA foundation model for bimanual manipulation (ICLR 2025). 7-month-deep open-permissive prior art for: diffusion-formulation VLA at billion-parameter scale, bimanual manipulation foundation policy, multi-robot pre-training corpus. The canonical Chinese-academy entry in the open-weight VLA race alongside Stanford OpenVLA and Physical Intelligence π₀. Directly cited as a comparison baseline in OpenVLA-OFT (round-12); now resolves correctly. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on diffusion-based bimanual VLA.

actuator_details: Gaussian-splatting SLAM in dynamic environments. Claimed as the first dynamic SLAM framework built on the foundation of 3D Gaussian Splatting. Distinct from DG-SLAM (Fudan, NeurIPS 2024) — same period, similar architectural ambition, different team.
control_architecture: GS-SLAM substrate with dynamic-object handling.
creator: Mangyu Kong, Jaewon Lee, Seongwon Lee, Euntai Kim (per arXiv 2411.10722)
disclosure_citation: Kong, M., Lee, J., Lee, S., Kim, E. 'DGS-SLAM: Gaussian Splatting SLAM in Dynamic Environment'. arXiv:2411.10722, November 2024.
notes: DRAFT: full venue/published-date should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: DGS-SLAM (Kong et al. arXiv 2411.10722, November 2024). 6-month-deep prior art on dynamic-aware Gaussian-splatting SLAM. Cited as a competitor in the RADIO-ViPE Table II TUM-RGBD ATE benchmark; the round-10 RADIO-ViPE entry's claim of SOTA is anchored by comparison against this and several sibling systems. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on dynamic-scene GS-SLAM.

actuator_details: Robust dynamic dense RGB-D SLAM built on Neural Radiance Fields. Operates in the dynamic-environment regime alongside the dynamic-GS-SLAM lineage; uses NeRF rather than 3DGS for the radiance representation. IEEE RAL 2024.
control_architecture: NeRF-based dynamic SLAM substrate. Open-source.
creator: Fudan University ZVG; Haochen Jiang, Yueming Xu, Kejie Li, Jianfeng Feng, Li Zhang
disclosure_citation: Jiang, H., Xu, Y., Li, K., Feng, J., Zhang, L. 'RoDyn-SLAM: Robust Dynamic Dense RGB-D SLAM with Neural Radiance Fields'. IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters 2024. arXiv:2407.01303 July 2024. Fudan University ZVG (Zhang Vision Group).
notable_capabilities: robust to moving objects in indoor scenes
prior_art_notes: RoDyn-SLAM is Fudan ZVG's NeRF-based dynamic-scene SLAM (IEEE RAL 2024). 10-month-deep prior art on the NeRF branch of dynamic SLAM (distinct from the GS-based lineage of WildGS-SLAM, DGS-SLAM, DG-SLAM, etc.). Cited as a competitor in RADIO-ViPE Table II — the TUM-RGBD ATE benchmark RADIO-ViPE compares against. Together with DGS-SLAM, DG-SLAM, WildGS-SLAM, and DynaSLAM, establishes the academic dynamic-SLAM substrate that RADIO-ViPE measures itself against.
sources: Jiang et al. IEEE RAL 2024; arXiv:2407.01303 July 2024.

actuator_details: Sprawl-tuned reconfigurable robot extended with an **active two-link tail**. The tail allows the robot to run upright or inverted (orientation-flip resilience). Distinct from RSTAR (extension via body) and DSTAR (decoupled FBEM); TSTAR's distinguishing mechanism is the active tail.
control_architecture: Multi-DoF reconfiguration with active tail control. Mode-switching: upright run, inverted run, orientation flip via tail.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; David Zarrouk group
disclosure_citation: Zarrouk, D., et al. 'TSTAR: a reconfigurable robot with active two-link tail and sprawling mechanism, capable of running upright or inverted'. Ben-Gurion University, Bio-inspired and Medical Robotics Lab. ICRA / RA-L 2018-2019.
end_effector: four/six wheels or whegs + active tail end-effector
notable_capabilities: active 2-link tail (architectural innovation vs. STAR baseline)
notes: DRAFT: exact venue and date should be verified before promotion to commons-grade. The TSTAR paper is part of the Zarrouk lab's STAR-family publication stream 2017-2019.
prior_art_notes: TSTAR (Ben-Gurion Zarrouk lab, ~2018) extends the STAR family with an active two-link tail for orientation-flip resilience. ~7-year-deep open-academic prior art for the active-tail-on-wheel-leg-hybrid pattern. Cited in star-fearing-2013's prior_art_notes; round-14 backfill closes the citation chain.
sources: IEEE Spectrum 'Sprawling Wheel Leg Robot Crawls and Climbs' coverage.

actuator_details: **Hybrid flying-quadcopter and ground-running** robot. Same motors drive 4 propellers (flight) and 4 wheels/whegs (ground). 2.6 m/s ground speed; standard quadcopter flight regime. Sprawl-tuned ground stance. The first STAR-family member to add aerial DoF.
control_architecture: Mode-switching: ground-run vs. quadcopter-flight, same actuator pool.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; David Zarrouk group
disclosure_citation: Zarrouk, D., et al. 'Flying STAR (FSTAR): a hybrid flying-and-running quadcopter with sprawl-tuned mechanism'. Ben-Gurion University, ICRA 2019 era.
notable_capabilities: single actuator pool drives both ground and air locomotion
STAR-family + LEONARDO architectural cousin (LEONARDO is bipedal+thrust; FSTAR is quadruped+thrust)
notes: DRAFT: exact venue and date should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: FSTAR (Ben-Gurion Zarrouk lab, ~2019) is the first hybrid flying + ground-running STAR-family member. 6-year-deep open-academic prior art for: shared-motor-pool hybrid aerial-ground locomotion, sprawl-tuned wheel-leg + propeller integration. Architectural cousin of Caltech LEONARDO (round-8/round-12 entry caltech-leonardo-2021): FSTAR is quadruped+thrust, LEONARDO is bipedal+thrust. Together they establish the hybrid-locomotion academic substrate.

actuator_details: Successor to FSTAR adding **wall-climbing via thrust reversal**. Propellers can produce reversed thrust; combined with 4-wheel drive, the robot drives over steep slopes including walls. Penetrates 25 cm diameter pipes. Ground speed up to 4.5 m/s. The most architecturally extreme STAR-family member to date.
control_architecture: Mode-switching: ground / wall-climbing / pipe-traversal / flight, with shared actuator pool.
creator: Ben-Gurion University; David Zarrouk group
disclosure_citation: Zarrouk, D., et al. 'FCSTAR: Design and Analysis of a Hybrid Flying and Climbing Sprawl-Tuned Robot'. ResearchGate publication 353205537, July 2021. Ben-Gurion University. Builds on FSTAR with thrust-reversal wall-climbing capability.
notable_capabilities: STAR-family extension that further validates shared-actuator-pool design
notes: DRAFT: exact peer-reviewed venue should be verified before promotion to commons-grade.
prior_art_notes: FCSTAR (Ben-Gurion Zarrouk lab, ~2021) is the most architecturally ambitious STAR-family member: 4 modes (ground, wall-climb, pipe, flight) on a single actuator pool. 4-year-deep open-academic prior art for: thrust-reversal wall-climbing, multi-mode-on-shared-actuator-pool reconfiguration, narrow-pipe traversal. Closes the STAR family lineage chain that begins at star-fearing-2013 and ends with dstar-zarrouk-2026 (decoupled FBEM, Jan 2026). The full 13-year-deep STAR family chain: STAR (Berkeley 2013) → RSTAR (Zarrouk 2019) → TSTAR → FSTAR → FCSTAR → AmphiSTAR → DSTAR.

actuator_details: All-electric quadruped (no hydraulics — distinguished SpotMini from the hydraulic BigDog/Spot ancestors). ~25-30 kg. Brushless DC actuators throughout. Optional 6-DoF arm on dorsal mount. Specific actuator architecture trade-secret.
control_architecture: Closed-source autonomy stack with Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR + depth cameras + IMU. Some autonomous tasks; high-level human guidance for novel tasks. Architectural predecessor to commercial Spot product line.
creator: Boston Dynamics
disclosure_citation: Boston Dynamics. SpotMini public reveal June 2016 demo video; subsequent IEEE Spectrum coverage 2017-2018; capability demonstrations via Boston Dynamics YouTube. Discontinued in favor of Spot (the production quadruped) circa 2019.
end_effector: optional 6-DoF arm with parallel-jaw gripper (dorsal mount)
notable_capabilities: stair climbing, fall recovery, mobile manipulation with optional arm
dishwasher loading + garbage disposal demos (2018 viral)
the architectural predecessor to commercial Spot
prior_art_notes: SpotMini is the architectural predecessor to commercial Spot. ~9-year-deep public-disclosure prior art for: all-electric quadruped morphology (distinct from hydraulic BigDog/Spot ancestors), dorsal-mount manipulator on quadruped base, Velodyne+depth-camera quadruped sensor stack. Trade-secret control software, public capability surface. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid-quadruped or quadruped-manipulator claim. Cited in cheetah-cub-epfl and black-mirror-metalhead-2017 prior_art_notes; round-14 backfill closes those citation chains.
sensing: Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR (360° surround), depth cameras, IMU, joint proprioception
sources: Boston Dynamics YouTube reveal videos June 2016 and 2018.
IEEE Spectrum 'Boston Dynamics' SpotMini Is All Electric, Agile, and Has a Capable Face-Arm', 2017.

actuator_details: Transformer-based diffusion-policy generalist robot policy. Trained on **800k robot trajectories** from a curated 25-dataset subset of the Open X-Embodiment dataset. Two model sizes: Octo-Small (27M parameters) and Octo-Base (93M parameters). Open weights, open code, open dataset. Demonstrated zero-shot and few-shot transfer across 9 robotic platforms with new observation and action spaces.
control_architecture: Transformer + diffusion-policy action head. Conditioned on language instruction OR goal image. Lightweight finetuning recipe enables adaptation to new robots in hours on consumer GPUs.
creator: Octo Model Team (UC Berkeley + Stanford + CMU + Google DeepMind); Levine + Finn + Sadigh group lineage
disclosure_citation: Octo Model Team: Ghosh, D., Walke, H., Pertsch, K., Black, K., Mees, O., Dasari, S., Hejna, J., Kreiman, T., Xu, C., Luo, J., Tan, Y. L., Sanketi, P., Vuong, Q., Xiao, T., Sadigh, D., Finn, C., Levine, S. 'Octo: An Open-Source Generalist Robot Policy'. arXiv:2405.12213, May 2024. Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2024. UC Berkeley + Stanford + Carnegie Mellon + Google DeepMind.
notable_capabilities: first fully open-source generalist robot policy (predates OpenVLA by 1 month)
prior_art_notes: Octo is the canonical first open-source generalist robot policy. 1-year-deep open-permissive academic prior art predating OpenVLA by ~1 month (RSS May 2024 vs OpenVLA arXiv June 2024). Establishes the architectural pattern for: transformer + diffusion-policy action head, Open-X-Embodiment-trained cross-embodiment policy at 27M-93M parameter scale, language-OR-goal-image conditioning. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid VLA claim on diffusion-policy action heads (RDT-1B, π₀ both build on this) and on Open-X-Embodiment-trained cross-embodiment foundation. Together with OpenVLA, π₀, π₀.₅, OpenVLA-OFT, and RDT-1B, establishes the open academic VLA baseline against which Figure Helix, NVIDIA GR00T N1, Microsoft Magma, and any closed commercial VLA must be evaluated.

actuator_details: Multimodal agent foundation model serving **both digital (UI navigation) and physical (robot manipulation) tasks** under one model. Two distinguishing techniques: **Set-of-Mark (SoM)** — annotated key objects/UI elements relevant to a goal; **Trace-of-Mark (ToM)** — extends SoM to dynamic videos by overlaying tracing lines following object motion through interaction. Magma-8B variant has open weights via HuggingFace.
control_architecture: Multimodal foundation policy unified across digital and physical action spaces. SoM + ToM as visual-grounding annotations.
creator: Microsoft Research; Jianwei Yang et al.
disclosure_citation: Yang, J., et al. 'Magma: A Foundation Model for Multimodal AI Agents'. arXiv:2502.13130, February 2025. CVPR 2025. Microsoft Research.
end_effector: any (cross-domain: digital UI agents + physical manipulators)
notable_capabilities: unified digital + physical agent foundation model
SOTA on UI navigation + robot manipulation simultaneously
prior_art_notes: Magma is Microsoft's canonical multimodal agent foundation model (CVPR 2025). 3-month-deep prior art for: unified digital + physical task foundation policy, Set-of-Mark + Trace-of-Mark visual grounding annotations. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on 'one model controls both robot manipulation AND computer/phone interaction' (a notable claim cluster from 1X NEO marketing and Sanctuary Phoenix demos). Magma-8B's open weights make it a re-implementable baseline that any commercial claim must outperform on UI + robot benchmarks to differentiate.

actuator_details: **Vision-Language-Action foundation model purpose-built for humanoid robots.** Dual-system architecture inspired by human cognition: System 1 fast-thinking action model (reflex-class); System 2 slow-thinking deliberate-decision model. 2B parameters in the public N1 release. Trained on a diverse mix: **egocentric human videos + real robot trajectories + simulated robot trajectories + synthetic data**. The N1.7 successor adds Cosmos-Reason2-2B VLM backbone + 20,854-hour EgoScale pre-training across 20+ task categories.

actuator_details: **Pneumatic artificial muscle**: an inflatable inner bladder encased in a braided helical shell. When pressurized, the bladder expands radially and the braided shell shortens axially, producing **contraction-and-tension** that mimics biological muscle. Contraction ratio 25-30%, force-to-weight >1 kN/kg. The architectural parent of all braided-shell pneumatic actuators in modern soft robotics (Festo Fluidic Muscle, Shadow Air Muscle, Pisa-IIT McKibben-actuated platforms).
control_architecture: Pneumatic pressure-driven; inherently compliant (gas-spring behavior); typically actuated against an antagonistic muscle pair for bidirectional control.

Subsequently extensively studied — Daerden + Lefeber 'Pneumatic Artificial Muscles: actuators for robotics and automation' European Journal of Mechanical and Environmental Engineering 47(1) 2002 is a canonical academic survey.
notable_capabilities: high force-to-weight (>1 kN/kg) at low cost

The de facto open-source academic vision-based tactile sensor.

actuator_details: **Magnetic-based tactile skin**. A thin elastomeric skin embeds randomly-oriented magnetic particles; an underlying array of magnetometers detects skin deformation via local magnetic-field changes. **Replaceable + low-cost (~$5 per skin)**: when the skin wears out, peel and replace; the sensor electronics underneath are reused. Distinct from vision-based tactile (DIGIT, GelSight) by sensing modality.
control_architecture: Provides magnetic-deformation signal stream; learned-network mapping to force / contact-position estimates.
creator: Carnegie Mellon University + Meta AI Research; Bhirangi, Hellebrekers, Majidi, Gupta

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on magnetic-based tactile skin or replaceable-tactile-skin architecture.

actuator_details: **Lifelong robot learning benchmark** — 130 manipulation tasks across four suites: LIBERO-Spatial (spatial-knowledge transfer), LIBERO-Object (object-knowledge transfer), LIBERO-Goal (goal-knowledge transfer), and LIBERO-100 (entangled knowledge across 100 tasks). Built on the SAPIEN simulator. Extendible procedural generation pipeline that can generate infinitely many tasks. MIT-licensed.

actuator_details: **The canonical sim-to-real method**. Trains a policy in simulation while randomizing simulator parameters (lighting, textures, camera positions, friction, mass, joint dynamics) so the policy must learn invariances that generalize to the real world. Demonstrated zero-shot transfer of object-detection and manipulation policies from sim to real. **The architectural anchor for every modern sim-to-real workflow**.
control_architecture: Provides a training-procedure pattern, not a runtime system. Composes with any policy class.
creator: OpenAI + UC Berkeley; Tobin, Fong, Ray, Schneider, Zaremba, Abbeel
disclosure_citation: Tobin, J., Fong, R., Ray, A., Schneider, J., Zaremba, W., Abbeel, P. 'Domain Randomization for Transferring Deep Neural Networks from Simulation to the Real World'. arXiv:1703.06907, March 2017. IROS 2017. OpenAI + UC Berkeley.
notable_capabilities: zero-shot sim-to-real demonstrated for object detection + manipulation
the architectural anchor of OpenAI Dactyl (in corpus), ANYmal sim-to-real, every modern RL policy
prior_art_notes: Domain Randomization (Tobin et al. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on sim-to-real training methodology. actuator_details: **Dexterous manipulation policy training from human videos** (rather than robot teleoperation). Demo tasks: pour, place, relocate, hammer use. Direct conceptual ancestor of NVIDIA GR00T N1's egocentric-video-pretraining approach.

actuator_details: Visuomotor policy class extending **Diffusion Policy** (corpus entry `diffusion-policy`) to 3D visual representations (point clouds rather than RGB images). Demonstrates ~24% absolute success rate improvement over Diffusion Policy on 72 simulation tasks; effective with as few as 10 demonstrations. Generalizes across spatial configurations, viewpoints, and embodiments. Used in IROS 2025's Generalizable Humanoid Manipulation paper alongside Open-TeleVision.

actuator_details: **Cortically-implanted brain-computer interface**. 96-channel Utah-array microelectrode implanted in motor cortex (or related cortical regions). Records single-unit + multi-unit neural activity at 30 kHz. Decoded into intended movement commands by neural decoders (Kalman filter, ReFIT, recurrent neural networks). Demonstrated in human clinical trials since 2004; reach + grasp with robotic arm (Nature 2012); typing at 90 chars/min via neural decoded handwriting (Nature 2021).
control_architecture: Neural decoding pipeline: Utah-array signal acquisition → spike sorting → linear/nonlinear decoder → control output. Closed-loop calibration. Open-source via Stanford NeuralEnsemble + brain-gate.org publications.
creator: BrainGate consortium; John Donoghue (Brown), Leigh Hochberg (Mass. General Hospital), Krishna Shenoy (Stanford), Andrew Schwartz (Pittsburgh)
disclosure_citation: Donoghue, J. P. et al. 'Connecting cortex to machines: recent advances in brain interfaces'. Nature Neuroscience 5(11) 2002. First human BrainGate implant: Matthew Nagle, July 2004 (Brown University + Cyberkinetics). Hochberg, L. R. et al. 'Reach and grasp by people with tetraplegia using a neurally controlled robotic arm'. Nature 485 (2012). BrainGate consortium: Brown + Stanford + Massachusetts General + Case Western + Providence VA.
end_effector: connects to robotic arms (DEKA, MPL, Kinova) or computer cursors
notable_capabilities: first long-term human cortical BCI for paralysis (2004+)
typing at 90 chars/min via decoded handwriting (Nature 2021)
closed-loop somatosensory feedback (Modular Prosthetic Limb integration)
20+ years of continuous human clinical record

The architectural anchor for every subsequent commercial BCI (Neuralink, Synchron, Paradromics) and the substrate for Modular Prosthetic Limb integration. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on neural-controlled robotic-arm operation, BCI-mediated teleoperation, or cortical-feedback rehabilitation.

Honda holds 100s of humanoid-specific patents. Most have expired or are expiring (20-year patent term from filing); thus **most Honda humanoid patents are now public-domain prior art.**

actuator_details: **Foundational 6-DoF / 3-DoF haptic interface device**. Stylus-form factor mounted on 6-DoF parallel-link kinematic structure. Renders forces via electric motors at the joints. Position resolution sub-millimeter; force output up to ~6.4 N (Premium 1.5) / 22 N (Premium 6DOF). The architectural ancestor of all stylus-based haptic interfaces. Used in surgical training simulators, molecular modeling, dental training, virtual prototyping.
control_architecture: Cartesian-space force rendering at >1 kHz update; impedance control. Standard SDK (OpenHaptics).
creator: MIT Salisbury Robotics Lab (Thomas Massie + Kenneth Salisbury); commercialized via SensAble Technologies / Geomagic / 3D Systems
disclosure_citation: Massie, T. H., Salisbury, J. K. 'The PHANTOM Haptic Interface: A Device for Probing Virtual Objects'. ASME Dynamic Systems and Control Division 1994. MIT Salisbury Robotics Lab; commercialized via SensAble Technologies (founded 1993, MIT spinout). Acquired by Geomagic 2012; subsequently 3D Systems (Geomagic Touch, Phantom Premium product lines).

notable_capabilities: the architectural ancestor of all stylus haptic devices

Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim on stylus-based teleoperation interfaces or impedance-controlled haptic rendering.

Position resolution sub-millimeter at >1 kHz update rate. **The canonical high-fidelity teleop master used in surgical robotics research, OceanOne (Stanford, corpus entry), and many other teleoperation academic systems.**

actuator_details: **Microfluidic tactile glove + force-feedback exoskeleton hybrid**. Each glove has **135 microfluidic tactile actuators per glove** (displacing skin up to 2 mm at 9 psi peak pressure) — replicating the sensation of real-world objects. **5 force-feedback actuators per glove** delivering up to 40 lb of resistive force. **6 motion-capture sensors** tracking 36 DoF per glove at 0.3 mm positional / 0.3° rotational accuracy at 120 Hz / 16 ms latency. Glove life expectancy 18 months / 540 hours.
control_architecture: Microfluidic actuator pressure-control via tethered air supply; SDK for tactile + force rendering.

actuator_details: **Vision-based tactile sensor with 3D-printed biomimetic skin**. An internal camera images the inner surface of an elastomeric fingertip-shaped 3D-printed skin embedded with white-marker papillae (mimicking skin's intermediate-epidermal ridges). When the skin contacts an object, the papillae shift; image-based tracking gives high-resolution tactile signal. Open-hardware design released for free academic use. **The architectural ancestor of Tactile SoftHand-A (round-11) and Educational SoftHand-A (round-12)** — both of which integrate TacTip-class sensors at fingertips.
control_architecture: Provides camera-based tactile-image stream consumable by downstream perception. Open-source.

disclosure_citation: Ward-Cherrier, B., Pestell, N., Cramphorn, L., Winstone, B., Giannaccini, M. E., Rossiter, J., Lepora, N. F. 'The TacTip Family: Soft Optical Tactile Sensors with 3D-Printed Biomimetic Morphologies'. Soft Robotics 5(2) 2018; arXiv:1803.04922. Bristol Robotics Laboratory (Lepora group).
end_effector: vision-based tactile fingertip (mountable on grippers / hands)
notable_capabilities: 3D-printed biomimetic papillae skin (architecturally distinct from DIGIT/GelSight)

actuator_details: **The first energetically autonomous load-carrying human exoskeleton**. 7 DoF per leg, 4 powered by linear hydraulic actuators. Walks at 0.9 m/s (2 mph) carrying 34 kg (75 lb) external payload. Onboard hydraulic power unit (engine + pump) provides energetic autonomy — no tether. The architectural anchor of subsequent commercial exoskeletons (Sarcos Guardian XO, ExoAtlet, etc.).

Designed for rehabilitation of stroke + spinal-cord-injury patients. ~15 kg device weight. The architectural anchor of bioelectric-controlled exoskeletons (vs. force-sensing controlled Berkeley BLEEX).

Walk with energetic cost-of-transport ~0.04-0.20 — comparable to human-walking efficiency, vastly lower than ZMP-based humanoids (Asimo's COT ~3.2).

actuator_details: Foundational dynamic-legged-robot research program. Hydraulic actuators with passive springs (Spring-Loaded Inverted Pendulum / SLIP model). Three-part Raibert decomposition: hop-height control (vertical), forward-velocity control (foot placement), body-attitude control (hip torque). Each control axis independently solvable, enabling stable dynamic locomotion at a time (1983-1995) when the field was dominated by ZMP statically-stable walking.
canonical_name: Raibert MIT Leg Lab (foundational dynamic legged locomotion)
control_architecture: Three-part Raibert decomposition: vertical / horizontal / attitude control. Each axis solved independently; remarkably effective in practice. The conceptual ancestor of every modern dynamic-legged-robot controller.

actuator_details: **Opposition-space theory of hand kinematics**: human grasps are structured around three fundamental opposition types — (1) **pad opposition** (thumb pad → finger pad), (2) **palm opposition** (thumb → palm + finger), (3) **side opposition** (thumb → lateral side of index finger). Any complex grasp is composed of these three primitives. The framework underlies **virtual-finger** modeling (multiple actual fingers acting as one virtual finger) which enables synergy-driven underactuated hand designs.
control_architecture: N/A — kinematic theory framework.
creator: Thea Iberall (UCSD; later USC); Michael Arbib (USC) collaboration
disclosure_citation: Iberall, T. 'Opposition Space as a Structuring Concept for the Analysis of Skilled Hand Movements'. In Heuer, H. + Fromm, C. (eds.) 'Generation and Modulation of Action Patterns', Springer 1986. Subsequent: Iberall, T., Bingham, G., Arbib, M. A. 'Opposition Space as a Structuring Concept for the Analysis of Skilled Hand Movements'. In Whiting, H.T.A. + Wing, A.M. (eds.) 'Themes in Motor Development', Springer 1986. UCSD + USC.
notable_capabilities: foundational reference for synergy-reduced underactuated hands
prior_art_notes: Iberall's 1986 opposition-space theory is the canonical academic framework for human grasp kinematics. 39-year-deep public-domain prior art for: 3-primitive opposition decomposition, virtual-finger modeling. **Directly underlies the Pisa-IIT SoftHand synergy reduction** (corpus entry pisa-iit-softhand): the SoftHand's single-DoF synergy maps onto Iberall's opposition primitives. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid hand claim on synergy-reduction or virtual-finger mechanism. actuator_details: **Variable Stiffness Actuator (VSA)**: a serial-elastic actuator where the stiffness itself is mechanically adjustable in real time. Two motors per joint: one sets joint position, the other sets joint stiffness. Enables **soft-when-needed, stiff-when-needed** behavior — soft for safe collaboration, stiff for precision manipulation. The architectural cousin of the Pratt-Williamson SEA (corpus entry `pratt-williamson-sea`, 1995, fixed compliance) — VSAs add the variable-stiffness dimension.
control_architecture: Two-motor co-control: position-motor + stiffness-motor. The stiffness controller sets the spring's pretension or geometry.

disclosure_citation: Tonietti, G., Schiavi, R., Bicchi, A. 'Design and Control of a Variable Stiffness Actuator for Safe and Fast Physical Human/Robot Interaction'. ICRA 2005. Pisa-IIT (later: IIT-Pisa joint lab; antecedent of Pisa-IIT SoftHand corpus entry).

actuator_details: **Foundational motion-capture-imitation reinforcement learning** for physics-based character animation. Trains a physics-based RL policy that imitates a specific motion-capture clip plus satisfies a task objective (e.g., walk in target direction). Demonstrates results on humanoid + Atlas + dinosaur + dragon characters across locomotion, acrobatics (flips, spins), martial arts. **The architectural anchor of subsequent imitation-from-demonstration humanoid policies** including AMP, ASE, and the bipedal-RL literature 2018-2024.
control_architecture: PPO-trained policy with imitation reward (matching reference motion) + task reward. Policy outputs joint torques.

actuator_details: **Adversarial Motion Priors (AMP)** — combines DeepMimic-style motion-capture imitation with **GAN-style discriminator** trained to distinguish reference-motion-style from policy-generated motion. Replaces DeepMimic's clip-by-clip imitation with **latent-space style imitation** — the policy can produce task-specific motion that 'looks like' the reference style without exactly tracking any specific clip. Major architectural advance over DeepMimic: **distillation of motion style from unstructured motion-capture corpus** rather than clip-specific imitation.
control_architecture: GAN discriminator distilled from motion-capture corpus + task reward + RL policy. Latent style space.

actuator_details: **Perceptive RL locomotion for quadrupeds** — extends Hwangbo's ANYmal sim-to-real (corpus entry hwangbo-anymal-sim2real, 2019, blind locomotion) by integrating **exteroceptive vision** (depth from elevation maps) with proprioception. Achieves robust locomotion in challenging unstructured terrains (snow, dense vegetation, rubble, slippery surfaces). The current SOTA academic quadruped RL — directly cited by every modern quadruped RL paper. **Two-stage privileged-teacher / proprioception-+-exteroception-student distillation**.

actuator_details: **Capture Point theory of humanoid balance**: defines the **point on the ground where the robot must step to come to a complete stop**, given current center-of-mass position + velocity. Generalizes ZMP (Vukobratović 1969) to dynamic walking + push recovery. Equivalent to **Divergent Component of Motion (DCM)** — the same concept under different mathematical framing. Direct engineering anchor of modern humanoid balance controllers, used in: Boston Dynamics Atlas, IHMC's NASA Valkyrie + Atlas-running controllers, Honda P-series stabilization.
control_architecture: Capture-point-based foot-placement controller. Compute capture point → place next swing foot at or near it → recover stable gait. Real-time at 1 kHz on humanoid hardware.

actuator_details: **The foundational state estimation + optimal control duo**. Two seminal Kalman papers in 1960: (1) Kalman filter — recursive Bayesian state estimator for linear-Gaussian systems; (2) LQR (Linear-Quadratic Regulator) — optimal feedback control for linear systems with quadratic cost. **Used in essentially every robotic system**: every state estimator (orientation, pose, velocity), every control law derivation. The Kalman filter underlies every IMU-based attitude estimator + every GPS-INS-DVL fusion stack in the corpus.
control_architecture: Foundational state estimation + linear-quadratic optimal control framework.

notable_capabilities: the foundational optimal feedback control law (LQR, 1960)
>80,000 citations on the Kalman filter paper
the substrate of every state-estimator + every control-law derivation
prior_art_notes: The Kalman filter + LQR (Kalman 1960) is the foundational state estimation + optimal control framework. 65-year-deep public-domain prior art. Used in essentially every robotic system. actuator_details: **The foundational 6-DoF parallel mechanism**. 6 prismatic actuators connecting a fixed base to a moving platform via ball joints. Provides full 6-DoF motion (3 translation + 3 rotation). The antecedent (Gough 1947 / Dunlop) was the first production application — universal tire test rig. Stewart's 1965 paper formalized the kinematic theory. **The architectural anchor of**: every flight simulator, every motion-base (Disney/Universal rides), every 6-DoF haptic device (round-18 Phantom), every parallel-kinematic machine tool.

disclosure_citation: Stewart, D. 'A Platform with Six Degrees of Freedom'. Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers 180(1) 1965. Antecedent: Gough, V. E., Whitehall, S. G. 'Universal Tyre Test Machine' FISITA 9th International Conference 1962.
notable_capabilities: the architectural anchor of flight simulators, motion bases, parallel haptics, parallel-kinematic machines

prior_art_notes: The Stewart platform (Stewart Proc. IME 1965 + Gough Dunlop 1947) is the foundational 6-DoF parallel mechanism. 60-year-deep public-domain prior art. Direct shielding for any commercial humanoid claim that uses parallel mechanisms or hexapod-class actuator architectures.

Rumelhart-Hinton-Williams Nature 1986 paper popularized the algorithm; mathematical antecedents go back to Werbos 1974 + Linnainmaa 1970.

actuator_details: **The first and only commercial universal-jamming-gripper product**. Granular-filled elastomer membrane (coffee grounds + balloon membrane); when pressed onto an object, the granules flow around the object's geometry, then a vacuum is applied to lock the granules into a rigid mass that grips the object. Single-actuator, geometry-agnostic, conforms to arbitrary shapes. Empire Robotics commercialized 2012-2016; the failed-company status makes its prior-art status especially defense-worthy because every detail was publicly disclosed before wind-down.

actuator_details: **The defining bionic continuum-tentacle gripper**. Silicone-rubber pneumatic continuum tentacle inspired by octopus tentacle biomechanics. Two rows of suction cups along the tentacle's underside (passive vacuum or active when needed). When inflated the tentacle wraps around the object; suction cups attach. Adapts to arbitrary object geometries from delicate (eggs) to heavy (industrial parts). Part of Festo's broader bionic gripper research portfolio (MultiChoiceGripper 2014, FlexShapeGripper 2015, OctopusGripper 2017, FinGripper / Adaptive Bionic Gripper 2009).

actuator_details: **The Fin Ray Effect adaptive finger — now ubiquitous in soft commercial fingers**. Triangular finger geometry with cross-ribs: when force is applied to the side of the finger (i.e., the finger contacts an object), the geometry causes the finger to wrap around the object rather than away from it. Single passive mechanism, no electrical or pneumatic actuation in the finger itself. Festo FinGripper commercialized this principle 2009. Now appears in dozens of academic + commercial soft fingers (HOWE-CUTKOSKY tactile work, OnRobot Soft Gripper, etc.). Fin Ray Effect® is a registered trademark of EvoLogics.

Fin Ray Effect now ubiquitous across global soft-finger gripper market.

actuator_details: **The foundational dexterous robotic hand**. Four fingers (three fingers + opposable thumb), 16 active DoF, tendon-driven by 32 remote pneumatic-piston actuators (push-pull tendons). Each finger has 4 DoF; thumb has 4 DoF. Hand-mounted directly on Utah/MIT teleoperator arm. Co-foundational with Salisbury Stanford-JPL Hand (corpus) of the entire dexterous-hand research field. Stephen Jacobsen subsequently founded Sarcos (corpus sarcos-guardian-xo-2018 lineage).
control_architecture: Decentralized PD joint control; teleoperation + autonomous-grasp research target.
creator: University of Utah Center for Engineering Design + MIT AI Lab; Stephen Jacobsen, John Wood, David Knutti, Klaus Biggers

actuator_details: **The world's first externally-powered five-finger myoelectric anthropomorphic prosthetic hand**. Belgrade Hand (1963): five fingers + adaptive underactuated grasp + sensory feedback to the wearer; controlled by myoelectric signals from the residual limb. The mechanism that pre-dates and prefigures every modern anthropomorphic prosthetic + dexterous research hand. Belgrade-USC Hand (~1988) refined version at USC under George Bekey.

Pioneered the 'soft-strong' design philosophy: simultaneously compliant (safe) and capable of strong grasping (useful).

actuator_details: **The most-cited soft anthropomorphic hand**. Five fingers + thumb made of fiber-reinforced silicone-rubber 'PneuFlex' pneumatic actuators. Pressurizing each chamber bends the corresponding phalanx. Achieves 31 of 33 grasps in the GRASP taxonomy (Cutkosky / Feix). Demonstrates that soft-pneumatic anthropomorphic hands can match dexterous-hand functionality with much simpler mechanism + control. RBO Hand 3 (2022) is the successor with full thumb opposition + dexterous in-hand manipulation.

Each section bends in any direction by differential extension; combined three sections give 9 DoF + elongation. Cephalopod-tentacle inspired. Field-tested on Foster-Miller TALON unmanned ground vehicle. Predates and anchors all subsequent continuum-manipulator research (Festo OctopusGripper round-42, Festo BionicSoftArm corpus, etc.).

Microscopic angled silicone hairs that engage when loaded in shear (one direction) and disengage when unloaded (other direction). Tendon-loaded shear activation. 100× body-weight payload demonstrated. NASA JPL parallel work (Parness LEMUR / Astrobee gecko gripper) is the space-rated variant. OnRobot Gecko Gripper (round-42 / corpus) is the commercial license.

actuator_details: **The defining commercial multi-articulated myoelectric prosthetic hand category**. Three flagship products: (1) i-LIMB (Touch Bionics 2007) — first commercially available individually-powered five-finger prosthetic; later i-LIMB Quantum (2015) with gesture control. (2) BeBionic (RSL Steeper 2010 → Otto Bock 2017) — 14 grip patterns, refined wrist articulation. (3) Michelangelo Hand (Otto Bock 2012) — multi-articulated with independently-positioned thumb and 7 grip patterns. All three are myoelectrically controlled (EMG signals from residual-limb muscles). Together they define the modern commercial multi-articulated prosthetic hand standard.

actuator_details: **The foundational deep grasp-quality network**. Dex-Net 2.0: synthetic depth + analytic grasp metrics + GQ-CNN (Grasp Quality Convolutional Neural Network) trained on 6.7M point-cloud + grasp-pair examples. 99% grasp success on novel objects from depth images alone. Dex-Net 4.0 (2019) extended to 'ambidextrous' policy across parallel-jaw + suction grippers, achieving 1600 novel-object grasps with reliable selection between gripper modes.

'Dex-Net 2.0: Deep Learning to Plan Robust Grasps with Synthetic Point Clouds and Analytic Grasp Metrics'. Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2017. arXiv:1703.09312. UC Berkeley Goldberg Lab AUTOLAB. Dex-Net 1.0 (2016 ICRA) preceded; subsequent Dex-Net 3.0 (suction grasps, 2018) + Dex-Net 4.0 (ambidextrous parallel-jaw + suction, *Science Robotics* 2019).

actuator_details: **The dominant academic grasp benchmark**. 97k RGB-D scenes with 1.1 BILLION annotated grasp poses across 88 objects (graspable + ungraspable + cluttered scenes). Real-world capture (RealSense + Kinect) + synthetic ground truth via simulation. Defines the modern academic grasp-detection benchmark that all subsequent grasp papers (Contact-GraspNet, AnyGrasp, etc.) compare against. First major Chinese academic grasp benchmark.

actuator_details: **The surgical procedure that enables intuitive multi-DOF prosthetic-arm control**. After upper-limb amputation, severed motor nerves are surgically re-routed to spare chest / back muscles. When the patient thinks 'open hand', the corresponding chest muscle contracts; surface-EMG electrodes pick up the signal and drive the prosthetic. Result: intuitive multi-DOF control without joystick / switch input. Without TMR, myoelectric prostheses are limited to 1-2 DoF (open/close, rotate). With TMR + pattern-recognition (Coapt 2013 commercial license), full multi-DoF anthropomorphic-hand control becomes feasible.

actuator_details: **The dominant assembly-robot architecture worldwide**. Now the dominant assembly-arm architecture: Epson (round-45) is the global SCARA volume leader; FANUC, Yaskawa, ABB, KUKA all make SCARA variants.

EPFL patent expired 2007; productized by ABB FlexPicker (round-45), Adept Quattro, FANUC M-1iA, Yaskawa MPP, Codian D5, etc. Defining architecture for food-processing + pharmaceutical high-speed packaging worldwide.

actuator_details: **The canonical multi-gait single-actuator amphibious robot — one mechanism, four gaits, four environments**. The fin pair is described as 'four-dimensional objects with a hyperbolic geometry'. A single pair of undulating fins (each fin a twisted ribbon-like structure) drives the same mechanism through four distinct animal gaits without any mechanical reconfiguration: (1) **swim like a ray** — undulating-fin thrust through water; (2) **crawl like a millipede** — fin ripples push the body along land/ice/sand surfaces; (3) **jet like a squid** — fast pulsed-fin thrust for water-jet propulsion bursts; (4) **slide like a snake** — lateral ripple along the body. Length 1 m. Operates in water + land + ice + snow + sand. C-Ray adds: GPS + IMU + external pressure/depth + wifi + GSM sensing; MOOS-IvP autonomy stack; HydroMAN navigation. Application focus: beach-survey buried-metal-object detection (ONR mission).
