prior_art_notes: Luna 16 (Lavochkin 1970) is the first robotic sample return. 55-year-deep public-domain prior art.

actuator_details: **First successful Mars rover — established the rocker-bogie architecture**. 10.5 kg six-wheel rocker-bogie chassis. Onboard hazard avoidance. APXS (Alpha Proton X-ray Spectrometer). 91 sols of operations. Established the rocker-bogie suspension that defines all subsequent NASA Mars rovers (Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, Perseverance). Honeybee Robotics-derived wheels became the lineage for all NASA Mars sampling tools.
canonical_name: Sojourner (Mars Pathfinder; first successful Mars rover)
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mission profile + hazard avoidance + Earth-tasking.
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (Pasadena, CA, USA)
disclosure_citation: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (USA). Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner rover landed July 4, 1997 in Ares Vallis, Mars. First successful Mars rover.
notable_capabilities: established rocker-bogie suspension for all subsequent NASA Mars rovers
prior_art_notes: Sojourner (NASA JPL 1997) is the first successful Mars rover. 28-year-deep public-domain prior art.

actuator_details: **Twin solar-powered Mars rovers — Opportunity ran 14 years (90-day design life)**. 185 kg each. Pancam mast + Mössbauer spectrometer + Honeybee Robotics Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT, first powered tool to grind a Mars rock). Spirit operated 2,210 sols (stuck 2009). Opportunity operated 5,498 sols and traversed 45.16 km — first marathon-distance off-world drive.
control_architecture: Onboard hazard avoidance + Earth-tasked mission planning.
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
disclosure_citation: NASA JPL (USA). Spirit (MER-A) launched June 10, 2003; landed Gusev Crater January 4, 2004. Opportunity (MER-B) launched July 7, 2003; landed Meridiani Planum January 25, 2004.
notable_capabilities: Opportunity: 14 years operational vs. 90-day design life
Opportunity 45.16 km traverse — first marathon off-world drive
Mössbauer + RAT (Honeybee Robotics) first powered Mars-rock grinder
established water-ice presence at Meridiani Planum
prior_art_notes: Spirit + Opportunity (NASA JPL 2003-2018) are the twin solar Mars rovers. 22-year-deep public-domain prior art.
sensing: Pancam + Microscopic Imager + Mössbauer + APXS + Mini-TES

actuator_details: **First nuclear (RTG)-powered Mars rover — sky-crane EDL + ChemCam laser spectroscopy**. 899 kg, scaled-up rocker-bogie. Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator (MMRTG). ChemCam laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy. SAM (Sample Analysis at Mars) gas chromatograph. CHIMRA drill + sample-handling. Established the sky-crane Entry-Descent-Landing architecture later reused for Perseverance.
canonical_name: Curiosity (Mars Science Laboratory; first nuclear Mars rover)
control_architecture: Onboard hazard avoidance + Earth-tasked mission planning + autonomous drive.
creator: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
disclosure_citation: NASA JPL (USA). Curiosity launched November 26, 2011; landed Gale Crater August 5/6, 2012 via sky-crane EDL. First nuclear (RTG)-powered Mars rover.
end_effector: 2 m robotic arm + drill + CHIMRA + APXS + MAHLI
prior_art_notes: Curiosity (NASA JPL 2012+) is the first nuclear-powered Mars rover. 13-year-deep public-domain prior art.
sensing: MastCam + ChemCam + SAM + APXS + MAHLI + RAD

actuator_details: **Perseverance: sample-caching Curiosity successor. Ingenuity: FIRST POWERED CONTROLLED FLIGHT OFF EARTH**. Perseverance: Curiosity-derived chassis + sample-caching drill that deposits sealed tubes on Mars surface for future Mars Sample Return; SHERLOC + PIXL + MOXIE in-situ resource utilization. Ingenuity: 1.8 kg coaxial counter-rotating rotor helicopter; 72 flights April 2021 - January 2024 (5x design lifetime); rotor damage ended mission. The first aerial vehicle on another planet — landmark Wright-brothers-class achievement.
canonical_name: Perseverance + Ingenuity (Mars 2020; first powered flight off Earth)
control_architecture: Perseverance: onboard hazard avoidance + autonomous-drive. Ingenuity: onboard autonomous flight planning.
creator: NASA JPL + AeroVironment (Ingenuity)
disclosure_citation: NASA JPL (USA) + AeroVironment. Perseverance landed Jezero Crater February 18, 2021. Ingenuity Mars Helicopter first flight April 19, 2021 — first powered controlled flight on another world.
notable_capabilities: Ingenuity: FIRST POWERED CONTROLLED FLIGHT OFF EARTH (April 2021)
MOXIE first in-situ oxygen production from Martian atmosphere
first aerial vehicle on another planet
prior_art_notes: Perseverance + Ingenuity (NASA JPL 2021+) are the Curiosity-successor + FIRST POWERED CONTROLLED FLIGHT OFF EARTH. 4-year-deep public-domain prior art.
sensing: Mastcam-Z + SHERLOC + PIXL + MOXIE + RIMFAX + 23 cameras (Persy); 2 cameras + IMU + altimeter (Ingenuity)

actuator_details: **First Chinese Mars rover — China second nation to operate a Mars rover**. 240 kg six-wheel solar rover. Foldable butterfly-wing solar arrays. Ground-penetrating radar. NaSTAR (Navigation and Topography Camera) + Multispectral Camera + LIBS (Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy). Tianwen-1 orbiter + lander + rover triple deployment in single mission — architectural achievement (vs. NASA's separate orbiter/rover missions).
control_architecture: Onboard hazard avoidance + Earth-tasked mission planning.
creator: CAST / CNSA (China)
disclosure_citation: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CAST) / China National Space Administration (CNSA). Tianwen-1 launched July 23, 2020; Zhurong rover landed Utopia Planitia May 14, 2021.
notable_capabilities: China second nation to operate Mars rover
Tianwen-1 single-mission orbiter + lander + rover triple deployment
prior_art_notes: Zhurong (CAST CNSA 2021+) is the first Chinese Mars rover. 4-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.
sensing: NaSTAR + multispectral + LIBS + ground-penetrating radar + magnetometer

actuator_details: **Yutu-2: FIRST EVER LUNAR FAR-SIDE LANDING + LONGEST-LIVED LUNAR ROVER**. Yutu (2013): 140 kg, 6-wheel solar rover, ended mobility after 114 m. Yutu-2 (2019): far-side rover relying on Queqiao L2 relay satellite for Earth comms (direct comms impossible from far-side); >5 years operational, longest-lived lunar rover ever. Established the relay-based far-side operations architecture.
control_architecture: Onboard hazard avoidance + Queqiao-relayed Earth-tasking (Yutu-2).
creator: CAST / CNSA (China)
disclosure_citation: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CAST) / CNSA. Chang'e-3 + Yutu landed Mare Imbrium December 14, 2013 — first soft landing on Moon since Luna 24 (1976). Chang'e-4 + Yutu-2 landed Von Kármán crater far side January 3, 2019 — FIRST EVER LUNAR FAR-SIDE LANDING.
notable_capabilities: Yutu (2013): first soft lunar landing since Luna 24 (1976)
Yutu-2 (2019): FIRST EVER LUNAR FAR-SIDE LANDING
Queqiao L2 relay satellite for far-side comms
prior_art_notes: Yutu / Yutu-2 (CAST CNSA 2013, 2019+) demonstrate first lunar far-side landing. 12-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **First rover near lunar south pole (69°S) — fourth nation to soft-land Moon**. 26 kg six-wheel solar rover. APXS + LIBS spectrometers. Operated for one lunar day (14 Earth days) before lunar night ended mission. India becomes 4th nation to soft-land Moon. Pre-cursor to ISRO's planned Mars + Venus missions and Gaganyaan crewed program.
canonical_name: Pragyan (Chandrayaan-3; first lunar south pole rover)
control_architecture: Onboard hazard avoidance + Earth-tasked mission planning.
creator: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO; India)
disclosure_citation: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO; India). Chandrayaan-3 + Pragyan landed near lunar south pole August 23, 2023. Made India fourth nation to soft-land on the Moon (after USSR, USA, China).
notable_capabilities: first rover near lunar south pole 69°S (August 2023)
fourth nation to soft-land Moon (after USSR/USA/China)
prior_art_notes: Pragyan (ISRO 2023+) is the first lunar south-pole rover; 4th nation to soft-land Moon. 2-year-deep public-domain prior art.

actuator_details: **Pinpoint lunar landing demonstration + transformable toy-engineered rover**. SLIM achieved ~3-10 m landing accuracy (vs. typical km-class targeting); demonstrated vision-based descent + new 'two-stage' landing posture. LEV-1: hopping rover with direct-Earth comms (7 hops over 107 minutes). LEV-2 / SORA-Q: baseball-sized 250g transformable rover that opens like a toy to roll on Moon (Tomy/Takara toy-engineering lineage). First Japanese soft lunar landing — Japan 5th nation to land on Moon.
control_architecture: SLIM: vision-based pinpoint landing + 2-stage posture. LEV-2: roll-locomotion via shell-transformation.
creator: JAXA (Japan); LEV-2 SORA-Q with Tomy + Sony + Doshisha
disclosure_citation: JAXA (Japan). SLIM (Smart Lander for Investigating Moon) landed Shioli Crater January 19, 2024. LEV-1 + LEV-2 (SORA-Q) deployed at landing. Pinpoint landing demonstration (~10 m accuracy).
notable_capabilities: first pinpoint lunar landing (~10 m accuracy, January 2024)
first Japanese soft lunar landing — Japan 5th nation to Moon
LEV-1: 7-hop hopping rover with direct-Earth comms
Tomy / Sony / Doshisha LEV-2 toy-engineering lineage
prior_art_notes: JAXA SLIM + LEV-1/LEV-2 (2024) are the first pinpoint lunar lander + first transformable toy-rover on Moon. 1-year-deep public-domain prior art.
sensing: SLIM: cameras + LIDAR + radar. LEV-1: cameras + altimeter. LEV-2: cameras.

actuator_details: **First-ever sample return from the lunar far side**. 1,935 g returned from Apollo crater in South Pole-Aitken (SPA) basin. Used Queqiao-2 relay satellite for Earth comms (direct comms impossible from far side). Required retrograde-orbit takeoff/ascent. The architectural achievement of far-side robotic sample return — 54 years after Luna 16 (round-48) on the near side.
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mission profile + Queqiao-2 relay tasking.
creator: CAST / CNSA (China)
disclosure_citation: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CAST) / CNSA. Chang'e-6 launched May 3, 2024; sampled Apollo crater on far side; sample returned to Earth June 25, 2024. First-ever far-side lunar sample return.
notable_capabilities: first-ever sample return from lunar far side (June 2024)
1,935 g returned from Apollo crater in SPA basin
Queqiao-2 relay satellite for far-side comms
54 years after Luna 16 on near side
prior_art_notes: Chang'e-6 (CAST CNSA 2024) is the first-ever far-side lunar sample return. 1-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **First fully successful commercial lunar landing**. Landed Mare Crisium within 100 m of target. Operated 14 Earth days delivering 110 GB of NASA data. Distinguished from earlier 2024 commercial attempts: Astrobotic Peregrine (failed 2024), Intuitive Machines IM-1 Odysseus (tipped 2024), iSpace HAKUTO-R Mission 1 (lost 2023). Direct evidence the commercial lunar lander market reached operational maturity in 2025.
canonical_name: Firefly Aerospace Blue Ghost (first fully successful commercial lunar landing)
control_architecture: Vision-aided terrain-relative navigation; trade-secret commercial.
creator: Firefly Aerospace (Cedar Park, TX, USA)
disclosure_citation: Firefly Aerospace (Cedar Park, TX, USA). Blue Ghost Mission 1 landed Mare Crisium March 2, 2025. First fully successful commercial lunar landing — landed within 100 m of target, operated 14 Earth days.
notable_capabilities: first fully successful commercial lunar landing (March 2025)
operated 14 Earth days delivering 110 GB NASA data
the operational-maturity inflection point for commercial lunar landers
prior_art_notes: Firefly Blue Ghost (Cedar Park 2025) is the first fully successful commercial lunar landing. <1-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **The foundational space robotic arm**. 15.2 m, 410 kg six-DoF manipulator on Space Shuttle. Deployed/retrieved payloads on 90 missions through 2011 (Shuttle program end). Canadian flagship technology contribution to NASA Shuttle program. Direct ancestor of Canadarm2 (round-48), JEMRMS, ERA (round-48). Established the Canadian space-robotics industrial base.
canonical_name: Canadarm (Shuttle Remote Manipulator System; foundational space arm)
control_architecture: Astronaut hand-controller teleop + computer-aided positioning.
creator: Spar Aerospace + National Research Council (Canada)
disclosure_citation: Spar Aerospace + National Research Council Canada. Canadarm first flight STS-2 November 13, 1981. Foundational space robotic arm.
prior_art_notes: Canadarm (Spar / NRC 1981+) is the foundational space robotic arm. 44-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **ISS canonical robotic-manipulation system**. Canadarm2: 17.6 m seven-DoF arm with end-to-end relocatable 'inchworm' architecture (either end can grapple — neither end is 'base'). Performed ISS assembly and Dragon/Cygnus/HTV/SpaceX cargo capture. Dextre (2008): two-armed dexterous 'hand' attached to Canadarm2; 1,662 kg torso with two 3.5 m arms for ORU swap and refueling demos — astronaut-level dexterity in teleoperated platform.
control_architecture: Astronaut hand-controller + ground-controller teleop + computer-aided positioning.
creator: MDA / Canadian Space Agency
disclosure_citation: MDA / Canadian Space Agency. Canadarm2 (SSRMS) launched STS-100 April 2001. Dextre (SPDM) launched March 2008.
end_effector: dual end-effector grapple (Canadarm2); two arms + ORU/RTL tools (Dextre)
prior_art_notes: Canadarm2 + Dextre (MDA / CSA 2001, 2008+) are the ISS canonical robotic-manipulation system. 24-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.
sensing: position encoders + cameras + force-torque + collision detection

actuator_details: **First robotic arm on ISS Russian segment**. 11 m, 8-tonne payload capacity. Hand-over-hand mobile (relocatable like Canadarm2) and operable from inside or outside the station. Servicing the Russian Nauka science module + Multipurpose Laboratory Module. European space-robotics flagship.
canonical_name: European Robotic Arm (ERA; ESA Russian segment ISS arm)
control_architecture: Astronaut hand-controller + ground-controller teleop.
creator: Airbus Netherlands + European Space Agency (Europe)
disclosure_citation: Airbus Netherlands / European Space Agency. ERA launched July 2021 with Nauka module. First robotic arm on ISS Russian segment.
notable_capabilities: first robotic arm on ISS Russian segment (2021+)
operable from inside or outside the station
prior_art_notes: European Robotic Arm (Airbus NL + ESA 2021+) is the first ISS Russian segment robotic arm. 4-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **ISS open robotic-research platforms — free-flying microgravity testbeds**. SPHERES (2003-2017): basketball-sized free-flyers using CO2 thrusters for formation-flying, docking, zero-g algorithm research; foundational testbed. Astrobee (2018+): three 12.5-inch cube-shaped free-flying robots (Bumble, Honey, Queen) with electric-fan propulsion + perching arms. The ISS open robotic-research platforms for autonomous mobile manipulation in zero-g.
control_architecture: Onboard autonomous navigation + ground-controlled tasking.
creator: NASA Ames Research Center + MIT Space Systems Lab
disclosure_citation: NASA Ames Research Center + MIT Space Systems Lab. SPHERES first ISS operations 2003-2017. Astrobee (Bumble + Honey + Queen) launched April 2018, operations 2019.
notable_capabilities: SPHERES: cold-gas thrusters, formation-flying + docking research
open research platform for ISS autonomous robotics
prior_art_notes: SPHERES + Astrobee (NASA Ames + MIT 2003-2018+) are the ISS open robotic-research platforms. 22-year-deep public-domain prior art.
sensing: cameras + IMU + Wi-Fi mesh + perching sensors

actuator_details: **First humanoid robot in space**. 34 cm, 1 kg companion humanoid. First robot-human conversation in orbit December 2013 with astronaut Koichi Wakata. Designed by Tomotaka Takahashi (also of Robi commercial robot). Toyota + JAXA partnership. Predecessor of Robonaut 2 ISS crew assistance (though Robonaut 2 went up earlier 2011, Kirobo is the first explicitly-humanoid companion-AI robot in space).
control_architecture: Voice-recognition + speech-synthesis + onboard expression generation.
creator: University of Tokyo + Toyota + JAXA; Tomotaka Takahashi designer
disclosure_citation: Tomotaka Takahashi / University of Tokyo + Toyota + JAXA. Kirobo launched to ISS August 2013. First robot-human conversation in orbit December 2013 with astronaut Koichi Wakata.
prior_art_notes: Kirobo (Toyota + JAXA + Univ Tokyo 2013) is the first humanoid robot in space. 12-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **First AI-powered free-floating astronaut assistant**. 5 kg, soccer-ball-size sphere with 12 fans + screen-displayed face. IBM Watson conversational AI + speech recognition. Designed for astronaut crew companionship + mission-procedure assistance. CIMON-2 (2019): IBM Watson Tone Analyzer for emotion-aware interaction. The architectural ancestor of any 'AI floating assistant' commercial humanoid claim.
control_architecture: IBM Watson AI + 12-fan stabilization + voice + screen-face expression.
creator: Airbus + IBM Watson + DLR (Germany)
disclosure_citation: Airbus + IBM Watson + DLR (Germany). CIMON launched June 2018; first operations with ESA astronaut Alexander Gerst. CIMON-2 December 2019 with IBM Watson Tone Analyzer.
notable_capabilities: 5 kg soccer-ball-size sphere + 12 fans + screen face
CIMON-2 (2019) Tone Analyzer for emotion-aware interaction
prior_art_notes: CIMON (Airbus + IBM + DLR 2018+) is the first AI-powered free-floating astronaut assistant. 7-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **First humanoid on unmanned Soyuz**. ~160 kg adult-size bipedal humanoid. Performed teleoperated cable-mating tasks on ISS exterior simulation. Distinguished from Kirobo (companion humanoid) by adult-form-factor + physical-task focus. Russian counterpart to NASA Robonaut 2 (corpus). Subsequently became prototype for Russian humanoid-cosmonaut concepts.
canonical_name: Skybot F-850 / FEDOR (Russian humanoid in space)
control_architecture: Teleoperated + autonomous skills; visual-recognition + voice command.
creator: Android Technics / Roscosmos (Russia)
disclosure_citation: Android Technics / Roscosmos (Russia). Skybot F-850 / FEDOR launched on unmanned Soyuz MS-14 August 22, 2019. First humanoid in space on unmanned crewed-class spacecraft.
notable_capabilities: first humanoid on unmanned Soyuz crewed-class spacecraft (Aug 2019)
teleoperated cable-mating tasks on ISS exterior simulation
prior_art_notes: Skybot F-850 / FEDOR (Android Technics + Roscosmos 2019) is the first humanoid on unmanned Soyuz. 6-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **The first soft landing on a comet**. Cold-gas thruster + harpoon anchoring attempted (both failed); resulted in two bounces before resting in shadowed crevasse. Rosetta orbiter delivered Philae to 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko after 10-year journey. Foundational prior art for low-gravity small-body landing despite anchoring failure.
canonical_name: Philae (first soft landing on a comet)
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mission profile + Earth-tasked science operations.
creator: DLR + European Space Agency (Europe)
disclosure_citation: DLR / European Space Agency. Philae landed comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko November 12, 2014. First soft landing on a comet.
notable_capabilities: first soft landing on a comet (November 12, 2014)
two bounces, settled in shadowed crevasse
prior_art_notes: Philae (DLR + ESA 2014) is the first soft landing on a comet. 11-year-deep public-domain prior art.

actuator_details: **First rovers to operate on an asteroid + first artificial-impactor experiment**. MINERVA-II1A + 1B: hexagonal 1.1 kg hopping rovers using internal-flywheel-torque hops (no wheels — wheels would float off Ryugu's microgravity surface). First rovers to operate on an asteroid surface. Hayabusa-2 also demonstrated active artificial-impactor experiment to expose subsurface material before sampling. Returned 5.4 g of Ryugu regolith December 2020.
control_architecture: Pre-programmed + Earth-tasked autonomous descent + sample collection.
creator: JAXA (Japan)
disclosure_citation: JAXA (Japan). Hayabusa-2 launched December 2014; arrived asteroid Ryugu June 2018; deployed MINERVA-II1A + MINERVA-II1B hopping rovers September 2018. Sample returned to Earth December 2020.
end_effector: MINERVA-II hopping rovers + Hayabusa-2 sample horn
notable_capabilities: first rovers to operate on an asteroid (September 2018)
MINERVA-II1A + 1B hopping rovers via internal-flywheel torque
prior_art_notes: Hayabusa-2 + MINERVA-II (JAXA 2014-2020) deployed first asteroid rovers + first artificial-impactor experiment. 11-year-deep public-domain prior art.

actuator_details: **First US asteroid sample return**. 121.6 g returned from Bennu. 'Touch-and-go' (TAG) sampler used pressurized N2 burst to lift regolith into a sampling head on a robotic arm — TAGSAM (Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism). Distinct from Hayabusa-2's projectile-impact sampling. October 2020 TAG event was successful.
canonical_name: OSIRIS-REx (Bennu sample return; first US asteroid sample)
control_architecture: Pre-programmed mission profile + autonomous TAG descent.
creator: NASA Goddard + Lockheed Martin (USA)
disclosure_citation: NASA Goddard + Lockheed Martin (USA). OSIRIS-REx launched September 2016; arrived asteroid Bennu December 2018; sample returned to Earth September 24, 2023.
prior_art_notes: OSIRIS-REx (NASA + Lockheed Martin 2016-2023) is the first US asteroid sample return. 9-year-deep public-domain prior art.

actuator_details: **First operational commercial satellite servicer + life-extension**. MEV-1 (2020): docked Intelsat 901 in graveyard orbit, towed back into service for 5 years; first commercial GEO undocking April 2025. MEV-2 (2020): docked active Intelsat 10-02 directly in GEO without service interruption — proved life-extension for active satellites. The architectural definer of the satellite-life-extension service category.
control_architecture: Trade-secret commercial; autonomous proximity ops + manual docking sequence.
creator: Northrop Grumman SpaceLogistics (USA)
disclosure_citation: Northrop Grumman SpaceLogistics (USA). MEV-1 launched October 2019; docked Intelsat 901 February 2020. MEV-2 docked active Intelsat 10-02 April 2020. First operational satellite servicers; first commercial GEO undocking April 2025.
notable_capabilities: MEV-2: active-satellite docking without service interruption
Northrop Grumman SpaceLogistics service category definer
prior_art_notes: MEV-1 / MEV-2 (Northrop Grumman SpaceLogistics 2019-2020+) are the first operational commercial satellite servicers. 6-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **World's first commercial active-debris-removal demonstration**. Magnetic-capture system between a 184 kg Servicer satellite and a 16 kg Client (target) satellite. Demonstrated successive capture-and-release of the Client over multiple orbital scenarios. The architectural definer of commercial space-debris-removal service. Subsequent: ADRAS-J (Active Debris Removal demo for Japan, 2024 first inspection of large debris).
control_architecture: Autonomous proximity operations + capture sequence; trade-secret commercial.
creator: Astroscale Holdings Inc. (Tokyo, Japan); Mitsunobu Okada founder
disclosure_citation: Astroscale Holdings Inc. (Tokyo, Japan; founded 2013 by Mitsunobu Okada). ELSA-d launched March 2021. World's first commercial active-debris-removal demonstration.
notable_capabilities: 184 kg Servicer + 16 kg Client magnetic-capture demo
Astroscale Tokyo founded 2013 by Mitsunobu Okada
prior_art_notes: Astroscale ELSA-d (Tokyo 2021+) is the world's first commercial active-debris-removal demonstration. 4-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **The first commercially successful autonomous home robot**. Random-walk navigation + bump-sensor architecture + cliff sensors. Disc-shaped vacuum robot. Original $199 price unlocked the mass market for service robotics. Subsequent: Roomba 800/900 series with VSLAM (2015), Roomba i7 (2018) with self-emptying base, J7 with object-recognition. >40 million units sold by 2020. Defines the consumer-service-robot category.

creator: iRobot Corporation (Bedford, MA, USA); Colin Angle + Helen Greiner + Rodney Brooks
disclosure_citation: iRobot Corporation (Bedford, MA, USA; founded 1990 by Colin Angle + Helen Greiner + Rodney Brooks). Roomba launched September 2002 at $199. First commercially successful autonomous home robot.

$199 launch price unlocked mass-market service robotics
iRobot lineage: Brooks/Angle/Greiner from MIT AI Lab
prior_art_notes: iRobot Roomba (Bedford MA 2002+) is the foundational autonomous home robot. 23-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **First consumer robot with LIDAR-based SLAM mapping**. Spinning LIDAR + real-time map-building. D-shaped form factor (corner-coverage advantage). Broke the iRobot random-walk paradigm. Paved the way for Roborock + DJI + Dyson LIDAR vacuums. Acquired by Vorwerk 2017; brand sunset 2023.

D-shaped form factor for corner coverage

actuator_details: **The first major Chinese-origin consumer robot vacuum brand**. Deebot evolution: random-walk → vSLAM → LIDAR-SLAM. Deebot Ozmo (mopping). Deebot X1/X2 OMNI (vacuum + mop + self-cleaning station). Established the Chinese consumer-robot-vacuum manufacturing base. >60% China market share. Subsequent Roborock + Dreame + Eufy descend from Ecovacs ecosystem.

S8 (2023) with auto-empty + mop-washing. Brought premium-class features to mass-market price tier. Now one of top-3 global vacuum-robot brands by revenue.

prior_art_notes: Roborock S-series (Beijing 2017+) is the mid-price LIDAR-vacuum market leader. 8-year-deep public-disclosure prior art.

actuator_details: **The world's first commercial robotic lawnmower (1995) — predates Roomba by 7 years**. Husqvarna Solar Mower (1995): 40W solar-powered design by Belgian inventor André Colens. Husqvarna Automower (1998): grid-charging Solar Hybrid; established the boundary-wire + dock-charging pattern that defined the entire robotic-lawnmower category. >1.5M Automower units sold by 2024. The architectural definer of robotic outdoor service robotics.

actuator_details: **Sealed soft artificial muscle fiber — the configurable actuation substrate**. Sub-2mm diameter fiber actuators integrating electrohydrodynamic (EHD) pumps directly into sealed fluid-filled fibers. Apply DC voltage (8 kV) → 20% contraction in 0.3 seconds. ~50 W/kg specific power (matches human skeletal muscle). Key engineering insight: bias internal pressure to optimal point + seal the loop = fully untethered fluidic actuation with only electrical input. Eliminates the portability bottleneck plaguing fluidic soft robotics. Bundle fibers (8x bundle achieves 70 mm stroke in <2 sec) like muscle fascicles for force multiplication. Weave into textiles for wearable assistive systems (knitted glove bends finger 60° in <1 sec; woven structure bends forearm 90° in 1 sec). Platinum electrodes (700% pressure improvement vs. prior copper). 3M Novec 7100 dielectric (PFAS-exit risk; ETI 7100 / BestSolv 7100 are drop-in replacements). Palm-sized 18g HV converter at <100 µA below human safety threshold. **The first artificial-muscle architecture compatible with textile manufacturing infrastructure** — looms / braiders / knitters already handle 1-2mm fibers.

actuator_details: **Fluidic pumps in stretchable-fiber form factor — direct predecessor to EFM**. Twisted-helical 80-µm copper electrodes wound around a central mandrel with TPU; heat-fused into a single tube where both continuous electrodes contact the internal dielectric fluid. DC field at 5-8 kV ionizes the dielectric; ion drag toward collector electrode drives unidirectional flow. No moving parts. Demonstrated wearable fluidic-system integration (cooling vests, soft actuators). The fiber form factor was the architectural breakthrough that enabled EFM (round-51) two years later.

Foundational to subsequent Smith fiber pump (round-51 2023) and EFM (round-51 2025). Cacucciolo's PhD thesis work at EPFL with Shea + Floreano labs.

actuator_details: **Pouch-form electrohydraulic artificial muscle — closest EFM competitor**. HASEL = Hydraulically Amplified Self-healing ELectrostatic actuator. Liquid dielectric inside flexible polymer pouch; electrodes on outside. Apply voltage → electrostatic force pulls electrodes together → displaces fluid → pouch contracts. **Self-healing**: dielectric breakdown self-heals because liquid dielectric flows back into the breakdown path. Peano-HASEL variant (linear-actuator geometry) achieves >100% strain, muscle-like specific power. Direct competitor to EFM (round-51) but pouch-shaped rather than fiber-shaped: higher peak strain but no fiber modularity and worse power density. Keplinger group moved from CU Boulder to Max Planck (Stuttgart) 2020. The foundational pouch-electrohydraulic artificial muscle prior art.

actuator_details: **Foundational electroactive-polymer artificial muscle (Science 2000)**. Elastomer film (silicone / acrylic) sandwiched between compliant electrodes. Apply voltage → Maxwell stress squeezes film → film expands area-wise (preserves volume), thinning in thickness direction. >100% strain demonstrated. Fast (sub-millisecond response). High specific energy. The foundational EAP/DEA prior art. Direct competitor to EFM (round-51) and HASEL (round-51) but vulnerable to dielectric breakdown (no self-healing like HASEL). Pelrine SRI International anchor of EAP research. Subsequent commercialization: Artificial Muscle Inc. (SRI spinout).

actuator_details: **Artificial muscles from fishing line + sewing thread — radically simple thermal actuator**. Coiled nylon fishing line: take a nylon monofilament, twist it until it forms a tight coil, anneal. Resulting fiber contracts up to 49% when heated, expands when cooled. Drive by Joule heating (resistive wire wound on outside) or hot/cold air. ~5.3 kW/kg specific power (100x human muscle). Radically simple — fishing line + sewing thread + an iron. Tradeoff: thermally driven means slow response (~100ms-seconds for cooling-limited cycle) and terrible efficiency (~1%). Foundational thermal-artificial-muscle prior art.

actuator_details: **Foundational shape-memory alloy — the original 'smart material' actuator**. Nickel-Titanium alloy (NiTi) — discovered by William Buehler at US Naval Ordnance Laboratory 1962. Acronym: NItinol = NIckel TItanium Naval Ordnance Laboratory. Reversible solid-state phase change at ~30-90°C (martensite ↔ austenite). Deform at low temperature → heat above transition → recovers original shape with up to 8% strain at high stress. Driven by Joule heating (resistive). Used in: medical stents, surgical tools, microactuators, eyeglass frames, dental archwires, MEMS valves, and the early robotic-finger actuators (Wood RoboBee uses NiTi predecessors; soft-robotic-fish use SMA strips). Slow cooling-limited cycle. The foundational shape-memory-actuator prior art.

actuator_details: **Foundational ionic-polymer-metal-composite bio-inspired actuator**. Nafion (perfluorinated ionomer) membrane with platinum or gold electrodes plated on both faces. In water, applying ~1-3 V causes ion migration → asymmetric swelling → strip bends toward the cathode. Soft + silent + low-voltage (vs. HV electrohydraulic competitors). Bio-inspired — operates similarly to fish-fin actuation in fluid. Used in: biomimetic underwater robots (early RoboTuna lineage), MEMS micro-actuators, soft grippers. Tradeoffs: requires hydrated state (or solid-polymer-electrolyte variants), slow response, low specific power vs. EHD/HASEL/DEA. The low-voltage bio-inspired counter-class to high-voltage electrohydraulic actuators.
control_architecture: Low-voltage 1-3 V DC; ion-migration-driven bending.
